tasks.description: Survey open-source macOS cleaners: PureMac, Pearcleaner, Mole and any other well-starred cleaner. Parent task; one deep-dive task per source is linked via relatedTo.

comments.author: sweep-cleaner
comments.text:
## sweep-cleaner: cleaner candidates (facts from `gh api repos/...` on 2026-09-23)

**MUST**
- **tw93/Mole**: 68,135 stars, GPL-3.0, Shell + Go, pushed 2026-09-23. The broadest open-source rule set: clean, uninstall, analyze, optimize, purge (build artifacts), installer. Also has dry-run, a whitelist at `~/.config/mole/whitelist`, history, and Trash-based `analyze` (README L82-135). Study it, do not copy it: GPL. "Mole for Mac" (mole.fit) is a separate proprietary app (README L454).
- **momenbasel/PureMac**: 6,677 stars, MIT, Swift/SwiftUI, pushed 2026-09-23. This is the real PureMac repo; the only other hits are unrelated or tiny forks. It covers cleanup, app management, storage exploration and scheduled auto-clean. Built with xcodegen. Permissive license, so direct reuse is possible.
- **alienator88/Pearcleaner**: 14,715 stars, Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause (source-available; no selling), Swift, pushed 2026-06-22. The reference for matching app leftovers (AppCleaner-style). README says "Project Status: On Hold" since end of 2025. Learn from it only; also relevant to T-0005.

**SHOULD**
- **Tencent/lemon-cleaner**: 6,328 stars, GPL-3.0 (LemonDaemon GPL-2.0, per LICENSE*.txt), Objective-C, pushed 2026-05-08. Has a per-app junk rule DB at `LemonClener/LemonClener/libcleaner/garbage1_en.xml`, plus a disk-space visualizer, duplicate and similar-photo finders, and a privileged daemon.
- **iliyami/MacSai** (formerly MacClean): 1,584 stars, BSD-3-Clause, Swift 6, pushed 2026-09-22. Claims Trash-first deletion, a protected-paths blocklist, symlink/TOCTOU guards and a `SafetyGuard` that checks every path. Worth a safety-pattern deep dive; the license allows reuse.
- **mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-py**: 2,374 stars, Apache-2.0, Python, pushed 2026-04-14. A well-known list of cleanup targets (successor of mac-cleanup-sh: 2,815 stars, MIT, deprecated). Reusable target list.
- **AdventDevInc/kudu**: 3,562 stars, MIT, TypeScript, cross-platform, pushed 2026-09-22. Cleaning rules are plain JSON with a schema (`rules/darwin/*.json`, 8 files, `rules/RULES.md`). A good model for a data-driven rule format, and MIT data can be reused.
- **harry0703/MangoDisk**: 3,058 stars, GPL-3.0, Rust, pushed 2026-09-22. Cleanup plus treemap analysis plus duplicates plus uninstall in one app: the closest to the macontrol merge. Study only (GPL). Overlaps with T-0002.
- **tbillington/kondo**: 2,413 stars, MIT, Rust, pushed 2026-04-24. Detects build artifacts per project type across many ecosystems. Reusable list for "dev junk".

**COULD**
- guhcostan/mac-cleaner-cli: 1,980 stars, MIT, TypeScript. CLI list of caches/logs/Homebrew/Xcode targets.
- vashpan/xcode-dev-cleaner: 1,612 stars, GPL-3.0, Swift. Xcode-specific: DerivedData, archives, device support.
- waylybaye/XcodeCleaner-SwiftUI: 1,423 stars, **no license** (cannot reuse).
- voidcosmos/npkill: 9,451 stars, MIT, TypeScript. node_modules only.
- jithin-sabu/purge-app: 853 stars, MIT, Swift. Fixed allowlist, Trash-only.
- bysiber/cleardisk: 704 stars, MIT, Swift. Dev-cache menu bar app.
- 2ykwang/mac-cleanup-go: 460 stars, MIT, Go TUI.
- Kevin-De-Koninck/Clean-Me: 1,850 stars, MIT, archived 2021.
- vorssaint/vorssaint-utils: 20,818 stars, GPL-3.0, Swift. A menu bar toolkit where the cleaner is a minor feature.
- ggbond268/MacTools: 1,217 stars, GPL-3.0. Menu bar toolkit with a cleanup plugin.
- qarmin/czkawka: 33,668 stars, MIT per README ("entire code ... MIT"; the GitHub API says NOASSERTION). A duplicate/similar-file engine; belongs to the engine/dup topic.

Out of scope, no clone needed: bleachbit (Windows/Linux only), sickcodes/osx-optimizer (tweaks, not cleanup).
Note for T-0010: "remove bundled system apps". Apple apps on the Sealed System Volume (Safari, Mail, etc.) cannot be deleted with SIP on. Only /Applications apps like GarageBand, iMovie, Pages, Keynote and Numbers can be. None of the tools above claim otherwise (unverified per tool).

comments.author: sweep-visualizer
comments.text:
**Visualizer sweep: 17 candidates (5 must/should-level worth a code deep-dive + reference-only). Facts from `gh api repos/...` on 2026-09-23.**

**Radix identified:** `colinvkim/Radix` (https://github.com/colinvkim/Radix, site https://tryradix.app). Open source, **MIT**, Swift/SwiftUI, 861 stars, pushed 2026-09-20, not a fork. `rvetlyakov/Radix` and `birhantprkc/Radix` are 0-star forks of it. `mimobn/radisk` (Rust TUI, 11 stars) is a different project, not it.

MUST
- **colinvkim/Radix**: MIT, 861, Swift, pushed 2026-09-20. Sunburst+treemap, scan comparison, "Discard Pile" staged delete, LZFSE `.radixscan` snapshots, APFS clone-aware accounting, incremental rescans. Files: `Radix/Services/ScanEngine.swift`, `BulkDirectoryEnumerator.swift`, `IncrementalRescanPlanner.swift`, `SharedAllocationDeduplicator.swift`, `SunburstGeometry.swift`, `TreemapGeometry.swift`, `Models/FileTreeStore.swift`. MIT = directly reusable.
- **137137137/OpenDisk**: MIT, 216, Swift, pushed 2026-09-22. Sunburst DaisyDisk alternative; README claims 1 TB cold scan 17 s vs DaisyDisk 37 s (unverified, their bench), incremental rescan 20-28x faster via FSEvents replay. Files: `OpenDisk/Services/Scanning/CatalogScanner.swift`, `SystemInterop/SearchFS.swift` (catalog search path), `SystemInterop/BulkDirectoryReader.swift`, `SystemInterop/FSEventsChangeJournal.swift`, `Views/Charts/RingsChartLayout.swift`. Needs macOS 15+ per README.

SHOULD
- **GrandPerspective** (SourceForge git https://git.code.sf.net/p/grandperspectiv/source): GPL-2.0, Objective-C, v3.8.1 2026-09-14, actively maintained. The reference macOS treemap: filters, color mappings, scan tree. GPL = ideas only unless macontrol goes GPL. GitHub copies (`patmoore/grandperspective`, `bezigon/GrandPerspective`) are unofficial mirrors.
- **tkslucas/Neodisk**: GPL-3.0, 579, Swift, pushed 2026-09-23. Read-only treemap+sunburst, age heatmap, content-hash duplicates, "Show Package Contents" (bundles stay solid), changes tab, arrow-key navigation in both charts. Note: `Sources/NeodiskKit/...` shares many type names with Radix (`ScanIncrementalModels`, `AtomicDirectorySummary*`, `ScanSnapshot`, `BulkDirectoryReader`): lineage unverified, check before citing either as original.
- **windirstat/windirstat**: GPL-2.0, 4105, C++, pushed 2026-09-23. Cushion treemap (van Wijk) + extension/type legend + cleanup actions. Algorithm reference.
- **shundhammer/qdirstat**: GPL-2.0, 2593, C++, pushed 2026-09-20. Squarified cushion treemap, configurable cleanup actions, file-age/type stats. Algorithm + UX reference.
- **DaisyDisk** (closed, https://daisydiskapp.com): UX benchmark for sunburst + "collector" drag-to-delete flow. Reference only.

COULD
- adileo/squirreldisk: AGPL-3.0, 1826, TypeScript/Tauri, last push 2023-08-04 (stale). Sunburst on top of parallel-disk-usage.
- AlexGladkov/Spacie: license NOASSERTION (README says Non-Commercial, not reusable), 85, Swift. README claims fts scanner, arena tree + string interning (<500 MB for 5M files), progressive duplicate hashing.
- imsnif/diskonaut: MIT, 3133, Rust TUI treemap, last push 2024-03-07.
- GNOME/baobab: GPL-2.0, 167 (read-only mirror of gitlab.gnome.org), Vala, ring chart + treemap.
- KDE/filelight: GPL-2.0/3.0 (LICENSES dir; API reports none), 289, C++, sunburst.
- jeromerobert/k4dirstat: GPL-2.0, 82, C++, last push 2024-02-05 (QDirStat supersedes).
- Disk Inventory X (https://www.derlien.com): GPL, v1.3, macOS 10.13-10.15, no Apple Silicon build listed; GitHub copy `alinradut/Disk-Inventory-X` (GPL-2.0, 68, last push 2019).
- lludo/SwiftSunburstDiagram (MIT, 551) and yahoo/YMTreeMap (MIT, 163, last push 2023): drop-in SwiftUI sunburst / squarified layout libs.
- Byron/dua-cli (MIT, 6292), KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage (Apache-2.0, 732), zevv/duc (LGPL-3.0, 711): scan engines; better covered by T-0006.

Excluded / flagged: `redtrillix/SpaceSniffer` (2039 stars, archived, no code, closed freeware redistribution), `caezium/burrow` (MIT app but engine is FSL-1.1 source-available; cleaner-sweep territory), `harry0703/MangoDisk` (GPL-3.0 Tauri cleaner+analyzer, cleaner-sweep territory), `Prithvi-Web/TreeMap-Disk-Visualizer` (MIT Electron, 800 stars in 3 months, not native).

comments.author: topic-size-accounting
comments.text: From T-0009: when surveying visualizers, check size base (logical vs allocated), hard-link dedupe, clone handling and scan root. Of PureMac, Mole and dust, none is clone-aware (F-0004), and Mole's overview misses Data-volume-only space (F-0005). Useful probe: research/bench/size-accounting/run.sh builds a clone/hardlink/sparse/compressed fixture with known true totals (du says 38 936 KiB, true unique is 23 576 KiB).

comments.author: dive-harry0703-mangodisk
comments.text: Visualizer overlap from the MangoDisk dive (T-0019): the treemap is a one-level squarified layout of DOM buttons (src/lib/utils/treemap-layout.ts, area proportional to bytes, remainder tile below 0.75 %). The backend caps each folder at 80 children (cache.rs:302, F-0016 class). The scanner is a good reference design: parallel getattrlistbulk, 8 workers, a reaper for stuck kernel calls, and SF_DATALESS skip (platform/src/macos/analysis.rs). GPL-3.0, so study only. Details: research/reports/sources/harry0703-mangodisk.md

comments.author: sweep-ui
comments.text:
Reuse and lineage facts from the UI sweep (T-0007) for the license matrix:
- **bysiber/cleardisk** (MIT) vendors RadixCore from colinvkim/Radix at rev `d26a57b9aec4f9887c1832784ce249fb9e0559e3`. It keeps the upstream LICENSE.txt and adds a single `ClearDiskBridge.swift` so upstream refreshes stay easy (`Vendor/DiskScanBackend/UPSTREAM.md`). This is a working template for how macontrol could vendor Radix.
- **thaw-app/Thaw** (GPL-3.0) is derived from jordanbaird/Ice (GPL-3.0). Its file headers carry both copyrights (`Thaw/Permissions/Permission.swift:5-6`). Ice's last commit was 2025-09-20.
- **Jarvis322/macos-sysdata**: the API reports NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE is proprietary and source-available ("not so that they can be reused"). Ideas only.
- **MacPaw/cleanmymac-cli**: the API reports NOASSERTION, but the LICENSE is a MacPaw EULA dated 2026-06-26. Not open source.
- **MacPaw/PermissionsKit** is MIT (FDA detection) and **EmergeTools/Pow** is MIT (SwiftUI transitions): both can be reused. **insidegui/VirtualBuddy** is BSD-2-Clause.

comments.author: dive-momenbasel-puremac
comments.text: FYI from dive-momenbasel-puremac (T-0013): PureMac uninstaller engine appears derived from Pearcleaner, relicensed MIT without the Commons Clause notice or credit. Evidence: PureMac/Logic/Scanning/{Conditions,Locations,AppPathFinder}.swift (added in PureMac commit f2eeceeb "v2.0.0 - Complete architecture overhaul", 2026-04-14) share distinctive identifiers and data with Pearcleaner/Logic/{Conditions,Locations,AppPathsFetch}.swift: skipReverse, skipDeepSearch, darwinCT(), listAppSupportDirectories, standardLibrarySubdirectories, MCMMetadataIdentifier container lookup, bundleLastTwoComponents, and rule strings like "comappleconfigurator", "cleaner for xcode", "embeddedbinaryvalidationutility", "aaprofilepicture", PasswordManagerBrowserExtensionHelper path (grep counts match 1:1). README Acknowledgments name no Pearcleaner credit. Treat those 3 PureMac files (+StringNormalization.swift) as Pearcleaner-licensed: study only. The rest of PureMac (ScanEngine, CleaningEngine, StorageExplorer, ProviderPaths, FileProtection, CleanupExclusions, cli/) shows no such overlap and can be treated as MIT.

comments.author: dive-iliyami-macsai
comments.text: License fact for the matrix: iliyami/MacSai (1,585 stars) is BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE:1-3, API spdx BSD-3-Clause). I searched for Pearcleaner code markers (skipReverse, skipDeepSearch, darwinCT, bundleLastTwoComponents) and got 0 hits. The README credits Pearcleaner, Mole and Lemon only as inspiration. Code can be copied if we keep the notice and do not endorse with the 'Mac Sai' name. Take candidates: OrphanedAppFiles.swift, PathExclusion.swift, dev and AI cache path list (Constants.swift:153-187), per-target TCC denial probe (TargetedScanner.swift:55-79). Report: research/reports/sources/iliyami-macsai.md

comments.author: dive-mac-cleanup-mac-cleanup-py
comments.text: License facts for mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-py: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE, pyproject.toml:5, gh api), 2,374 stars, no NOTICE file, and the LICENSE appendix still has the '[yyyy] [name of copyright owner]' placeholder. Lineage: the rule list comes from mac-cleanup/mac-cleanup-sh (MIT, 'Copyright (c) 2020 Florian Wartner'). The same literals appear in both, e.g. /private/var/folders/bh/*/*/*/* (sh :154, py default_modules.py:23), MobileSync/Backup (:190/:74), ~/*.hprof (:444/:417). Verdict: the target list can be taken with attribution to both projects. The code is not worth taking. Open question: whether bare path lists are copyrightable at all. Details in research/reports/sources/mac-cleanup-mac-cleanup-py.md.

comments.author: dive-adventdevinc-kudu
comments.text: License and lineage, Kudu (AdventDevInc/kudu@0ef4292): MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 Advent Development Inc (LICENSE, gh api .../license). All 22 commits touching rules/darwin are by the maintainer dbfx. A grep for bleachbit/cleanerml/pearcleaner/puremac found no lineage markers. Decision: the darwin rule data can be imported with the MIT notice in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES. Code is ideas only, because it is an Electron/TS app. Details are in research/reports/sources/adventdevinc-kudu.md.

comments.author: dive-harry0703-mangodisk
comments.text: MangoDisk (harry0703/MangoDisk) is GPL-3.0 (LICENSE; API reports GPL-3.0). It has no vendored code and no UPSTREAM/NOTICE files, and its UI kit is shadcn-vue (MIT, components.json). Study only. Its 238 rule TOMLs (core/rules/**) are part of the GPL work, so do not copy the TOML or the evidence text. Re-derive paths from the official URL each rule cites in references=[...]. Report: research/reports/sources/harry0703-mangodisk.md

comments.author: dive-tbillington-kondo
comments.text: kondo (tbillington/kondo) is MIT, Copyright (c) 2020 Trent Billington, per LICENSE and each crate's Cargo.toml. The reusable part is data: marker files and artifact folder names in kondo-lib/src/lib.rs:9-119 @1d351ca. The table was added over the years through contributor PRs listed in CHANGELOG.md, and I found no sign that it was copied from another tool (unverified beyond the changelog). If we import it, add a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry. No kondo code is planned for reuse. Details: research/reports/sources/tbillington-kondo.md (T-0020).

comments.author: dive-colinvkim-radix
comments.text: License facts for Radix: colinvkim/Radix is MIT (LICENSE:1-3, 'Copyright (c) 2026 Colin Kim'); RadixCore has no dependencies, app uses Sparkle (MIT). Copying is allowed with the notice preserved. Files carry 'Created by Codex' headers (agent-written for the author), no third-party code found in the tree. tkslucas/Neodisk (GPL-3.0) is a derivative that credits Radix: take code from Radix, never from Neodisk. bysiber/cleardisk vendors Radix (M-0001). Reuse table: research/reports/sources/colinvkim-radix.md.

comments.author: dive-137137137-opendisk
comments.text: OpenDisk (T-0022) lineage for the license matrix: MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 137137137. Services/FullDiskAccess.swift says it is 'Derived from ... github.com/inket/FullDiskAccess, MIT' (lines 7-9), so keep that notice too if copied. Models/ChartItem.swift:6-9 says the chart design 'follows GNOME baobab's chart; the implementation is original Swift'. Baobab is GPL, so reuse the idea, not baobab code. Neodisk (GPL-3.0) also has a BulkDirectoryReader.swift, but I found no shared comments or literals, so I treat it as a common name. Report: research/reports/sources/137137137-opendisk.md.

comments.author: dive-sourceforge-net-p-grandperspectiv-source
comments.text: GrandPerspective (official SF git @3e0088c): GPL-2.0-or-later (LICENSE=GPLv2 text + Credits.rtf 'or any later version'), no per-file headers, single copyright holder (Erwin Bonsma / Eriban Software). GitHub copies patmoore/bezigon are stale unofficial mirrors (2011/2015). Rated study-only; .clr palettes, XIBs and help book are GPL assets too. Details: research/reports/sources/sourceforge-net-p-grandperspectiv-source.md

comments.author: dive-windirstat-windirstat
comments.text: WinDirStat (windirstat/windirstat@da13ad6): GPL-2.0, study only. LICENSE.md and the GitHub API say GPL-2.0. The file headers say 'v2 or (at your option) any later version', but the README says v2 only. There is one permissive island: Controls/HilbertMooreTreeMap.cpp:12-37 adapts templates from varg-dev/hilbert-moore-treemap-layouts-prototype, which is MIT per gh api. Port the Hilbert/Moore stable treemap layout from that MIT upstream with attribution, never from WinDirStat's GPL file. The logo is CC BY 3.0 (irrelevant to us).

comments.author: dive-dundee-gdu
comments.text: License fact from T-0032: dundee/gdu is MIT (LICENSE.md, Copyright 2020-2021 Daniel Milde; gh spdx MIT). A grep for foreign license headers (Permission is hereby granted, Apache, adapted from, ported from, Copyright (c)) over the .go/.ts/.tsx sources found none, so no vendored islands. Candidate takes: pkg/fs/dataless_darwin.go (setiopolicy_np dataless opt-out) and the webui/tree.go best-first node budget (idea). Keep the MIT notice if code is copied.

comments.author: dive-ggbond268-mactools
comments.text: License fact for ggbond268/MacTools: GPL-3.0-only at HEAD, but Apache-2.0 from a8627a0 (2026-05-16) until bcd9f9f (2026-08-27, 'migrate to GPL-3.0-only'). LICENSING.md §Historical Releases says pre-transition Apache grants are not revoked. At the last Apache revision 9197035650b67f1c313960e8b1dded7a710264dd (LICENSE = Apache-2.0), the DiskClean 2.0 engine (df1dcdd, rkrkrkk, 2026-07-30) is byte-identical to HEAD: 25 of 39 Plugins/DiskClean/Sources files, among them WorkerPool, FastWalker, SlowWalker, DirectoryTreeWalker, RootOpener, RemovalPrimitive, StagingJournal, StagingReconciler, SafetyPolicy, SizeCache, Plan, PurgeScanner and RunningAppLock (diffed locally). Suggested matrix row: MacTools DiskClean @9197035 = Apache-2.0, copy with NOTICE and change marks. Fetch by ref, never from HEAD. StorageExplorer (added 2026-09-06) and Sources/MacToolsFileSystem (2026-09-07) are GPL-only, ideas only. Details: research/reports/sources/ggbond268-mactools.md, journal M-0027.

comments.author: dive-munki-munki
comments.text: munki/munki: Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.md and the per-file headers (rmpkgs.swift:8-18); the GitHub API says NOASSERTION. There is no NOTICE file. Copyright line: 'Copyright 2024-2026 The Munki Project'. The code may be copied with attribution and change marking. The recommendation is to take the idea only (report reuse table), so no munki code is planned to be vendored.

comments.author: dive-homebrew-brew
comments.text: Homebrew/brew is BSD-2-Clause ('Copyright (c) 2009-present, Homebrew contributors'; gh api repos/Homebrew/brew/license). If macontrol copies the SYSTEM_DIRS / UNDELETABLE_PATHS lists (Library/Homebrew/cask/macos.rb:6-378) or any other brew code or data, THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES must carry the copyright line plus the BSD-2 text. The rest of the engine is design-only (Ruby to Swift rewrite). Source: research/reports/sources/homebrew-brew.md (T-0036).

comments.author: dive-objective-see-knockknock
comments.text: License facts, KnockKnock (T-0038): repo GPL-3.0 (LICENSE, API agrees) -> study only. The prebuilt Libraries/BTM/libDumpBTM.a comes from objective-see/DumpBTM, also GPL-3.0; do not link it into macontrol (a test-only oracle under research/bench is fine locally). Vendored: 3rdParty/HyperlinkTextField.* MIT (Toomas Vahter); 3rdParty/RFOverlayScroll* 'Copyright (c) 2012 Rheinfabrik. All rights reserved.' with no license text, so treat as not reusable. research/bench/objective-see-knockknock/ holds only macontrol-written probe code that links the clone's lib via SRC=.

comments.author: architect
comments.text:
Reuse policy (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 11, research/reports/M1-decisions.md):
- Study only, never copy code, data or assets: GPL (Mole, MangoDisk, GrandPerspective, WinDirStat, QDirStat, Neodisk, Lemon, KnockKnock, MacTools at HEAD), Pearcleaner (Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause) and PureMac's Pearcleaner-derived Logic/Scanning/{AppPathFinder,Conditions,Locations,StringNormalization}.swift, unlicensed code (dumac, diskly).
- Adapt with attribution: Radix (MIT), OpenDisk (MIT, plus inket/FullDiskAccess MIT), dua-cli (MIT), gdu (MIT), PureMac other files (MIT), Mac Sai (BSD-3, no endorsement), kondo (MIT), Kudu (MIT), mac-cleanup-sh (MIT) / -py (Apache-2.0), Homebrew brew + cask data (BSD-2), munki (Apache-2.0), MacTools DiskClean at 9197035 (last Apache-2.0 revision, fetch by ref), varg-dev hilbert-moore treemap (MIT, not WinDirStat's copy).
- Mechanism: every adaptation adds an entry to THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (project, commit, files, full license text) in the same commit. The file exists in the scaffold (b5224eb) with a template.

License for macontrol itself (USER DECISION, not decided by the architect): recommend **MIT**. It matches Radix, OpenDisk and dua-core, whose code we are most likely to adapt, and every permissive source above is compatible with it. Alternative: Apache-2.0 if an explicit patent grant matters. Choose GPL-3.0 only if you want to import GPL material (for example Mole's rule set) or forbid closed forks; it would then bind the whole app. Until decided, the repo has no LICENSE file (all rights reserved).

comments.author: build-safety-trash
comments.text: Attribution needed in THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md (not in my owned paths, so the integrator/architect please add): Sources/Safety/ProtectedLocations.swift adapts folder lists from Homebrew brew @ 3f12c3ee9d2385a84250c218bcefcda97b3734fd, Library/Homebrew/cask/macos.rb SYSTEM_DIRS + UNDELETABLE_PATHS (BSD-2-Clause, Copyright (c) 2009-present, Homebrew contributors) and from PureMac @ bef6083ffda49fae033c1d72fb92870149d8e667, PureMac/Logic/Utilities/ProviderPaths.swift (MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 PureMac Contributors). Both full license texts are already in a comment at the end of ProtectedLocations.swift.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.text: User decided: MIT. LICENSE committed on main.

comments.author: bench-harness
comments.text: Re topic-size-accounting's PRIVATESIZE question: measured with research/bench/bulkwalk.c, a serial fd-relative getattrlistbulk walker, with and without -x (forkattr PRIVATESIZE|CLONEID|EXT_FLAGS + FSOPT_ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED). Fixture (300k files): wall 7.10 -> 7.94 s (+12%), sys 1.27 -> 2.05 s (+61%). ~/projects (469k entries): wall 11.41 -> 18.74 s (+64%), sys 3.12 -> 5.29 s (+70%). Correctness: the sum of private sizes on the fixture = 1,446,752,256, exactly the clones-counted-once total minus the shared extents (partial clone included). Recommendation: do not request it in the first-paint walk; fetch it lazily per selection or in a second pass. Data: results/{fixture,real}-bulkwalk-summary.json; report section 'Baseline: bulkwalk and the cost of the APFS extended attributes'.

comments.text: Three bench asks from the dua-core dive (T-0029). (1) Add per_node_stable_across_runs next to total_stable_across_runs by hashing each run's depth-2 listing. dua's totals are stable, but its per-folder sizes flip between runs when hard links or clones are shared (F-0054, probe research/bench/byron-dua-cli/attribution_probe.sh). (2) dua 2.45 switches a directory from getattrlistbulk to readdir + per-entry lstat when two bulk refills spend more wall than CPU time (crates/dua-lib/src/macos/mod.rs:256-323). Its own comment says this is sensitive to scheduling. Please measure how often that fires at loadavg 15+ against idle (fs_usage needs root), and sweep -t 2..12 (the default is 8, src/options.rs:66; it was 3 before, CHANGELOG.md:1622). (3) Tree-build cost, rough (2 runs, load ~16): on the fixture 'dua stacks --depth 1000' took 0.81/0.87 s with 49-52 MB peak footprint, against 'dua aggregate' at 0.65/0.75 s with 5.2-5.7 MB. The TUI integration path (per-entry channel and ancestor walk) adds about 0.1-0.16 s per 311k entries.

comments.author: dive-healeycodes-dumac
comments.text: dumac numbers on your fixture (research/bench/healeycodes-dumac/, same hyperfine flags, load 17→12): dumac 670±61 ms, dua 722±68, diskus 1325±139, bulkwalk 6204, du 6582 (3 runs). Total 2,360,152,064 B, 3 of 3 stable, exit 0. That is du/dua + 528,384 B, because it counts 1,032 symlinks at 512 B each (src/main.rs:332-335), which hides 6% of the PATH_MAX loss. Extra evidence for F-0008: dumac calls `open(fullpath)` (src/main.rs:167-191), drops pathmax/, reports ENAMETOOLONG as "Cannot access directory" and exits 0. RSS was 42.9 MB against dua's 11.2 MB. No license, so a dumac line in run.sh would need a local build: rustup in the scratchpad plus the one-line bytes patch, as described in run_probes.sh. I did not edit run.sh.

comments.author: dive-ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage
comments.text: From T-0031 (pdu): pdu's release benchmark is a model for the harness: a 48-category self matrix run against the last release with a 10% regression gate (ci/github-actions/benchmark/matrix.ts, check-for-performance-regressions.ts), a competing matrix with pinned versions (hyperfine --warmup=1), and raw reports published per release (deploy.yaml:497-700; KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage-*-benchmarks). What it lacks and ours has: total checks, APFS/macOS, and a big hard-link tree (its tree has 20 inodes). Two notes on the pdu lines in run.sh: (1) at -d 1 pdu keeps no tree and skips the -H dedup pass, so 14 MB RSS and the pdu-H time do not reflect a full-tree app. Keeping the full fixture tree (-d 200 --min-ratio 0.5) peaked at 30.7 MB footprint vs 6.6 MB at -d 1, about 77 B/node incl. names (1 run). (2) The -H pass is quadratic per wide folder: 1k/2k/4k/8k same-folder link pairs cost 0.14/0.53/1.94/7.89 s user. A fixture folder with thousands of same-folder link pairs would catch this class in any engine. Generator: research/bench/ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage/repro.sh quadratic.

comments.author: dive-dundee-gdu
comments.text: From T-0032 (gdu dive): the F-0007 root cause is now verified, no longer just inferred. With gdu's own type (pkg/analyze/wait.go @848a5dd), Init; Add(1); Done(); Add(1); Wait() returns at once with one job outstanding: check() unlocks the mutex when the count hits 0, and Add never re-locks it. Probe: research/bench/dundee-gdu/probe_engine_test.go TestProbeWaitGroupRearm, run via research/bench/dundee-gdu/run.sh (go test -overlay, clone untouched). The maintainer knows the weakness: stored.go:41-46 sleeps 1 s before closing badger ('Wait returns immediately if value is 0, few last goroutines might still start after that'). ParallelAnalyzer (TUI/-o) is unaffected, because each parent's Done follows its children's results. An extra data point: 2 runs of gdu-go -n -p -s on the fixture gave 2,340,888,576 and 2,359,623,680.

comments.author: sweep-uninstaller
comments.text:
## sweep-uninstaller: uninstaller and leftover-detection candidates (facts from `gh api repos/...` on 2026-09-23; licenses checked in the LICENSE files)

**MUST**
- **alienator88/Pearcleaner**: 14,715 stars. Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause per LICENSE.md and README:122; the API reports NOASSERTION. Swift, pushed 2026-06-22, README:7 says "Project Status: On Hold". This is the reference for leftover matching. `Logic/AppPathsFetch.swift` matches on bundle id, app name, entitlements (:357) and, in "deep" mode, the Team ID (:409), plus group containers through `containerURL(forSecurityApplicationGroupIdentifier:)` (:151). Other key files: `Logic/Locations.swift` (the search roots, :64-91), `Logic/Conditions.swift` (per-app include/exclude rules), `Logic/ReversePathsFetch.swift` (orphaned files of apps already deleted), `Logic/UndoManager.swift`, `PearcleanerSentinel/FileWatcher.swift` (Trash watcher), `Logic/PKG/PKGManager.swift`, and `Logic/Brew/HomebrewUninstaller.swift`. Learn from it only: the no-sell clause blocks copying.
- **Homebrew/homebrew-cask** (DATASET): 22,226 stars, BSD-2-Clause. The feed https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask.json (18.9 MB, last-modified 2026-09-23) lists 7,754 casks. It holds 4,715 `zap` stanzas with 21,512 hand-curated leftover paths, plus uninstall directives: 678 `pkgutil` and 437 `launchctl` (counted locally). Use it as a leftover-path dataset and as a test oracle for our matcher. Attribution is required.
- **tw93/Mole** (uninstall module): 68,135 stars, GPL-3.0, study only (T-0001 also lists it). `lib/core/app_protection.sh:954` has `find_app_files` and :2000 finds files by BOM receipt. `lib/core/app_protection_data.sh:621` guards against generic app-name words matching unrelated LaunchAgents. The explicit allowlist of removable Apple apps sits at `app_protection_data.sh:167-171` and `docs/SECURITY_DESIGN.md:48-50`: never remove `com.apple.*` except purchasable apps such as GarageBand, iMovie, iWork, Logic and Xcode. The safety suite is 7 `tests/uninstall*.bats` files plus `tests/brew_uninstall.bats`.

**SHOULD**
- **Homebrew/brew**: 49,753 stars, BSD-2-Clause, reusable. `Library/Homebrew/cask/artifact/abstract_uninstall.rb` (710 lines) is a proven ordering of uninstall steps: launchctl before quit, "for cases where app would instantly re-launch" (:214), and quit/signal before kext (:82). It also has wildcard launchctl lookup (:173), `uninstall_login_item` (:488), `uninstall_pkgutil` (:592) and `uninstall_trash` (:619).
- **munki/munki**: 3,472 stars, Apache-2.0 per LICENSE.md (the API says NOASSERTION), Swift. `code/cli/munki/shared/installer/rmpkgs.swift` (670 lines) keeps a SQLite receipt DB built with lsbom (:236). `getPathsToRemove` (:373-390) removes only paths that no other package references. `forgetPkgFromAppleDB` is at :411 and bundle-aware removal at :466-514. This is the correct way to remove pkg-installed apps and the GarageBand/MAContent receipts.
- **objective-see/KnockKnock**: 794 stars, GPL-3.0, study only. `Plugins/BTM.m`, `LaunchItems.m`, `LoginItems.m`, `SystemExtensions.m` and `Kexts.m` enumerate every kind of background item an app can leave behind, including macOS 13+ Background Task Management.
- **sunknudsen/guides `app-cleaner.sh`**: the repo has 937 stars, MIT. `archive/how-to-clean-uninstall-macos-apps-using-appcleaner-open-source-alternative/app-cleaner.sh` (122 lines) is the ancestor that Pearcleaner credits (README:40). It matches by name and bundle id with `find -maxdepth 1` over a fixed list of roots and receipt .bom files (:47-48, :103-107). A minimal, reusable baseline.

**COULD**
- nrlquaker/homebrew-createzap: 46 stars, MIT, archived. Its location list in `cmd/brew-createzap:15-35` shares most of its roots with app-cleaner.sh and Pearcleaner `Locations.swift`.
- milanvarady/Applite: 7,052 stars, MIT. A Homebrew cask GUI whose uninstall is `brew --zap`, for brew-installed apps. buresdv/Cork (4,704 stars, Commons Clause) is similar.
- sindresorhus/macos-trash: 459 stars, MIT, Swift. Moves items to the Trash with Put Back support.
- wpexpertinbd/BHUninstaller: 55 stars, MIT, Rust/Tauri. `crates/bhu-core/src/leftovers/macos.rs` implements Trash-only deletion with a review sheet that says why each file matched.
- kvijayan/AppTrap: 147 stars, permissive custom license, Obj-C, last push 2017. Watches the Trash and removes the preferences of deleted apps (SmartDelete-style).
- JPrasca/darwin-survival-kit: 1 star, NO license. `uninstalls/uninstall-garageband.sh`, `uninstall-imovie.sh` and `uninstall_iwork.sh` are the only scripts for removing bundled Apple apps that this sweep found. Reference only.
- taniguti/scripts_for_mac_manage: 4 stars, MIT. `tools/remove_garageband_sound_library` also deletes `/Library/Application Support/Logic`, which Logic and MainStage share. A counter-example for T-0010.
- closed:AppCleaner (freemacsoft.net): the closed-source UX baseline (drag-drop, SmartDelete).
- kamjin3086/AppUninstaller (34 stars, MIT) and AlexTkDev/MacOSCleaner (96 stars, GPL-3.0 + Commons Clause, the API says NOASSERTION): minor.

**Notes**
- No open-source tool removes apps on the Sealed System Volume (Safari, Mail, and so on). GarageBand, iMovie, Pages, Numbers and Keynote are App Store apps in /Applications. Their content lives in `/Library/Application Support/GarageBand`, `/Library/Audio/Apple Loops` and `/Library/Application Support/Logic`, which are shared with Logic, MainStage and iMovie (source: makeuseof.com/how-to-remove-garageband-sound-library-mac; not verified on this Mac). Owner: T-0010.
- Dropped: undergroundwires/privacy.sexy (AGPL-3.0). `src/application/collections/macos.yaml` has no app-removal scripts.

comments.author: dive-alienator88-pearcleaner
comments.text: Pearcleaner deep dive (T-0014) is done: research/reports/sources/alienator88-pearcleaner.md, journal M-0008. New findings: F-0022 (a depth-2 match promotes to the whole vendor folder), F-0023 (uninstall never runs launchctl bootout, so jobs keep running; verified with research/bench/uninstall-oracle/launchd_probe.sh) and F-0024 (the delete guard is 12 exact paths and it clears uchg). I added more evidence for F-0002 and F-0011 on T-0014. For your leftover work: the MCMMetadataIdentifier container lookup (AppPathsFetch.swift:160-181) is the reliable UUID-container attribution. The 26 per-app Conditions (Conditions.swift:45-202) are the curated knowledge worth re-deriving as JSON. research/bench/uninstall-oracle/fixture.sh lists user-data paths that no matcher may pre-select.

comments.author: dive-tencent-lemon-cleaner
comments.text: Uninstaller evidence from T-0015 (Lemon). (1) Incident note: FinalShell's bundle id is 'st', and an earlier containsString: bundle-id match deleted every launchd plist on the machine (localPod/LemonUninstaller/.../LMLocalApp.m:1606-1611). Worth a regression test. (2) Leftover matching today is a full-string regex over space-stripped lowercase names, \\b((bundleName)|(executableName)|(showName))(\\..*){0,}\\b, plus a bundle-id regex and a company-subfolder match (LMLocalApp.m:1504-1630). (3) The predefined per-app scanner is dead in the public tree: _curAppSettings is never assigned and the loader is commented out (McUninstallSoftManager.m:83-113). json_setting.qce (475 KB) is encrypted. (4) Apple apps cannot be uninstalled except Keynote, Numbers and Transporter (LMLocalAppListManager.m:629-645). (5) Every group except 'Other' is deleted permanently via the root-fallback path (LMFileGroup.m:186-192).

comments.author: dive-harry0703-mangodisk
comments.text: MangoDisk (T-0019) uninstaller, for the survey. SAFE CORE worth modelling: the bundle ID must match Info.plist; associations are exact-ID paths in 8 ~/Library places (Caches, App Support, Preferences plist, Logs, Saved State, Containers, WebKit, HTTPStorages) with only rebuildable ones preselected (core/src/applications/uninstall/macos.rs:578-642); never display-name matching (test :1051). Orphans are found only from containermanagerd metadata in ~/Library/Containers (core/src/applications/leftovers/macos.rs:69-275). FEATURE GAPS (no defect): no LaunchAgents/LaunchDaemons, Group Containers, /Library, PrivilegedHelperTools or pkg receipts, no system apps, and app location depth is at most 1 under /Applications and ~/Applications (:696-716). GPL-3.0, so study only.

comments.author: dive-daisydisk
comments.text:
dive-daisydisk (T-0028): the Homebrew cask zap/uninstall data is not ground truth for privileged helpers. Filed as F-0055.
- DaisyDisk 4.34.2 installs the SMJobBless helper com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone.AdminHelper (Info.plist SMPrivilegedExecutables; embedded launchd plist with AssociatedBundleIdentifiers=com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskStandAlone; research/sources/daisydisk/bundle-metadata.txt:93-95,205-211).
- The cask Casks/d/daisydisk.rb:20-21 (@4691afd4c4) uninstalls com.daisydiskapp.DaisyDiskAdminHelper, a label that no longer matches. brew's uninstall_launchctl (abstract_uninstall.rb:232-256) skips it silently, so the root helper survives "brew uninstall --zap".
- 85 of 7,755 casks hard-code PrivilegedHelperTools paths.
- This Mac has live orphans: /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/com.docker.socket and com.docker.vmnetd, with no plist, no Docker app (mdfind) and no service loaded.
- Suggested rule: derive helper labels from the bundle (SMPrivilegedExecutables keys, Contents/Library/LaunchServices, Contents/Library/LaunchDaemons), and match /Library/LaunchDaemons plists by AssociatedBundleIdentifiers or by Program path. Treat cask data only as a hint, with every path existence-checked.

comments.author: dive-homebrew-homebrew-cask
comments.text: Homebrew cask dataset deep dive (T-0035) is done: research/reports/sources/homebrew-homebrew-cask.md, journal M-0028. Take the data (BSD-2, notice required): 4,716 zap casks, 21,517 paths; a zap+uninstall+app subset is 2.15 MB, 313 KB gzipped. Matcher ceiling on curated paths (research/bench/homebrew-homebrew-cask/matcher_coverage.txt): bundle ID alone finds 64.8%, plus app name 87.5%, plus vendor prefix 93.5%. The remaining 6.5% are Team-ID group containers, vendor folders and user content. Application Support is only 32% bundle ID (54% app name), and Logs 9% (78%). New findings: F-0066 (zap mixes own, shared and user-content paths, so do not preselect cask paths blindly), F-0067 (wildcard launchctl resolves only running jobs in the user domain, unanchored; verified with brew's own code), F-0068 (630 zap lines in 179 casks freeze a version number: rebuild templates from the .rb). Worth taking: brew's teardown order (abstract_uninstall.rb:23-35) and rmdir-if-empty (:651-700).

comments.author: dive-munki-munki
comments.text: munki rmpkgs dive (T-0037) done. TAKE the idea: remove only paths(selected receipt) minus paths(every other receipt) (rmpkgs.swift:373-389), plus package-level ref counting (analyze.swift:1021-1062). The fixture probe confirmed the shared dylib and shared dirs are kept. DO NOT PORT the Swift code as-is: bundle detection is dead ('app' vs '.app'), so munki 7 leaves a gutted .app, forgets the receipt and reports success (F-0069); ids are pasted into SQL as double-quoted strings (F-0071). Use lsbom -p fmsc (mode/size/CRC32) for an identity check, and look for BOMs in /var/db/receipts AND /Library/Apple/System/Library/Receipts. GarageBand caveat: the munki wiki says the old MAContent10 CoreContent2/v3 packs share one pkg id (GarageBand.md:46), and since Jan 2026 Logic/MainStage content ships as .aar with no receipt (GarageBand.md:4-5). So receipts alone will not clean loops; a path rule is still needed (unverified here, no content installed). Journal M-0029.

comments.author: dive-objective-see-knockknock
comments.text: From the KnockKnock dive (T-0038, journal M-0031): (1) the BTM db /private/var/db/com.apple.backgroundtaskmanagement/BackgroundItems-v16.btm (0644 root) is the one place macOS lists background items with bundleID/teamID/associatedBundleIDs/parent. It decodes as uid 501 with FDA (verified, 42 records here), so the uninstaller can list 'background items owned by <app>' without root. (2) SMAppService agents store bundle-relative executablePath/plist and must be joined to the parent record's url (F-0072; KnockKnock drops them, upstream #49/#50). (3) Stale 'developer (0x20)' records outlive uninstalled apps (3 here, all disabled, no url; upstream #27). No per-record public removal API found (only sfltool resetbtm, all-or-nothing, unverified). (4) The full location catalogue for 20 persistence mechanisms is in M-0031. Feature gap, not a finding: the uninstaller must also scan <app>/Contents/Library/LaunchAgents|LaunchDaemons|LoginItems, read BundleProgram, and show disabled items.

tasks.title: Survey fast scan engines
tasks.description: Fastest filesystem walkers (gdu, dua-cli, dust, pdu, ncdu and Swift/ObjC ones). APIs used (getattrlistbulk, fts, readdir), parallelism, APFS clone and hard link handling. Parent task.

comments.author: sweep-engine
comments.text:
**Engine sweep: 16 candidates, 9 of them must/should.** Facts come from `gh api repos/...` on 2026-09-23, or from the Forgejo API for ncdu. Every file:line was read through `gh api .../contents`. Nothing was cloned.

**Short answer on the API:** on APFS, the fastest macOS walkers use parallel `getattrlistbulk(2)` on a work-stealing pool, with hard links deduplicated by inode. That covers dua-core, dumac, OpenDisk, Radix and MacTools. `searchfs(2)` catalog search only wins on HFS+. OpenDisk measured it about 2x slower than parallel bulk traversal on APFS, and it aborts with EBUSY while the volume is changing (`OpenDisk/Services/Scanning/CatalogScanner.swift:13-21`, their own numbers, which I have not checked). Plain `readdir` beats `getattrlistbulk` only when no attributes are needed. With sizes it becomes readdir+lstat, which is the slowest option (T. Tempel, http://blog.tempel.org/2019/04/dir-read-performance.html). T-0004 should re-benchmark this.

MUST
- **Byron/dua-cli**: MIT, 6292 stars, Rust, pushed 2026-09-22. Its new workspace crate `dua-core` (`crates/dua-lib`, "Fast parallel filesystem traversal iterators") is the most complete reference.
  - Concurrency: a crossbeam work-stealing pool with per-worker LIFO queues and injector roots (`crates/dua-lib/src/lib.rs:1-26`).
  - macOS walk: `getattrlistbulk` (`src/macos/mod.rs:1`, `:369`).
  - APFS clones: clone identity read with `FSOPT_ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED` (`mod.rs:143-166`, `:362`), plus `nlink`.
  - `jwalk` is not in its Cargo.toml dependencies, and Byron/jwalk (288 stars) is now archived.
  - Delete flow and clean hub: `src/interactive/app/deletion.rs`, `clean_hub.rs`.
  - Being MIT, we can port the algorithm to Swift.
- **137137137/OpenDisk**: MIT, 216 stars, Swift, pushed 2026-09-22. Also listed under T-0002.
  - Scan: `SystemInterop/BulkDirectoryReader.swift` (getattrlistbulk traversal) and `Scanning/CatalogScanner.swift` (searchfs, HFS+ only, with the measured APFS penalty quoted above).
  - Incremental rescan: `FSEventsChangeJournal.swift`, `IncrementalUpdater.swift`, `ScanCache.swift`.
- **colinvkim/Radix**: MIT, 861 stars, Swift, pushed 2026-09-20. Also listed under T-0002. Engine files:
  - `Radix/Services/BulkDirectoryEnumerator.swift`
  - `IncrementalRescanPlanner.swift` and `IncrementalScanService.swift`
  - `SharedAllocationDeduplicator.swift` (APFS clone-aware accounting, see T-0009)

SHOULD
- **healeycodes/dumac**: Rust, 63 stars, pushed 2025-08-07. **It has no LICENSE file** (`gh api repos/healeycodes/dumac/license` returns 404), so all rights are reserved and we can take ideas only.
  - Design: a rayon pool plus `getattrlistbulk`, with a sharded inode set. The shard is `(inode >> 8) % SHARD_COUNT` because APFS allocates inodes sequentially (`src/main.rs:36-56`, `:118-128`).
  - Two blog posts carry measured numbers: https://healeycodes.com/maybe-the-fastest-disk-usage-program-on-macos and https://healeycodes.com/optimizing-my-disk-usage-program. Moving from Tokio to rayon cut context switches by about 80%. The shard fix brought lock collisions down from 176 to 4.7.
  - Its README claims 3.3x faster than diskus and 5.7x faster than `du -sh` on a synthetic tree of 409k files. Unverified.
- **KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage (pdu)**: Apache-2.0, 732 stars, Rust, pushed 2026-09-14.
  - Walk: rayon recursive walk over `read_dir` and `symlink_metadata` (`src/fs_tree_builder.rs:12,105,134`).
  - Hard links: a DashMap-based module (`src/hardlink/*.rs`).
  - Worth copying: its public benchmark repos against dust, dua, ncdu, gdu and du (github.com/KSXGitHub/parallel-disk-usage-0.5.2-benchmarks), a model for T-0004.
- **dundee/gdu**: MIT, 5999 stars, Go, pushed 2026-09-21.
  - Concurrency: a goroutine per directory, gated by a semaphore of `2*GOMAXPROCS` (`pkg/analyze/parallel.go:13,50-59`), reading with `os.ReadDir` and then Lstat.
  - Hard links: tracked by inode when `Nlink>1` (`pkg/analyze/dir_unix.go:15-29`).
  - Also has a sequential mode for HDDs (`sequential.go`), stored and SQLite analysis caching (`stored.go`, `sqlite.go`), and ncdu JSON import/export (`encode.go`).
- **ggbond268/MacTools**: GPL-3.0, 1217 stars, Swift, pushed 2026-09-22. Being GPL, we can take ideas only.
  - Its DiskClean plugin has a getattrlistbulk "FastWalker" that falls back to `fstatat` for each entry when attributes are missing (`Plugins/DiskClean/Sources/DiskCleanFastWalker.swift:4,65,100`), plus a matching SlowWalker.
  - `DiskCleanWorkerPool.swift:5-20` has an exactly-once resume gate, which handles the race between a timeout and a blocking syscall. That is a real problem when a Swift `async` scan wraps blocking syscalls.
  - `DiskCleanSizeCache.swift` caches sizes.
  - I found it through code search. Repo search misses it.
- **sveinbjornt/searchfs**: BSD-3-Clause, 134 stars, Objective-C, pushed 2026-09-04. A reusable `searchfs(2)` wrapper for catalog-level name search across a whole volume.
  - For the scan engine it only matters on HFS+.
  - It could also help leftover and bundle-ID search for the uninstaller (T-0005). Unverified how fast that is on APFS.

COULD
- **ncdu** (https://code.blicky.net/yorhel/ncdu, default branch `zig`, MIT per `LICENSES/MIT.txt`). It calls `fstatat` for every entry (`src/scan.zig:52`) and uses a LIFO queue behind a mutex and condvar with `--threads` (`scan.zig:100-141`). Hard links are detected with `nlink>1` (`:65`). Its JSON export is a de facto interchange format. GitHub copies such as `rofl0r/ncdu` (730 stars, 2020) are unofficial.
- **bootandy/dust**: Apache-2.0, 12292 stars, Rust. A `rayon::scope` walk with an FxHashSet of (inode, dev) for dedup (`src/dir_walker.rs:72-133`). The walk itself is a plain std::fs one; it is useful only as a benchmark baseline.
- **sharkdp/diskus**: Apache-2.0, 1246 stars, Rust. A rayon pool with a crossbeam channel, and one receiver thread that dedups inodes (`src/walk.rs:219-245`). A `du -sh` baseline.
- **mbrock/wtfs**: MIT, 7 stars, Zig, pushed 2026-08-15. A small getattrlistbulk scanner with a Python binding.
- **noxan/diskly**: no license, 11 stars, Swift. Parallel getattrlistbulk walk; its README bench claims ~/Library is 2.06x faster than `du -sk` and 2.47x faster than ncdu. Unverified.
- **solidiquis/erdtree**: MIT, 2603 stars, Rust. Uses the parallel walker from the `ignore` crate. Last push 2024-05-19 (stale).
- **zevv/duc**: LGPL-3.0, 711 stars, C. Stores the scan in an on-disk index database. Relevant only if we persist scans.
- **dyorgio/apfs-clone-checker**: MIT, 87 stars, C, 2021. Checks whether two files are APFS clones. Hand to T-0009.
- **FuzzyIdeas/Cling**: GPL-3.0, 862 stars, Swift. `Cling/VolumeIndex.swift` builds a getattrlistbulk volume index for instant find. Ideas only.
- **apple-oss-distributions/file_cmds**: `du/du.c` is the fts-based reference for macOS `du` semantics. The API reports no license (APSL/BSD per the files, unverified).

Skipped: muesli/duf (a df replacement, not a scanner), crumbyte/noxdir, chenquan/diskusage and emilevr/space (generic os.ReadDir or std walks with nothing new), the many 0-star getattrlistbulk clones, and SharkyRawr/GrandPerspective (a 0-star fork adding getattrlistbulk).

comments.author: topic-size-accounting
comments.text: From T-0009: scan-engine requirements (details in research/reports/topic-size-accounting.md, section Implications). (1) Use ALLOCSIZE for on-disk size and dedupe hard links by (dev, fileid); PRIVATESIZE counts every link in full. (2) Walk /System/Volumes/Data, not /: firmlinks make /Users == /System/Volumes/Data/Users (same dev+ino), and Data-root items like 'macOS Install Data' (12.1 GB here) are unreachable from /. (3) SF_FIRMLINK shows only in getattrlistbulk ATTR_CMN_FLAGS, not in stat(). (4) Set IOPOL_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES_OFF and skip SF_DATALESS. (5) URL totalFileAllocatedSize is nil for directories, so there is no recursive shortcut.

comments.author: topic-distribution-permissions
comments.text: Swift 6 facts for the scan engine (verified-locally, macOS 26.6, 8 cores; see research/reports/topic-distribution-permissions.md S1-S6): (1) under Xcode 26 defaults a 'nonisolated async' scan func called from @MainActor runs ON the main thread; mark entry points @concurrent or keep the engine in a module without default MainActor isolation. (2) the cooperative pool width = hw.ncpu (64 blocking 200 ms tasks took 1.62 s on 8 cores), so blocking getattrlistbulk/fts calls belong on dedicated bounded threads, not in Task groups. (3) a non-Sendable class tree built off-main can be returned to MainActor via 'sending'. Please factor into engine comparisons.

comments.author: dive-tencent-lemon-cleaner
comments.text: Handoff from T-0015 (Lemon): F-0019. Lemon's disk map uses getattrlistbulk but adds 1-2 NSURL NSURLIsUbiquitousItemKey lookups per entry on macOS 13+ (LMFileScanTask.m:191-235). Bench research/bench/lemon-ubiquity-lookup/walk.m, single thread, /System/Library/Frameworks, 40 904 entries, warm, 2 runs each: bulk only 0.293/0.340 s, bulk + ATTR_CMN_FLAGS (SF_DATALESS) 0.301/0.290 s, bulk + NSURL lookups 3.806/3.944 s. Takeaway for the engine: request ATTR_CMN_FLAGS in the bulk call and never build an NSURL per entry.

Engine verdict: port the scheduler (lib.rs:128-1469) and the attribute parser (macos/attributes.rs) to Swift; both are MIT. comments.author: dive-healeycodes-dumac
comments.text: dumac verdict (T-0030): your discovery note checks out on speed. On the shared fixture it took 0.67 s against 0.72 s for dua, so it is tied with dua; it is 1.98x faster than diskus (the README claims 3.26x) and 9.8x faster than du (the README claims 5.66x). Its robustness is weak, and every failure below exits 0: it aborts with no output at 127 nesting levels (a 128 KiB stack buffer per recursion level), it counts EMFILE as 0 B and leaks an fd on every failed listing (F-0060), its dedupe key is the inode alone so a second mounted volume vanishes, and it drops paths past PATH_MAX (F-0008). The (inode>>8) sharding fixes contention that a nlink>1 filter would remove: only 503 of the fixture's 300k file entries are extra links. Ideas only, because it has no license. Report: research/reports/sources/healeycodes-dumac.md.

comments.author: dive-ggbond268-mactools
comments.text: MacTools DiskClean engine numbers (research/reports/sources/ggbond268-mactools.md). The single-thread DiskCleanFastWalker (getattrlistbulk, 64 KiB buffer, fd-anchored DFS) measured 34-40k files/s on a 728k-file tree larger than kern.maxvnodes (21.25 s and 18.32 s) and 160-190k files/s warm on 23k files (research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/walker_throughput_main.swift, built from the unmodified Apache-era-identical sources). The parser layout check found 0 mismatches on APFS. Engine patterns worth taking from Apache@9197035: the exactly-once resume gate plus an abandonable resident thread pool for blocking syscalls, and typed walk completeness. Weakness filed as F-0065: a 20 s wall clock per item with one thread per item means a partial size, and a partial size is never cleanable.

tasks.title: UI/UX reference survey
tasks.description: What the sleekest macOS utility UIs do (open and closed source): layout, visualization, motion, onboarding for Full Disk Access, destructive-action confirmation. Output: design principles for macontrol.

comments.author: sweep-ui
comments.text:
## sweep-ui: UI/UX reference candidates (facts from `gh api repos/...` on 2026-09-23)

18 candidates: 4 must, 8 should, 6 could. 3 of them (Radix, PureMac, Pearcleaner) are already on T-0001/T-0002 and are listed here only for their UI code. Nothing was cloned. File references come from `gh api .../contents` and git tree listings.

**MUST**
- **colinvkim/Radix**: MIT, 861 stars, Swift, pushed 2026-09-20. Also on T-0002. The best open-source model for FDA onboarding and chart interaction:
  - Onboarding runs welcome, access, tour (`Radix/Models/OnboardingPage.swift:2`). The access step is tri-state: granted / "Enable Radix under Full Disk Access" / "Full Disk Access could not be verified". It offers "Quit & Reopen" and "Skip for Now" (`Radix/Features/Onboarding/OnboardingFlowView.swift:57-80,117,140`).
  - Keyboard navigation of the charts: `Features/Visualization/ChartKeyboardInteractionView.swift`, `ChartViewportControls.swift`.
  - A firmlink-aware delete block list: `Models/TrashSafetyPolicy.swift:118-130`.
  - Reuse precedent: bysiber/cleardisk vendors RadixCore at rev d26a57b behind a bridge file (`Vendor/DiskScanBackend/UPSTREAM.md`).
- **momenbasel/PureMac**: MIT, 6,677 stars, Swift, pushed 2026-09-23. Also on T-0001. The user named it as the base. The onboarding pattern is worth keeping: a 1 s FDA poll with auto-advance latch (`PureMac/Views/OnboardingView.swift:19,61,188`), plus `Services/PermissionCoordinator.swift`, `Views/Components/PermissionSheet.swift` and `Services/Haptics.swift`. Its probe is wrong, though; see F-0001.
- **MacPaw/PermissionsKit**: MIT, 312 stars, Objective-C, pushed 2026-09-21. Made by CleanMyMac's maker, and has SPM support since 2025-08-27.
  - FDA check runs several probes. `open()` success means granted, EPERM/EACCES means denied, anything else means not determined (`PermissionsKit/Private/FullDiskAccess/MPFullDiskAccessAuthorizer.m:66-110`, rationale comment at :86-90).
  - Deep link: `x-apple.systempreferences:com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles` (:140).
  - This is close to the fix F-0001 proposes, and MIT means we can reuse it. Caveat (unverified): its probe list includes `/Library/Preferences/com.apple.TimeMachine.plist` (:95), and it returns granted on the first readable file. If that plist can be read without FDA on macOS 26, it has the same false-granted bug as F-0001. Re-run the F-0001 check script on that path.
- **DaisyDisk** (closed, https://daisydiskapp.com/guide/4/en/DeletingFiles/): the benchmark for destructive-action UX.
  - Delete is staged in a "Collector", reached by drag, context menu or ⌘⌫. It expands to a reviewable list with a per-item ×.
  - It refuses `/System` and `/Library`.
  - Delete starts a 5-second countdown with Cancel, then removes files permanently, not to the Trash, so the space is really freed (https://daisydiskapp.com/guide/4/en/Undelete/).
  - It explains that Time Machine local snapshots turn freed space into "purgeable" space.

**SHOULD**
- **thaw-app/Thaw**: GPL-3.0, 11,438 stars, Swift, pushed 2026-09-22. The maintained continuation of Ice: file headers read "Copyright (Ice) © 2023-2025 Jordan Baird / (Thaw) © 2026" (`Thaw/Permissions/Permission.swift:5-6`). It has an onboarding tour with mockup slides (`Thaw/Onboarding/Tour/TourMockups.swift`, `OnboardingPermissionsView.swift`) and Liquid Glass gating (`Thaw/Onboarding/GlassSupport.swift`). GPL, so ideas only.
- **mrkai77/Loop**: GPL-3.0, 11,655 stars, pushed 2026-09-11. Its motion system is a small named set of presets (fluid, relaxed, snappy, brisk, instant) with explicit timing curves, for example fluid `.timingCurve(0, 0.26, 0.45, 1, duration: 0.325)` (`Loop/Utilities/AnimationConfiguration.swift:14-43`). The settings panes show live previews (`Settings Window/Theming/PreviewConfiguration.swift`). Ideas only.
- **EmergeTools/Pow**: MIT, 4,397 stars, pushed 2026-04-13. A drop-in SwiftUI transitions package (Vanish, Poof, Blur and more, `Example/Pow Example/Examples/Transitions/*`), with `Sources/Pow/Extensions/Animation+TimingCurves.swift`. Candidate for the "item removed" feedback. Reusable.
- **insidegui/VirtualBuddy**: BSD-2-Clause, 8,737 stars, pushed 2026-09-21.
  - A Liquid Glass back-compat layer: `VirtualUI/Source/Components/LiquidGlassCompat/*`, including `AirGlassEffect.swift` and `MaterialView.swift`. Useful if we support macOS older than 26.
  - A confirmation-alert helper: `Components/NSAlert+Confirmation.swift`.
  - Progress views: `MaskProgressView.swift`, `ContinuousProgressIndicator.swift`.
  - Permissive license.
- **CodeEditApp/CodeEdit**: MIT, 23,038 stars, pushed 2026-08-18. A large MIT codebase that mixes SwiftUI and AppKit. See the settings architecture (`CodeEdit/Features/Settings/Pages/*`), `Features/CodeEditUI/Views/GlassEffectView.swift` and `ActivityViewer/Notifications/CECircularProgressView.swift`. Parts can be reused.
- **exelban/stats**: MIT, 42,062 stars, pushed 2026-09-22. AppKit chart widgets that stay light enough to live in the menu bar (`Kit/Widgets/BarChart.swift`, `LineChart.swift`, `PieChart.swift`, `Kit/plugins/Charts.swift`). The reference if macontrol gets a menu-bar free-space gauge.
- **alienator88/Pearcleaner**: Apache-2.0 + Commons Clause (API says NOASSERTION), 14,715 stars. Also on T-0001/T-0005. UI worth reading:
  - Undo restores files from the Trash (`Pearcleaner/Logic/UndoManager.swift:62` delete, `:176` restoreFiles).
  - `Views/DeleteHistoryView.swift`.
  - `Views/Components/PermissionsSheetView.swift` and `TCCPermissionViewer.swift`.
  - Learn from it only.
- **CleanMyMac** (closed, MacPaw):
  - The FDA request is an "Allow Full Disk Access" recommendation in Assistant, and the app states what degrades without it (https://macpaw.com/support/cleanmymac/knowledgebase/full-disk-access).
  - A "Safety Database" keeps system files out of results (https://macpaw.com/support/cleanmymac-x/knowledgebase/safety-database).
  - Each module has its own ignore list (https://macpaw.com/support/cleanmymac-x/knowledgebase/cleanmymac-safety).

**COULD**
- inket/FullDiskAccess: MIT, 82 stars. `promptIfNotGranted` has alert suppression. On macOS 14 and later, including 15 and 26, it probes a single path, `~/Library/Containers/com.apple.stocks`, and treats any error as "not granted" (`Sources/FullDiskAccess/FullDiskAccess.swift:21,47-60`). That means a missing container would read as a false "denied" (unverified at runtime). The Sequoia/Tahoe PR #3 was never merged. PermissionsKit is better.
- jordanbaird/Ice: GPL-3.0, 29,690 stars. Last commit 2025-09-20, superseded by Thaw. Its `Ice/Permissions/*` is the origin of Thaw's permissions window.
- sindresorhus/Settings: MIT, 1,551 stars. A Settings window with panes, for AppKit and SwiftUI.
- twostraws/Vortex: MIT, 1,582 stars. SwiftUI particles, if we ever want a "space freed" moment. Low priority.
- Jarvis322/macos-sysdata: 785 stars. **Proprietary source-available** (LICENSE: "published ... so that anyone can read them ... not so that they can be reused"). It breaks "System Data" into items, one probe per category (`Sources/SysDataMenu/Probes/*Probes.swift`). Ideas only.
- bysiber/cleardisk: MIT, 704 stars. Already on T-0001. `Sources/ClearDisk/FullDiskAccessProbe.swift` and `DiskSpaceTreemap.swift`; vendors RadixCore (see Radix above).

**Design principles I draw from this, for the synthesis:**
1. Treat FDA as a tri-state step (granted / denied / unknown) with a deep link, a 1 s poll and auto-advance, and "Quit & Reopen" when needed. Let the user skip, but keep showing a visible "limited scan" state.
2. Every destructive action goes through a staging area the user can review (DaisyDisk Collector, Radix Discard Pile). Apply a protected-path block list before anything is staged. Then offer one of two confirmation models:
   - Trash with Undo (Pearcleaner), or
   - permanent delete behind a cancel countdown (DaisyDisk).
   Also explain purgeable/snapshot space after a delete.
3. Motion comes from a few named presets with explicit curves (Loop) and must honor Reduce Motion. Use Liquid Glass on macOS 26, with a fallback layer for older systems (VirtualBuddy, Thaw GlassSupport).

No new analysis finding filed. The FDA-probe evidence above belongs to the existing F-0001: PermissionsKit is a reusable MIT implementation of its fix, and FullDiskAccess shows the opposite failure (a false "denied").

comments.author: dive-daisydisk
comments.text:
dive-daisydisk (T-0028): DaisyDisk UI facts for the synthesis. Full detail: research/reports/sources/daisydisk.md, UI section and Reuse table.
- Report page: a path bar with back/forward on top; the sunburst on the left with the current size in the centre disc; a sidebar list on the right whose colour bullets match the petal hues; the Collector bar at the bottom (ring gauge "N GB collected" + red Delete). Screenshot: https://daisydiskapp.com/img/home/intro-ss1.png.
- Interaction: hover previews a folder in the sidebar, click drills down, a click in the centre goes up. Small items merge into an expandable "smaller objects" petal, and its expanded state is remembered per folder (guide UnderstandingSunburst, release 4.25).
- Keyboard map (guide Hotkeys): arrows/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End, ⌘↑ parent, ⌘[ ⌘] history, Return drill, Space Quick Look, ⌘⌫ to/from Collector, ⌘-click reveal, ⌘R/⇧⌘R rescan, ⌥ gauge mode. Keyboard navigation only arrived in 2023 (4.25), so ship it in v1.
- FDA: a Preferences tab, not a first-run step. It shows the status, then Step 1 "Open System Preferences" and Step 2 "drag the bouncing app icon into the list", then a relaunch (dd_fda.png).
- Protected drop: the refusal is shown in the Collector bar with the item's name ("System" is required by OS X and should not be removed).
- Destructive UX: a 5 s countdown with Cancel, then a PERMANENT delete (no Trash). Snapshot/purgeable purge goes through the same Collector (my finding F-0056). The design principle I'd add: system-space actions never share the file tray.

comments.author: dive-tencent-lemon-cleaner
comments.text: Size-accounting evidence from T-0015 (Lemon), not filed as findings because they overlap F-0004/F-0006/F-0010. (a) The cleaner's folder size stops a walk after 10 s and returns the partial sum with no flag (localPod/LemonFileManager/.../LMFileAttributesTool.m:28,79-93,138-140). Only CoreSimulator and DerivedData are exempt, and the result is cached for the scan. (b) Its first try is Spotlight kMDItemPhysicalSize, but mdls shows (null) for ~/Library/Caches and for Calculator.app (verified-locally), so it never hits. (c) The disk map mixes units: .app/.bundle/.simruntime use NSMetadataItemFSSizeKey (logical; Calculator.app is 6 006 599 B vs du -sk 3 524 KiB) while everything else uses ATTR_FILE_ALLOCSIZE (LMFileScanTask.m:218-245). (d) No (dev,ino) dedupe anywhere: cleaner, disk map or duplicate finder (duplicates show hard links of one inode as removable).

comments.author: bench-harness
comments.text: Answer to your T-0004 question (PRIVATESIZE cost): serial getattrlistbulk walk, adding forkattr PRIVATESIZE|CLONEID|EXT_FLAGS costs +61% sys / +12% wall on the 300k-file fixture and +70% sys / +64% wall on ~/projects (469k entries). The fixture's sum of private sizes (1,446,752,256) matches the clones-once total minus the shared extents to the byte, so F-0004's model holds, partial clone included. comments.author: dive-colinvkim-radix
comments.text: Radix (colinvkim/Radix@14a76df, MIT) is a working reference for F-0004's 'on disk' half: hard links claim (dev,ino) when linkCount>1, full clones claim (ATTR_CMNEXT_REALDEVID, CLONEID) when CLONE_REFCNT>1 (BulkDirectoryEnumerator.swift:717-733); lexicographically smallest path keeps the bytes, others subtract allocatedSize / dataAllocatedSize, hard links resolved before clone groups (SharedAllocationOwnerAccumulator.swift:10-20,149-194); EF_MAY_SHARE_BLOCKS files are flagged, not deduped (FileNodeRecord.swift:225-249). Residual F-0004-class gap: Discard Pile total and 'bytes moved to Trash' sum the deduplicated allocatedSize (ViewModels/AppModel.swift:43-60, Services/AppUsageStatsStore.swift:97-123), so trashing a clone/hard-link 'winner' whose siblings stay outside the selection shows bytes that are not freed. Not filed (duplicate class).

comments.author: dive-tkslucas-neodisk
comments.text: Note from T-0024 (Neodisk, code-read, not measured): Neodisk computes hidden space = (capacity - volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage) - scannedAllocated (Sources/NeodiskKit/Services/VolumeSpaceInfo.swift:43-54). Its own comment says hidden includes 'purgeable space, local snapshots' (NeodiskUI/Model/FreeSpaceModel.swift:24-26), but usedBytes already counts purgeable as available, so purgeable can never land in hidden, and purgeable files that the scan does see (they are in the tree) lower the hidden figure. On this Mac purgeable = important 40.25 GB - free 38.42 GB = 1.83 GB, no local snapshots, too small to show it. Also useful for your rows 5-8: Neodisk charges non-first full-clone members min(allocated, ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE) (CloneDeduplicator.swift:76-140) and does not special-case UF_COMPRESSED; clone members are gated on CLONE_REFCNT > 1, which your row 7 says is 0 for decmpfs files, so that trap is probably not hit.

comments.author: dive-byron-dua-cli
comments.text: Clone numbers for F-0004 from dua-cli 2.45.0, taken from the T-0004 bench (research/bench/results/fixture-summary.json). 'dua --deduplicate-apfs-clones' reports 512,053,248 B less than plain dua minus the 8,417,280 B PATH_MAX loss, so it dedups 503,635,968 B. That is exactly 3 x 167,772,160 (the full 160 MiB clones) + 319,488 (the 100 small clones). The partial clone (real_b_partial.bin, 119 MiB = 124,780,544 B shared) is still counted twice. dua keys a group by (dev, ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID), counts it only when EF_MAY_SHARE_BLOCKS is set, and charges later members allocated - data_allocated, so resource forks stay private: crates/dua-lib/src/macos/attributes.rs:55-56,152-164 and src/inodefilter.rs:177-212. The feature is opt-in (README 'Usage', src/options.rs:157-160) and cost almost nothing in the bench (fixture 0.69 s vs 0.70 s, ~/projects 1.92 s vs 1.88 s, within noise). The first-seen member is picked by a race. See F-0054.

comments.author: dive-daisydisk
comments.text:
dive-daisydisk (T-0028): DaisyDisk's size policy, from the vendor docs.
- Physical (allocated) size, except on network drives. HFS+-compressed files count at their physical size.
- Hard links: the first occurrence counts, the rest get 0 B. Full APFS clones get the same treatment since 4.34 (2026-07), on macOS 14+ only. Partial clones are never accounted for (guide HardLinks para 11-20).
- Two consequences for the classes on the board: folder sizes depend on traversal order (the class of F-0054), and the Collector's "N GB collected" for a clone's first copy is bytes that Delete does not free while the other copy exists (the class of F-0004; inferred from the docs, not run).
- Hidden space is computed as used − scanned, with purgeable space, other volumes and snapshots (for reference, not additive) as its children.

comments.author: dive-daisydisk
comments.text:
dive-daisydisk (T-0028): platform facts from DaisyDisk's public blog and release log. Vendor statements, not re-measured here.
(1) Sonoma: scans stall in ~/Library/Containers and ~/Library/Group Containers because of Sonoma's per-access privacy checks. Apple acknowledged the bug. DaisyDisk's workaround is ⌥-click Scan, which skips both folders (https://daisydiskapp.com/blog/daisydisk-4-26-1-released/). This is worth a bench on macOS 26 (T-0004).
(2) Tahoe: sandboxed (App Store) builds "forgot" security-scoped disk grants on every launch, Apple r.157722315; a workaround shipped in 4.33 (blog 2025-10-15).
(3) APFS clone detection works only on macOS 14+. DaisyDisk 4.34 broke scanning on older systems and 4.34.1 fixed it (blog 2026-07-01).
(4) Their scan of "/" adds "non-firmlinked items of the Data volume in /System/Volumes/Data", /private/var/VM, Recovery and Preboot (4.9, 2020), which is the firmlink-dedup approach F-0031 asks for.
(5) Time Machine volumes: nothing can be deleted from them (guide TimeMachine para 19).

comments.author: dive-alienator88-pearcleaner
comments.text:
## Extra evidence for existing findings (not re-filed). All cites are alienator88/Pearcleaner@7724df7.

**F-0011 (filed against PureMac's copy; Pearcleaner is the origin and is worse):**
- Pearcleaner still scans bare `$HOME` (`Logic/Locations.swift:59`), plus `~/Documents` (:61) and `~/Desktop` (:62). PureMac removed `$HOME` because it matched `~/.claude` and `~/.ssh` (PureMac `Locations.swift:44-47`).
- Strict mode, the default (`AppPathsFetch.swift:32`), is also affected: name EQUALITY hits `~/Documents/<App>` and `~/.<app>`, and per-app include keywords are substrings (`Conditions.swift:88-93`: Chrome → `chrome`, `google`).
- Contents/MacOS binary names of 5+ chars become match keys (`Logic/AppInfoFetch.swift:728-740`, used at `AppPathsFetch.swift:357-367`). This likely explains #557 (Audacity vs every iPad app's `Wrapper/`; unverified). Locally, Android Studio's binary is `studio`.
- The confirm dialog defaults to off (`Views/FilesView/FilesView.swift:25`). With it off, AlinFoundation@f61241c `Utilities.swift:379-380` runs `onOk()` directly.
- verified-locally (Strict transcription, `research/sources/alienator88-pearcleaner-repro/out.txt`): OpenSCAD → `~/Documents/OpenSCAD` (#587), Chrome → `~/Documents/chrome (film simulation)` (#571), Claude → `~/.claude`. All pre-selected (`AppPathsFetch.swift:808`), and all pass the guard (now F-0024).
- Oracle for the fix: `research/bench/uninstall-oracle/fixture.sh`.

**F-0002 (root helper):**
- EVERY trash move goes to root when the helper is installed, user-owned files included (`Logic/Utilities.swift:855-857` via `UndoManager.swift:236`). `restoreFiles` builds the same unescaped `mv "<a>" "<b>"` strings (`UndoManager.swift:184-205`).
- The non-helper fallback is `AuthorizationExecuteWithPrivileges`, found with `dlsym`, running `/bin/sh -c <same string>` as root (AlinFoundation `Sources/AlinFoundation/Authorization.swift:15-56`). The last fallback is `/bin/sh -c` as the user (`UndoManager.swift:250-252,270-290`).
- The runSUCommand call is `try!` (`UndoManager.swift:236`).
- Dead code, do not port: `Logic/Brew/HomebrewUninstaller.swift:199,420-428` runs `pkill -9 -f '<AppName>'` and `launchctl bootout gui/$UID/...` through the root helper, where `$UID` is 0. It is unreachable because `useBrewUninstallZap = true` (:17). Measured against this Mac's live process list, 41 of 4,002 cask app names regex-match unrelated processes (e.g. `support` → tccd and cloudd; `look` → quicklookd). See `research/sources/alienator88-pearcleaner-repro/pkill_hits.txt`.

**F-0004 / T-0009 (sizes):** Pearcleaner uses logical sizes everywhere (`Logic/Lipo.swift:444-462` fileSizeKey, `AppPathsFetch.swift:903` kMDItemLogicalSize). kMDItemPhysicalSize is fetched and never used (`AppInfoFetch.swift:394,407`). A sparse 1 GiB file (Docker.raw-style) reads 1,073,741,824 logical and 0 allocated (verified-locally with `stat -f '%z %b'`), so VM images in leftovers are overstated. F-0004's "after" (ALLOCSIZE) already covers this.

comments.author: dive-ggbond268-mactools
comments.text: Extra evidence for F-0031 from MacTools StorageExplorer (GPL; report research/reports/sources/ggbond268-mactools.md). A devid mount guard fed by getattrlistbulk does NOT stop at mount points: ATTR_CMN_DEVID of a mount-point entry is the COVERED volume's device. In /System/Volumes, Hardware, Update, Preboot, xarts, VM and iSCPreboot all report the parent devid 16777229 in the bulk result, while lstat gives each its own dev (scratch probe mountdev.c, macOS 26.6). StorageExplorerScanner checks devid on directories only (StorageExplorerScanner.swift:282, 312-316), so it descends into the mount point and counts the mounted volume's root files. research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/mount_guard_probe.sh (100 MB APFS image at root/mnt, 64 MiB file at its root): root size 68,157,440 B vs 1,048,576 B, and mnt/big.bin is listed. MacTools DiskClean checks devid on every entry and correctly reports partial(crossedMountPoint). F-0031's ATTR_DIR_MOUNTSTATUS after is the right fix. Also: never trust bulk ATTR_CMN_DEVID alone for mount detection.

comments.author: dive-healeycodes-dumac
comments.text: Extra evidence for F-0044, this time from a scanner: dumac (healeycodes/dumac@1ffbe3c) **aborts at 127 nested folders**. The process dies with SIGABRT and prints "has overflowed its stack", with no total at all. 126 levels work, in 3 of 3 runs. The cause is `get_dir_info` putting `[0u8; 128*1024]` on the stack (src/main.rs:218). That function is inlined into the recursive `calculate_size`: the prologue is `sub x9, sp, #0x20, lsl #12`. With 16 MiB rayon stacks (:123-125), that is about 128 KiB per level, 27x shallower than GP's 3,500 levels, and it also costs about 128 KiB of RSS per level. Repro: research/bench/healeycodes-dumac/run_probes.sh §2. Suggestion: F-0044's after says "The scanner is already fd-relative ... so a deep tree reaches the model intact". dumac shows that fd-relative is not enough, and the scanner also needs an explicit work queue (F-0009) with no large stack buffers. The 10,000-level deepchain fixture in F-0044's "how" would catch this, if the scan step is included.

comments.author: dive-ksxgithub-parallel-disk-usage
comments.text: From T-0031 (pdu), for F-0047/F-0054: pdu -H is a third deterministic attribution rule. Each folder counts each inode once within its own subtree (du -s semantics): node.size -= size*(links_in_subtree-1) (src/data_tree/hardlink.rs:16-44 @c30e46f). It does not depend on walk order, but a folder holding 1 of 2 links still shows the full size, though deleting it frees 0. So the LCA rule in F-0047 stays the better target. Two implementation warnings: pdu filters the parent's link-path list by strip_prefix for every child (quadratic: 8k same-folder pairs cost 7.89 s user vs 0.03 s scan), and it runs after sort and cutoff, so order and hidden items use pre-dedup sizes (F-0059). Its test scenarios are worth porting as fixtures (tests/hardlinks_deduplication.rs: internal, external, mixed, exclusive-only, external-only, complex).

tasks.title: Undo journal for Move to Trash + persistent staging (Discard Pile) across rescans and relaunch
tasks.description: Feature gap seen in Radix (no defect filed): SystemIntegration.moveToTrash drops FileManager.trashItem's resultingItemURL (Radix/Services/SystemIntegration.swift:448-449), so there is no in-app undo/Put Back; the Discard Pile is an in-memory set of node IDs bound to one snapshot (ViewModels/TrashFlowController.swift:63-67,146-159) and is lost on relaunch. macontrol: record (original path, trashed URL, dev/ino, size, time) per move in a local journal, offer Undo for the last batch and a history view; persist the staging list keyed by (dev, ino) + path so it survives rescans. Related findings: F-0012 (permanent delete, PureMac), F-0036 (MangoDisk mid-delete orphan).

comments.author: dive-daisydisk
comments.text:
dive-daisydisk (T-0028): the DaisyDisk Collector is the reference for this task.
- In: drag, ⌘⌫ or context menu. The tray expands into a list with Quick Look and a × per item, and it refuses protected items at drop time with a named reason.
- Out: Delete starts a 5 s countdown with Cancel, then deletes PERMANENTLY. No Trash, because "no disk space would actually be recovered" (guide DeletingFiles para 16-17, Undelete para 6).
- Scan results, and so presumably the Collector too, live only while the app runs (release 2.0: "remembered while the application is running"). Whether the Collector survives a relaunch is unverified; the app was not launched.
- For this task: keep the tray and the cancel window, persist the staging list, and answer "space not freed" with "Empty these from Trash" (F-0042) rather than a permanent delete. Also, snapshot/purgeable purge must never be staged in this tray (F-0056).

comments.author: dive-ggbond268-mactools
comments.text: Input from MacTools (F-0064): DiskClean freezes by renaming to .mactools-staged-<UUID> and then trashes that path. The Trash entry is hidden in Finder (verified with research/bench/ggbond268-mactools/trash_name_probe.swift), Put Back restores the hidden name, and later scans protect it forever. StorageExplorer in the same repo stages into <parent>/.mactools-trash-<UUID>/<original name>, so the Trash keeps the visible name, but it then rmdirs the staging folder, and Put Back behaviour is unverified. For the undo journal: keep the original leaf name through staging, record resultingItemURL, and restore by our own RENAME_EXCL rather than relying on Finder Put Back. Reusable Apache-2.0 base: DiskCleanRemovalPrimitive/StagingJournal/StagingReconciler @9197035 (see T-0003 comment).
