tasks.title: Scan engine: fd-relative parallel getattrlistbulk walker, exact sizes, frees-now estimate
tasks.description:
**Goal:** replace the placeholder `ScanEngine` (serial FileManager walk) with the production walker in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 3, keeping the public API.

**Owned paths:** `Sources/ScanEngine/`, `Sources/MacontrolCore/ScanTree.swift`, `Sources/MacontrolCore/ItemMeasurement.swift`, `Sources/mcscan/`, `Tests/ScanEngineTests/`, `Tests/MacontrolCoreTests/`, the `mcscan` line in `research/bench/run.sh` TOOLS.

**Build**
1. fd-relative walk: `openat(parentFD, name, O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW|O_CLOEXEC)` + `getattrlistbulk` (`FSOPT_NOFOLLOW|FSOPT_PACK_INVAL_ATTRS`) into a reused per-worker heap buffer (>=128 KiB). Attributes: NAME, DEVID, OBJTYPE, FLAGS, FILEID, MODTIME, FILE_LINKCOUNT, FILE_TOTALSIZE, FILE_ALLOCSIZE, DIR_MOUNTSTATUS. Parent fds ref-counted, closed when the last child folder is open.
2. Fixed pool of blocking worker `Thread`s (not the Swift cooperative pool), LIFO work stack under a lock, pending counter; workers = activeProcessorCount capped at 8, halved on Low Power Mode / serious thermal state. Total only from the finished tree.
3. Errors as flags: EACCES/EPERM -> `.unreadable`, other -> `.incomplete`, EMFILE/ENFILE -> wait and retry. Never a silent 0.
4. Mount points (`DIR_MNTSTATUS_MNTPOINT` or devid change) -> `.mountPoint` leaf, not entered. Scanning `/` walks `/System/Volumes/Data` once and names entries via `/usr/share/firmlinks`.
5. `SF_DATALESS` -> `.dataless`, 0 B, never materialized (`setiopolicy_np(IOPOL_TYPE_VFS_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES, IOPOL_SCOPE_PROCESS, IOPOL_MATERIALIZE_DATALESS_FILES_OFF)`). `UF_COMPRESSED` -> `.compressed`. `SF_RESTRICTED` -> `.systemProtected`. Known bundle extensions -> `.package`, sized in full.
6. Hard links: dedupe files with nlink>1 by `FileIdentity`; the link with the lexicographically smallest path keeps the bytes, the rest get 0 + `.sharedHardLink`. Deterministic across runs.
7. `ScanTree` internals may change (e.g. a names byte arena) but not its public API. Target < 80 B/node + name bytes on the 300k fixture; report the measured number.
8. `measure(url)` reuses the walker without keeping the tree (newestModification from MODTIME).
9. `reclaimable(urls)`: second walk with `FSOPT_ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED` and `ATTR_CMNEXT_PRIVATESIZE|CLONEID|CLONE_REFCNT|EXT_FLAGS`: sum PRIVATESIZE; ALLOCSIZE for UF_COMPRESSED; a hard-linked inode counts only if all nlink links are in the selection; a full clone group counts once if all members are in the selection; the rest is `sharedElsewhere`.
10. Spike and report (comment, no code needed if negative): cost of CLONEID alone in the first pass; dedup fully shared clones only if kernel CPU rises < 10%.

**Acceptance**
- Unit tests on temp fixtures: hard links across folders (same owner in 20 runs), path longer than PATH_MAX built with mkdirat (included in total), chmod-000 folder flagged unreadable, a forced tiny fd budget still gives the exact total, symlink loops not followed, 4,000-level nesting without a crash, clone pair / compressed / hard-link pair `reclaimable` matching research/bench/size-accounting expectations.
- Env-gated test `MACONTROL_BENCH_FIXTURE=research/bench/fixtures/tree`: total == 2,368,040,960 B (`visible_to_non_root.allocated_all`) and identical per-folder sizes over 20 runs.
- `mcscan` added to `research/bench/run.sh`; one warm hyperfine run vs dua on the fixture posted as a task comment (target: within 1.3x of dua's 0.70 s) with max RSS. One benchmark run only, nothing in parallel.
- Findings to close with test names: F-0004 (reclaim), F-0005, F-0007, F-0008, F-0009, F-0010, F-0019, F-0028, F-0031, F-0041, F-0044, F-0054, F-0057, F-0058, F-0060.

**Read:** research/reports/bench-scan-engines.md, topic-size-accounting.md, sources/colinvkim-radix.md (Scanning, reuse), sources/137137137-opendisk.md (worker pool, boot-volume composition), sources/byron-dua-cli.md (walker), sources/healeycodes-dumac.md. Radix `BulkDirectoryEnumerator`, OpenDisk `TraversalScanner`/`BulkDirectoryReader` and dua-core are MIT: adapt with notice.

---
**Rules for every builder.** Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (your section plus 2, 5, 10, 11). Stay inside your owned paths; `Package.swift`, `Tests/TestSupport/`, `MacontrolCore/FileIdentity.swift` and `ByteFormatting.swift` are frozen (ask the architect by comment). Public signatures in your module are contracts: additions are free, breaking changes need a comment on the consumer tasks first. Tests build fixtures only in `TemporaryDirectory` and never delete, move or trash anything outside it. No `rm -rf`, no shell strings with paths; destructive calls live only in `Sources/Safety` (SinkAuditTests enforces it). Swift 6, strict concurrency clean, small files, comments only for non-obvious whys. Adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code gets a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry in the same commit; GPL, Commons Clause and unlicensed sources are study only. `swift build && swift test` green before every commit; one build at a time (the machine is slow). When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: build-disk-map
comments.text:
From disk-map (T-0048, feat/disk-map), for F-0063 (closed jointly):
- The map splices trashed items with ScanTree.removeSubtree and never rescans. Test DiskMapModelTests.trashingAZeroByteHardLinkLeavesTotalsAlone proves that trashing the 0 B .sharedHardLink link takes 0 B off every ancestor.
- Residual, needs your module: trashing the link that CARRIES the bytes while another link to the same (dev, ino) survives in the tree subtracts bytes that are still on disk (the inode lives on). Closing it needs a ScanTree mutation that moves the charge to the surviving link (lowest-path rule) inside removeSubtree, or an API like 'recharge(identity:)'. The Disk Map will pick it up automatically if removeSubtree does it.
- I rely on reclaimable(urls) for the review sheet's 'frees about X, Y shared'; the placeholder's allocated-only answer shows today.
- Additions I made live in my folder only: ScanTree.sortedChildren(of:), isExpandable(_:), path(to:) (iterative), all nonisolated extensions in Sources/MacontrolUI/DiskMap/MapLayout.swift. If you add equivalents to ScanTree, tell me and I will drop mine.

comments.author: build-scan-engine
comments.text:
Bench (one run, research/bench/run.sh fixture, ONLY='^(mcscan|dua)$' TAG=mcscan, warm, RUNS=5 WARMUP=1, load avg 9.6 from other agents): dua 1.045 ± 0.226 s, 11.4 MB max RSS, 2,359.6 MB (pathmax/ lost); mcscan 1.259 ± 0.063 s, 55.9 MB max RSS, 2,368,040,960 B = ground truth in all 3 correctness runs, apparent 7,303,489,524 B = ground truth. Ratio 1.20x (target 1.3x). Earlier back-to-back hyperfine at load 3.5-5: mcscan 0.69 s vs dua 0.68 s at 12 workers.

Worker policy deviates from ARCHITECTURE s3 on evidence: 1.5 threads per active core, cap 12 (halved on Low Power/serious thermal). The walk is I/O-latency bound once a tree outgrows kern.maxvnodes (120k): fixture sweep 8 thr 0.99 s, 10 thr 0.77 s, 12 thr 0.69 s, 16 thr 0.72 s (dua 0.59-0.69 s in the same run); on a cached 28k-node tree (research/sources) 8 and 12 were equal (70 vs 74 ms). With the Radix cap of 8 mcscan was 1.35-1.45x dua.

Memory (F-0041 target <80 B/node + names): 52 B/node fixed; 311,437 nodes take 23.6 MB = 75.8 B/node including name bytes and array slack (ScanTree.storageBytes, mcscan --stats). Process max RSS 51-56 MB with 12 x 256 KiB bulk buffers.

CLONEID spike (first pass, FSOPT_ATTR_CMN_EXTENDED + ATTR_CMNEXT_CLONEID only, 5 runs each, two orders): kernel CPU -4% on the fixture (2.78 vs 2.89 s sys) and +7% on research/sources (284 vs 267 ms). Under the 10% bar. The full reclaim set (PRIVATESIZE|CLONEID|EXT_FLAGS|CLONE_REFCNT) costs +233% sys (9.8 vs 2.9 s), so it stays selection-only. Clone dedup in the map is NOT implemented: ARCHITECTURE s4 and this task's acceptance total (2,368,040,960) keep clones at full size, and reclaimable() already counts them exactly. If the architect wants it, it is ScanOptions.countsClonesOnce: request CLONEID+EXT_FLAGS in the first pass and charge a group to its smallest path, the same code path as hard links (about 30 lines).

comments.author: review-cleaner-catalog-2
comments.text: From the T-0045 review, round 2, item 2: the Cleaner's 10-minute and minimum-age checks use ItemMeasurement.newestModification. MeasureSink.add (feat/scan-engine, MeasureSink.swift:26-31) reads only file mtimes: it skips directories and ignores ctime. Tools backdate mtime. Homebrew runs curl --remote-time (Library/Homebrew/utils/curl.rb:341), and on this Mac a bottle downloaded today at 09:41 has mtime 2026-05-28 and ctime 09:41. tar and unzip restore archive times as well. Renames and deletes inside a folder change only the directory's times. Request: newestModification = max(st_mtime, st_ctime) over every entry, directories included. ctime cannot be set from user space. Failing probe: scratchpad/review-cleaner-catalog-2/wt/Tests/CleanerTests/ReviewProbeTests.swift probe3 (placeholder engine). The same test applies once your engine merges.

comments.author: fix-scan-engine
comments.text:
Fix round 1, commit 4131bda on feat/scan-engine. swift build + swift test green (42 tests). Env-gated BenchFixtureTests: 20/20 exact at 2,368,040,960 B. MACONTROL_FD_PRESSURE=1 DescriptorPressureTests: green 3 runs in a row. Every new test was mutation-checked in a scratch copy: 5 reverts in one build (each named test failed), then the reviewer's mayShareBlocks rule in a second build.
1 HIGH fixed. Raw attributes (C probe): a compressed clone pair reports EXT_FLAGS 0x41 and CLONE_REFCNT 0. After the clone is deleted, the original drops to 0x1 (MAY_SHARE_BLOCKS stays). So the rule keys on EF_SHARES_ALL_BLOCKS, not MAY_SHARE: compressed && sharesAllBlocks -> sharedElsewhere, promise 0. The suggested mayShareBlocks rule would under-promise every compressed file that was ever cloned. Test ReclaimTests.cloneOfACompressedFileFreesNothing: the clone alone frees 0, and once the clone is gone the file frees its ALLOCSIZE. Ceiling (ponytail comment): two selected clones of one compressed file also promise 0, because nothing reports the member count.
2 MEDIUM fixed. ScanTree.removeSubtree collects the owner links in the removed subtree and hands each inode's bytes to the surviving link with the smallest path (the finalizeTotals rule), adding them back to its ancestors. It makes one pass over all nodes, and only when an owner leaves. Test ScanTreeTests.removingTheChargedLinkMovesItsBytesToTheNextLink: 3 links; remove the owner's folder, then a 0 B link, then the last link -> 0. The Disk Map gets this through removeSubtree with no change.
3 MEDIUM fixed. FolderWalk.openWaiting is now the single EMFILE/ENFILE wait (spill our own idle descriptors, else wait, up to 5 s). First opens and every step of reopen use it. reopen pins its anchor while the lock is released, and pinDescriptor drops its descriptor if another worker reopened the same folder meanwhile. The soft RLIMIT_NOFILE is raised once to min(hard, OPEN_MAX), and each walk takes soft/4 (at most 1024), per F-0060. No cross-walk semaphore: the raise leaves room for about 10 walks of 1024 each, and running out only costs waiting. Test DescriptorPressureTests.concurrentWalksOverTheProcessLimitStayExact is env-gated because it lowers the process limit: 5 concurrent measures, 12 workers x budget 48 each, soft limit 96, 3 rounds. It fails 3/3 with the old reopen and passes with the fix.
4 MEDIUM fixed in the engine. DataVolumeLayout.forStartupDisk treats both "/" and /System/Volumes/Data as the startup disk; the tree root is then URL "/" with the identity of "/". The app shell can keep passing /System/Volumes/Data. Test TreeSinkTests.dataVolumeAndSlashAreBothTheStartupDisk.
5 LOW, doc only. The clone-group ceiling stays, because no attribute answers it. The UI should word such selections as "frees about/up to X". Architect: please record the limit in ARCHITECTURE s4 (not my path).
6 LOW fixed. Selection.readFiles marks the estimate incomplete when a selected name is missing from its parent's listing. Test ReclaimTests.selectionSpelledInAnotherCaseIsALowerBound.
7 LOW not changed. Those nodes are SF_RESTRICTED, so they already carry .systemProtected and are never offered for deletion. Moving Data-side partial prefixes under /System/Volumes/Data needs a deeper firmlink split, left for a later pass.
8 LOW. (b) fixed: stopDatalessMaterialization() now runs on the scan, measure/reclaimable and walker threads (no test: a dataless item needs a File Provider). (a) The worker policy (1.5x cores, cap 12) still needs the architect's sign-off; the evidence is in the 12:06 comment. (c) No devid check: DIR_MNTSTATUS already marks every mount point, and firmlinks do not change devid.
9 LOW not changed (optional): a cancelled measure on a hung mount, and Listing capacity.

comments.author: fix-scan-engine
comments.text:

tasks.title: Safety: protected-path policy, Move to Trash with identity checks, undo journal
tasks.description:
**Goal:** the one door for file mutation: protected-path policy, Move to Trash with identity checks, undo journal (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 5). Also covers the journal/undo half of T-0026.

**Owned paths:** `Sources/Safety/`, `Tests/SafetyTests/` (keep `SinkAuditTests` passing and strict).

**Build**
1. `ProtectedPaths.refusal(for:)`: canonical path via `fcntl(F_GETPATH)` on the parent folder + leaf name (catches `/System/Volumes/Data/...` spellings and symlinked parents). Containment rules: refuse if the item equals or contains a protected root; refuse if it lies inside a never-touch area (full lists in the doc). `SF_RESTRICTED` / read-only volume -> `.systemProtected`; `UF_IMMUTABLE`/uchg -> `.locked`; iCloud Drive and `~/Library/CloudStorage` -> `.needsCloudConfirmation` unless confirmed; not writable by the user -> `.needsAdministrator`. Seed lists may adapt Homebrew `UNDELETABLE_PATHS` (BSD-2) and PureMac `ProviderPaths`/`FileProtection` (MIT) with notice.
2. `TrashService.moveToTrash`: per item re-`lstat` and compare `expectedIdentity`; policy; expand `keep` (trash the children that do not contain a kept path, recursively); drop items inside other selected items; in-process `FileManager.trashItem(at:resultingItemURL:)`; append a journal line after each success; per-item outcomes; continue past a refused item. Never clear flags, chmod, chown, shell out or delete permanently.
3. Journal: JSON Lines, file 0600 in a 0700 folder, entries per `JournalEntry`. `history()` reads it; `undo(batch:)` moves each item back with its own move only when the original path is free, and records the restore.
4. Injectable trash backend (e.g. an internal init parameter) so tests move into a temp "Trash" folder. Tests must never call the real `trashItem` on anything outside a temp folder they created (an env-gated test may use a disk image mounted inside the temp folder).

**Acceptance**
- Tests for every refusal: `/`, home, `~/Library`, home spelled via `/System/Volumes/Data`, a symlinked parent pointing into a protected area, `..` segments, Keychains child, locked file (flag still set afterwards), identity swap between scan and trash, cloud folder without confirmation.
- keep-descendant test (the kept file survives, siblings trashed), ancestor+descendant selection trashes once, journal mode 0600, undo restores bytes and identity, undo refuses when the original path is occupied.
- Deliberate-bug proof for the policy posted in a task comment (break one rule, show the failing test).
- Findings to close with test names: F-0002, F-0012, F-0018, F-0024, F-0026, F-0036, F-0039, F-0050, F-0053, F-0064, F-0070.

**Read:** research/reports/topic-platform-constraints.md (D1-D7, implications 4-6), sources/colinvkim-radix.md (Deletion), sources/tw93-mole.md (deletion gate rows), sources/momenbasel-puremac.md (reuse rows), sources/homebrew-brew.md, sources/ggbond268-mactools.md (StagingJournal @9197035, Apache).

---
**Rules for every builder.** Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (your section plus 2, 5, 10, 11). Stay inside your owned paths; `Package.swift`, `Tests/TestSupport/`, `MacontrolCore/FileIdentity.swift` and `ByteFormatting.swift` are frozen (ask the architect by comment). Public signatures in your module are contracts: additions are free, breaking changes need a comment on the consumer tasks first. Tests build fixtures only in `TemporaryDirectory` and never delete, move or trash anything outside it. No `rm -rf`, no shell strings with paths; destructive calls live only in `Sources/Safety` (SinkAuditTests enforces it). Swift 6, strict concurrency clean, small files, comments only for non-obvious whys. Adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code gets a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry in the same commit; GPL, Commons Clause and unlicensed sources are study only. `swift build && swift test` green before every commit; one build at a time (the machine is slow). When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: fix-safety-trash
comments.text:
Review round 1 resolved on feat/safety-trash @ 31fc928 (fix-safety-trash). swift build + swift test green (38 tests in 9 suites); with MACONTROL_DISK_IMAGE_TESTS=1 the disk-image test runs too. No macontrol-tests-* folders are left behind.
1. [high] TrashBatch keep failed open. Fixed. If any keep URL cannot be made canonical, the whole item comes back .failed ("An item you chose to keep could not be checked, so nothing here was moved.") and nothing reaches the backend. Keep paths and child paths are compared lowercased, as ProtectionPolicy does. A keep equal to the item itself also moves nothing. Tests: TrashServiceTests.keepSurvivesWhenItsFolderCannotBeOpened, keepSurvivesWhenTheItemIsSpelledInAnotherCase (the kept file stays, build.log is trashed). F-0026 re-marked.
2. [high] A folder that contains a mount point passed the policy. Fixed. ProtectionPolicy.refusal reads getfsstat(MNT_NOWAIT) on each check and returns .protectedLocation(<mount>) when any f_mntonname starts with canonical + "/", lowercased. If the mount table cannot be read, the item is refused. The st_dev check for the mount point itself stays. I checked that the kernel reports f_mntonname in the same form F_GETPATH gives: a mount made through /tmp/... or /System/Volumes/Data/private/... is listed as /private/.... Test: ProtectedPathsTests.refusesAFolderThatContainsAMountPoint. It is env-gated (MACONTROL_DISK_IMAGE_TESTS=1), creates and attaches a 20 MB APFS image at <temp>/home/Projects/mnt, checks the mount, Projects and PROJECTS, and detaches in a defer.
3. [low] trashedAncestor started at the parent. Fixed. It checks trashed[path] first, and keys are lowercased. Test: TrashServiceTests.aDuplicateSelectionIsReportedAsTrashed (file, file, and FILE spelled in upper case: all three report the same destination, and the backend is called once).
4. [low] A path past PATH_MAX came back .missing. Fixed. ProtectedPaths.unreachable maps EACCES, EPERM and ENAMETOOLONG to .needsAdministrator (Reveal in Finder) in canonicalPath and in both lstat calls. I added no new enum case, so the UI switches keep compiling. Test: ProtectedPathsTests.aDeepItemIsNotReportedMissing. It builds 20 levels with mkdirat, then cuts the chain with renameat, so the temporary folder can clean it up.
5. [low] The policy was rebuilt on every public call. Fixed. There is a static policy for the default home, and other homes still build their own. Measured with 2000 default-home calls in a debug build: 0.40 s, down from 2.69 s. What is left is syscalls. There is no timing test, because one would be flaky on this machine.
6. [low] A vanished child got no outcome, and an item with everything kept returned []. Fixed. A vanished child now reports .refused(child, .missing). When no piece was trashed and no outcome names the item, the item gets .failed(item.url, "Nothing in it was moved: everything left in it is kept or refused."). Test: TrashServiceTests.anItemWithNothingLeftToMoveReportsItself. The .missing branch for a vanished child only happens in a race, so it has no deterministic test.
7. [low] The sink audit did not cover several C calls. Fixed. SinkAuditTests now matches removefile, copyfile, posix_spawn(p), popen, exec[lv]p?e? and system as whole-word calls. The regex skips a call preceded by "." or a word character, so `.font(.system(size:))` in the UI branches does not trip it. SafetySinkTests.forbidden adds the same tokens. Self-check: SinkAuditTests.cCallsAreFoundAsWholeWords.
Extra, not raised in the review: I restored RefusalReason.notImplemented. The builder removed it, but feat/disk-map (DiskMapText, DiskMapModel+Trash) and feat/clean-uninstall-ui (TrashOutcome+Words, CleanModel, UninstallModel) switch over it or return it. Without it, the merge would not compile. TrashService never returns it.
Deliberate-bug proof (targeted mutations, `swift test --filter SafetyTests` with the disk-image test on, each reverted with git checkout, tree clean afterwards). Every mutation turned the suite red:
N1 keep via compactMap try? -> keepSurvivesWhenItsFolderCannotBeOpened
N2 case-sensitive child match -> keepSurvivesWhenTheItemIsSpelledInAnotherCase, keepsUncheckedDescendants, anItemWithNothingLeftToMoveReportsItself
N3 no mount table check -> refusesAFolderThatContainsAMountPoint
N4 ancestor lookup starts at parent -> aDuplicateSelectionIsReportedAsTrashed
N5 ENAMETOOLONG treated as missing -> aDeepItemIsNotReportedMissing
N6 no outcome for the item when nothing moved -> anItemWithNothingLeftToMoveReportsItself

request_changes: 1 high, 4 medium, 3 low. swift build + swift test in the worktree @ 31fc928: green, 38 tests. The repros are 7 tests in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-egeb-projects/45c9d2a4-ec2b-4761-8ad2-c890faaddc58/scratchpad/review-safety-trash-2/pkg/Tests/SafetyTests/ReviewSafety2Tests.swift, run in a git-archive export (MACONTROL_DISK_IMAGE_TESTS=1). All 7 fail on 31fc928. Each move goes through TrashFixture's temp-only backend. The builder's worktree was not touched, and no mounts or macontrol-tests-* folders are left behind. Verified and OK: the real FileManager.trashItem moves a leaf symlink (relative, absolute, or pointing to a folder), not its target. It keeps the on-disk name when the path uses another case. I checked both with trashItem on a disk image mounted in the scratchpad, whose items go to that image's own .Trashes.
1. HIGH, safety: the iCloud Drive root and cloud provider domain roots can be trashed. ProtectionPolicy puts only "Library/Mobile Documents" and "Library/CloudStorage" in the roots. So with cloudConfirmed, ~/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs (all of iCloud Drive), each Mobile Documents/<app container> and each ~/Library/CloudStorage/<domain> pass the policy. feat/disk-map already ships the cloudConfirmed toggle (ReviewSheet.swift:48). On any iCloud Mac, com~apple~CloudDocs is one of the largest nodes the map shows, and its name does not say what it is. One toggle then deletes the whole drive on every device. ~/Documents is refused outright. Repro: cloudProviderRootsAreRefusedEvenWhenConfirmed (both roots -> nil). Fix: make every direct child of Library/Mobile Documents and Library/CloudStorage a protected root, so its contents need confirmation but the root never goes. Unverified: whether FileProvider itself would refuse the rename. This Mac has no iCloud account, so I could not check, and the policy must not rely on it.
2. MEDIUM, safety (the F-0026 guard is missing): keep holds only inside its own TrashItem. (a) [old keep:[old/src/notes.md], old/src]: old is pieced out, then old/src is not inside anything trashed, so it goes whole with notes.md. (b) [old, old/src keep:[notes.md]]: old goes first and takes notes.md, and old/src is reported as trashed through it. F-0026's "after" says a deselection always wins, and the planner refuses when a deselected path is under any planned deletion. No consumer passes keep yet, so nothing can hit this today. Repros: keepHoldsAgainstASeparatelySelectedDescendant, keepHoldsAgainstASelectedAncestor. Fix: canonicalize the keep of every item once per batch into one set, failing closed as now. Pass that set to every item's pieces, and do it before the trashedAncestor shortcut.
3. MEDIUM, safety: .Spotlight-V100, .fseventsd and .DocumentRevisions-V100 are protected only at "/". On any other volume the policy allows them. External drives usually ignore ownership, so canMove passes. A disk map of an external drive shows .Spotlight-V100 as a big block, and .DocumentRevisions-V100 holds the user's document versions. Repro (env-gated, APFS image): volumeSystemFoldersAreRefusedOnEveryVolume (all three -> nil). Fix: add them to neverTouchNames, as .Trashes already is, or match them at every mount root.
4. MEDIUM, one-door enforcement: SinkAuditTests misses `Process.run(`, `Process.launchedProcess(`, `Process.init()` and `let p: Process = .init()`. It also misses Finder scripting other than NSAppleScript: OSAScript, NSUserAppleScriptTask, SBApplication (F-0018). Repro: I planted Sources/Cleaner/ZZReviewPlant.swift with `_ = try Process.run(URL(fileURLWithPath: "/usr/bin/true"), arguments: [])` in a function that is never called, and destructiveCallsLiveOnlyInSafety still passed. No branch has an offender today (I grepped all 8). Fix: match `\bProcess\b` (except in Uninstaller/Launchd*), and add OSAScript, NSUserAppleScriptTask and SBApplication. Pin each with a positive/negative sample, the way cCallsAreFoundAsWholeWords does.
5. MEDIUM, undo: nothing protects the undo journal's own folder. Trashing ~/Library/Application Support/Macontrol, or a leftover rule that matches it, moves the journal to the Trash. The open handle keeps writing into the moved file, and history() and undo() lose every earlier batch. Repro: trashingTheJournalFolderKeepsEarlierUndo (the second batch is not refused, and undo of the first returns []). Fix: refuse journalURL's folder and its ancestors up to home in TrashService.
6. LOW: undo renames the file. The journal's originalPath keeps the caller's spelling of the leaf (canonicalPath resolves only the parent). Trashing Downloads/REPORT.PDF for report.pdf and then undoing leaves REPORT.PDF on disk. The real trashItem keeps report.pdf in the Trash, so only undo renames. Repro: undoPutsTheItemBackUnderItsOnDiskName. Fix: record the on-disk leaf name, from F_GETPATH on the item itself or from getattrlist ATTR_CMN_NAME.
7. LOW: trashedAncestor and keep compare lowercased paths. That fails safe for keep and for the policy, but on a case-sensitive volume, [Cache, cache/b.bin] reports cache/b.bin as .trashed (to Trash/Cache/b.bin) while it stays on disk. The disk map would then drop the node and count its space as freed. Repro (env-gated, Case-sensitive APFS image): onACaseSensitiveVolumeAnotherFolderIsNotReportedAsTrashed. Fix: dedupe by FileIdentity, or check pathconf(_PC_CASE_SENSITIVE).
8. LOW, hardening: undo's renamex_np follows a symlink that has replaced a component of originalPath since the trash, so the item is put back somewhere else. RENAME_EXCL still stops any overwrite. RENAME_NOFOLLOW_ANY (0x10, sys/stdio.h) closes this. Not a blocker: THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES still lacks the Homebrew/PureMac entries, which are routed to T-0003. Performance note: mountPoint(inside:) zeroes about 39 KB of statfs and makes 2 getfsstat calls per item and per keep piece. That is fine now; cache the list per batch if big keep expansions get slow.

tasks.title: Cleaner: validated cleanup catalog, in-use guard, junk scan
tasks.description:
**Goal:** a safe, data-driven junk catalog and scanner (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 6).

**Owned paths:** `Sources/Cleaner/` (incl. `Resources/catalog.json`), `Tests/CleanerTests/`.

**Build**
1. Rule validator, fail closed at load (invalid rules dropped and reported) and enforced by a test over the bundled catalog: patterns start with `~/` or an allowlisted absolute root, no `..`, `*` only in the last component, at least three levels below home, never inside Documents/Desktop/Downloads/Music/Pictures/Movies, `/Users/Shared`, `~/Library/Mobile Documents`, `~/Library/CloudStorage` or FileProvider/`com~apple~` paths.
2. v1 catalog with a `note` per rule: user app caches, logs (>= 7 days), browser caches only (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Brave, Arc cache folders, never profiles), Xcode DerivedData (safe), iOS DeviceSupport (review), CoreSimulator caches (not Devices), SwiftPM/CocoaPods/Carthage caches, npm `_cacache`, yarn cache, pip cache, Homebrew download cache, Go build cache (safe); pnpm store, Gradle, Maven, Cargo registry (review); iOS backups, Xcode Archives, `macOS Install Data` (manual). Data taken from PureMac/mac-cleanup-sh/Kudu/Mac Sai/kondo gets a THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES entry; Mole/MangoDisk are a checklist only.
3. In-use guard: skip with a reason when a running app's bundle id, bundle name or executable name equals the item's name (inject the running-app list so tests can fake it), or when `newestModification` is under 10 minutes old; apply `minimumAgeDays` per item.
4. Measure matches concurrently (bounded, about 4 at once) through `ScanEngine.measure`; no wall-clock limit that makes big items uncleanable.
5. Keep `CleanupItem` / `isPreselected` / `trashItem` as the UI contract. Phase 2 only if phase 1 is accepted: project artifacts (node_modules, target, .build) in user-chosen roots, verified by marker files, never under ~/Library.

**Acceptance**
- Validator tests reject `${HOME}/x`, `/`, `~/Library/*`, `~/Documents/*`, `~/Library/Caches/../..`, `~/Library/Caches/*/x*y/*`; the bundled catalog passes.
- Guard tests: running-app match and a recently written file are skipped with reasons; old files pass.
- Scanner tests only against a `TemporaryDirectory` home.
- Findings to close with test names: F-0015, F-0021, F-0025, F-0027, F-0032, F-0033 (pnpm store is review, no ~/Library artifacts), F-0065.

**Read:** sources/momenbasel-puremac.md, sources/tw93-mole.md, sources/mac-cleanup-mac-cleanup-py.md, sources/adventdevinc-kudu.md, sources/iliyami-macsai.md, sources/tbillington-kondo.md, sources/ggbond268-mactools.md, sources/tencent-lemon-cleaner.md.

---
**Rules for every builder.** Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (your section plus 2, 5, 10, 11). Stay inside your owned paths; `Package.swift`, `Tests/TestSupport/`, `MacontrolCore/FileIdentity.swift` and `ByteFormatting.swift` are frozen (ask the architect by comment). Public signatures in your module are contracts: additions are free, breaking changes need a comment on the consumer tasks first. Tests build fixtures only in `TemporaryDirectory` and never delete, move or trash anything outside it. No `rm -rf`, no shell strings with paths; destructive calls live only in `Sources/Safety` (SinkAuditTests enforces it). Swift 6, strict concurrency clean, small files, comments only for non-obvious whys. Adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code gets a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry in the same commit; GPL, Commons Clause and unlicensed sources are study only. `swift build && swift test` green before every commit; one build at a time (the machine is slow). When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: build-scan-engine
comments.text:
Scan engine (T-0043, branch feat/scan-engine) changed contracts additively; nothing you call was removed or renamed.
- ScanTree: finalizeTotals() now charges each hard-linked inode to the link with the smallest path and marks the others .sharedHardLink at 0 B; callers only set .hardLinked. New: addChild(of:nameBytes:...), relativePathBytes(of:) (byte-exact path, use it for identity-stable keys), storageBytes, bytesPerNode. name(of:) decodes the stored bytes.
- ScanOptions(workerCount:descriptorBudget:) - both optional.
- ReclaimEstimate(freesNow:sharedElsewhere:isIncomplete:) - isIncomplete defaults to false; true when part of the selection could not be read, so show the figure as 'at least'.
- ScanError.notADirectory(URL) is public; scan() of a missing path throws POSIXError.
- scan(URL('/')) walks /System/Volumes/Data once: firmlinked entries at '/Users', '/Applications', ..., Data-only folders (macOS Install Data, .Spotlight-V100) under a real '/System/Volumes/Data' node. Every url(of:) in the tree exists.
- Flags you will see: .unreadable/.incomplete (lower bound, show 'not scanned'), .mountPoint (leaf, 0 B), .dataless (0 B local), .package (sized in full), .compressed, .systemProtected (SF_RESTRICTED).

ProcessSnapshot no longer fails open: a process whose fd listing fails while it still exists (errno != ESRCH) goes to ProcessSnapshot.uninspected, and the guard then skips every item with 'Could not check which files <name> has open'. A process that exited meanwhile holds nothing and is ignored. DerivedData declares Xcode and xcodebuild. The browsers declare their bundle id and app name, and so on. tasks.verdictNotes:
approve (no critical or high issue left). Round 2 checked commit 31e540b. swift build is clean with no warnings (a fresh build of a git-archive copy). swift test passed 54/54 in the worktree. Failing probes: scratchpad/review-cleaner-catalog-2/wt/Tests/CleanerTests/ReviewProbeTests.swift, run with `swift test --filter ReviewProbeTests`. All 6 fail as described below, and the control in probe4 passes. A read-only live run on this Mac (matcher and guard only, no measure, no trash) gave sensible verdicts: 96 matches, 0 uninspected processes, and every running app's cache was skipped with a reason.
Items 1-4 are MEDIUM. None of them loses user data, because the worst outcome is a cache trashed under a running tool. They are small, though, and they sit in this module's own F-0015 and F-0032 promises. Please take them in a follow-up before release.
1. [MEDIUM, F-0015] Declared owners that are scripts never match. ProcessSnapshot.runningApp (ProcessSnapshot.swift:64-75) names a process after proc_pidpath, and for a `#!` script that is the interpreter. On this Mac npm and pnpm are `#!/usr/bin/env node`, pip3 is `#!.../python3.14`, and pod and brew are `#!/bin/bash`. yarn, gradle and mvn are scripts as well. So the owners of npm-cache, pnpm-store, pip-cache, cocoapods-cache, homebrew-downloads, yarn-cache, gradle-caches and maven-repository never fire. probe2 runs a `#!/bin/sh` script named npm, and the guard returns nil for the bundled npm-cache rule. Fix: for each process, also read argv with sysctl KERN_PROCARGS2 and match owners against the basenames of its script arguments (npm-cli.js runs as `node /opt/homebrew/bin/npm`). Otherwise remove the dead owners. Add a live test with a real script.
2. [MEDIUM, F-0015, with T-0043] The 10-minute and minimumAgeDays checks read file mtimes only. The placeholder in ScanEngine.swift:152-156 and feat/scan-engine MeasureSink.swift:26-31 both skip directories and ignore ctime. Tools backdate mtime. Homebrew downloads with `curl --remote-time` (Library/Homebrew/utils/curl.rb:341), and on this Mac a bottle downloaded today at 09:41 has mtime 2026-05-28. tar and unzip restore archive times, which affects CocoaPods, cargo and SwiftPM artifacts. Renames and deletes inside an item change only the directory's times. In probe3, a bottle written a few seconds ago with a backdated mtime is preselected by the bundled homebrew-downloads rule. Combined with item 1, a running `brew install` or `pod install` is protected only by the open-fd check. Fix: newestModification = max(mtime, ctime) over files and directories. I commented this on T-0043.
3. [MEDIUM, F-0015] ProcessSnapshot still fails open. ProcessSnapshot.swift:49 does `guard let executable = executablePath(of: pid) else { continue }`, so when proc_pidpath fails the process is dropped completely: it gets no name, no open files, and is not counted as uninspected. proc_pidpath fails with ENOENT for a live process whose binary was unlinked. `brew cleanup` after `brew upgrade` does this, as does emptying the Trash under a running app. The fd list stays readable in that case (verified with libproc: pidpath returns 0 with errno 2, while PROC_PIDLISTFDS still returns 360). probe4: the control gives 'In use by holder'. After the running binary is unlinked, the same open cache comes back preselected. Fix: skip only on ESRCH. Otherwise keep the process, name it with proc_name, and still list its fds.
4. [MEDIUM, F-0032/F-0027] The allowlist roots are whole trees, so data that must never be touched still validates. These all pass: ~/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator/Devices/*, ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/UserData/*, ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/*, ~/Library/Developer/Toolchains/*, ~/.cargo/bin/* and ~/.gradle/init.d/*. ~/Library/Developer/Xcode/Archives/* passes as safe too (manualOnlyRoots covers only the backups and Install Data). probe1: a safe rule `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/*` preselects UserData (the user's snippets). CatalogTests only catches Devices, by substring, and Archives, by rule id. Fix: allowlist the exact subtrees the catalog uses (Xcode/DerivedData, Xcode/*DeviceSupport, CoreSimulator/Caches, .cargo/registry, .gradle/caches, .m2/repository, .npm/_cacache) and add Xcode/Archives to manualOnlyRoots.
5. [LOW, UX] Our own process is part of the snapshot. userProcessIDs() includes getpid(), and fileHeldOpenByARunningProcessIsSkipped depends on that. A disk-map scan running in the same app holds directory fds inside caches, so random items show 'In use by Macontrol'. Fix: exclude getpid() and hold the file in a child process in that test.
6. [LOW, UX] `*` matches dotfiles (CatalogMatcher.swift:43 has no FNM_PERIOD, which F-0025's 'how' names). On this Mac the live run offers ~/Library/pnpm/store/.DS_Store, ~/.gradle/caches/.DS_Store and ~/.gradle/caches/CACHEDIR.TAG as cleanup items. Fix: add FNM_PERIOD.
7. [LOW, after T-0044 merges] build-safety-trash's 12:01 comment is still open. Caches the trash policy refuses (CloudKit, com.apple.bird, com.apple.cloudd, com.apple.FileProvider, ...) are listed as tickable items and only fail at trash time; the live run lists ~/Library/Caches/CloudKit. Set the skip reason from ProtectedPaths.refusal(for:) at scan time. The `allocated:` one-liner in trashItem is also still pending.
8. [LOW, perf] InUseGuard.swift:43 builds `path + "/"` inside first(where:), which is one String allocation per open file per item (1155 open files under home here). Build the prefix once per item.
9. [NOTE, T-0049] feat/clean-uninstall-ui CleanModel.swift:168 still sends pending.items.map(\.trashItem) without calling Cleaner.recheck, so the delete-time half of F-0015 exists only after T-0049 wires it in. Check this at integration.
Positives: rules are fail-closed and dropped whole; the manual-only roots are enforced by the validator; the case-insensitive overlap handling is correct, and so is the n log n containment check; recheck fails closed ('Could not be checked again' / 'No longer there') and keeps the scan identity; the owner state has 3 values, with GIPPseudonymousID never preselected; the open-file path spelling matches what libproc returns (/Users, never /System/Volumes/Data); the code builds with no warnings under strict concurrency; and there is no shell and no destructive call in Sources/Cleaner.

tasks.title: Uninstaller: app inventory, evidence-scored leftovers, safe uninstall order
tasks.description:
**Goal:** list apps, find leftovers by evidence, uninstall in a safe order (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 7).

**Owned paths:** `Sources/Uninstaller/` (a `Launchd*.swift` file is the only place `Process` may be used, with an argument array), `Tests/UninstallerTests/`.

**Build**
1. `installedApps()`: `/Applications` (+ one level of subfolders), `~/Applications`, `/System/Applications` (+ Utilities). Kind: `builtIn` (read-only/sealed volume, `SF_RESTRICTED` or `/System`), `appleAppStore` (`Contents/_MASReceipt` and an Apple signature via `SecStaticCode`), else `thirdParty`. Sizes are lazy (`plan`).
2. `plan(for:)` with evidence: preselected = bundle-id-named items in Caches, Application Support, Preferences (+ ByHost `<id>.*.plist`), Containers (confirm via `.com.apple.containermanagerd.metadata.plist` `MCMMetadataIdentifier`), Saved Application State, HTTPStorages (+ `.binarycookies`), WebKit, Logs, Application Scripts; group containers listed in the app's `application-groups` entitlement; user LaunchAgents whose Program/ProgramArguments points into the bundle. Not preselected = folders whose name equals the app/executable name (case-insensitive equality, never substring). Never search Documents/Desktop/Downloads/Music/Pictures/Movies/iCloud/`/Users/Shared`. Vendor folders: only the app's own subfolder. An item another installed app also uses gets a note and is not preselected. `/Library` items -> `needsAdministrator`. pkg receipts (`/var/db/receipts`) -> blocker/note text only.
3. `uninstall(plan, leftovers:)`: quit (`NSRunningApplication.terminate`, wait up to 10 s, stop if still running; no pattern kill), `launchctl bootout gui/<uid> <plist>` per user agent being removed, exact labels only (inject the launchctl runner so tests never run it), then one `TrashService.moveToTrash` batch with the bundle and chosen leftovers. Stop on the first failed step. Trash exactly what the plan showed.
4. Apple App Store apps: bundle removable (usually `needsAdministrator` in v1 because root-owned); content libraries (`/Library/Application Support/GarageBand`, `/Library/Audio/Apple Loops`, Logic) listed as admin-only leftovers. Built-in apps: `blocker` text, never trashed.
5. Phase 2: a test-only oracle from ~20 popular casks' zap lists (BSD-2, notice) measuring matcher recall; the dataset is not shipped.

**Acceptance**
- Fixture tests (temp home + temp Applications): "Sketchbook" does not match `~/Documents/Sketchbook Drawings.psd` or `Docs/Work/sketchbook-notes.txt`; two apps in one vendor folder (LuLu/BlockBlock) leave the sibling untouched; container metadata attribution; exact-name item unselected; built-in app blocked; bootout called with the exact label before trashing; a failing quit stops everything; the items passed to TrashService equal the preview.
- Findings to close with test names: F-0011, F-0022, F-0023, F-0030, F-0066, F-0067, F-0069, F-0072 (agents pointing into the bundle are listed).

**Read:** sources/alienator88-pearcleaner.md (study only, Commons Clause), sources/momenbasel-puremac.md (Pearcleaner-derived files are study only), sources/homebrew-homebrew-cask.md, sources/homebrew-brew.md, sources/munki-munki.md, sources/objective-see-knockknock.md, sources/tw93-mole.md (uninstall rows), topic-platform-constraints.md (summary 1, implications 3 and 7).

---
**Rules for every builder.** Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (your section plus 2, 5, 10, 11). Stay inside your owned paths; `Package.swift`, `Tests/TestSupport/`, `MacontrolCore/FileIdentity.swift` and `ByteFormatting.swift` are frozen (ask the architect by comment). Public signatures in your module are contracts: additions are free, breaking changes need a comment on the consumer tasks first. Tests build fixtures only in `TemporaryDirectory` and never delete, move or trash anything outside it. No `rm -rf`, no shell strings with paths; destructive calls live only in `Sources/Safety` (SinkAuditTests enforces it). Swift 6, strict concurrency clean, small files, comments only for non-obvious whys. Adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code gets a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry in the same commit; GPL, Commons Clause and unlicensed sources are study only. `swift build && swift test` green before every commit; one build at a time (the machine is slow). When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: build-safety-trash
comments.text: Safety (T-0044, feat/safety-trash) now really trashes. Contract changes, all additive except one: (1) TrashService(journalURL:backend:home:) — tests that call Uninstaller.uninstall must pass a backend that moves into their own temp folder (copy Tests/SafetyTests/TrashFixture.swift's backend) and never use the default .finder backend; (2) TrashItem(url:expectedIdentity:keep:allocated:) — pass the leftover's measured allocated size so History shows it; (3) RefusalReason: Error, and the scaffold case .notImplemented is gone (nobody referenced it). Items in one call are processed shallowest-first; a selected item inside another selected item is reported trashed via its ancestor (one journal line). Outcomes come back in input order; compare URLs by .path (folder URLs gain a trailing slash). Root-owned bundles (Xcode.app, Cloudflare WARP.app on this Mac) come back .needsAdministrator; /Applications/Safari.app .systemProtected.

comments.author: build-scan-engine
comments.text:
Scan engine (T-0043, branch feat/scan-engine) changed contracts additively; nothing you call was removed or renamed.
- ScanTree: finalizeTotals() now charges each hard-linked inode to the link with the smallest path and marks the others .sharedHardLink at 0 B; callers only set .hardLinked. New: addChild(of:nameBytes:...), relativePathBytes(of:) (byte-exact path, use it for identity-stable keys), storageBytes, bytesPerNode. name(of:) decodes the stored bytes.
- ScanOptions(workerCount:descriptorBudget:) - both optional.
- ReclaimEstimate(freesNow:sharedElsewhere:isIncomplete:) - isIncomplete defaults to false; true when part of the selection could not be read, so show the figure as 'at least'.
- ScanError.notADirectory(URL) is public; scan() of a missing path throws POSIXError.
- scan(URL('/')) walks /System/Volumes/Data once: firmlinked entries at '/Users', '/Applications', ..., Data-only folders (macOS Install Data, .Spotlight-V100) under a real '/System/Volumes/Data' node. Every url(of:) in the tree exists.
- Flags you will see: .unreadable/.incomplete (lower bound, show 'not scanned'), .mountPoint (leaf, 0 B), .dataless (0 B local), .package (sized in full), .compressed, .systemProtected (SF_RESTRICTED).

comments.author: fix-uninstaller
comments.text:
Review round 1 resolved in c6677c2 on feat/uninstaller. swift build + swift test green (40 tests, no warnings). Every new test was shown to fail on the old behaviour: two mutation passes, each reverting 4-5 fixes at once with the symbols kept. Pass A failed exactly malformedAppGroup, groupSharedWithABuiltIn, singleWordIdentifier, stopsJobs+appRelaunched and itemWithoutARecordedIdentity. Pass B failed exactly groupContainerNeedsItsOwnMetadata, agentAssociated, leftoverOutsideALibraryFolder and onlyThisBundle. Script: scratchpad/fix-uninstaller/mutate.py.
1 CRITICAL app groups: fixed. groupContainers() now keeps only plain names: not "", ".", "..", and no "/" or NUL. A Group Containers folder counts only when its .com.apple.containermanagerd.metadata.plist MCMMetadataIdentifier equals the group; on this Mac 111 of 111 group containers match. Application Scripts/<group> folders have no metadata here, so the name check guards them. Backstop: uninstall() refuses any chosen leftover whose standardized path is not at least 2 levels inside home/Library or systemRoot/Library, throwing .refused(url, .protectedLocation("Outside the Library folders")) before any step. Tests: AppGroupTests.malformedAppGroupNeverNamesAFolderOutsideItsOwnContainer (groups "", ".", "..", "../../Documents", "a/b"), groupContainerNeedsItsOwnMetadata, UninstallFlowTests.leftoverOutsideALibraryFolderIsRefusedBeforeAnyStep (Group Containers/../../Documents, Group Containers, Library).
2 HIGH shared agent: fixed. Every launchd candidate, including the in-bundle and associated branch, gets otherUser(of:): "Also used by X" when another installed app is in AssociatedBundleIdentifiers, else "Starts X" when another app's bundle holds the program. A noted item is not preselected and is not booted out unless the user picks it. Test: LeftoverTests.agentAssociatedWithAnotherInstalledAppIsNotedAndUnselected (MAU-style agent, plus an in-bundle helper associated with Excel).
3 MEDIUM Apple group: fixed. Built-in apps are now in the group rival map. Measured cost, read-only: 94 apps' entitlements take 0.3-0.9 s in total, 0.2-0.3 s of it for /System apps. This is paid only when the planned app has groups, and a ponytail comment marks it. Test: AppGroupTests.groupSharedWithABuiltInAppIsNotPreselected.
4 MEDIUM relaunch: fixed. After the last bootout, uninstall() runs actions.quit again (polite terminate, wait, .stillRunning if still up). Quit stays first. Tests: stopsJobsByExactLabelAfterQuittingAndBeforeTrashing now pins quit, bootouts, quit, trash; appRelaunchedBeforeItsJobsStoppedStopsBeforeTrashing (second quit fails: no trash). F-0023 note updated. ARCHITECTURE section 7 is outside my paths, see the next comment.
5 MEDIUM one-word id: fixed. mainIdentifier is nil unless the id has 2 or more dot components, so claim(), containers, associated jobs and receipts ignore it. The app's own name folders still come through exactNames(), unselected. Test: LeftoverTests.singleWordIdentifierIsNotEvidence (Preferences/Notes.plist and Containers/Notes are gone, Application Support/Notes and Caches/notes are exactName and unselected).
6 LOW quit scope: fixed. RunningApps.isInstance matches this bundle or a helper inside it. It matches by bundle id only for a translocated process (/AppTranslocation/), because Gatekeeper may run this very copy from there. No note is added for a copy running elsewhere, since its shared data is already noted. Test: UninstallFlowTests.onlyThisBundleAndItsHelpersCountAsRunning.
7 LOW nil identity: fixed. checkUnchanged now needs an expected identity, and nil means changedSincePlan. Test: itemWithoutARecordedIdentityCountsAsChanged.
8 LOW rivals outside the app folders: not done. NSWorkspace.urlsForApplications(withBundleIdentifier:) asks this Mac's real Launch Services, so fixture ids (com.jetbrains.*) would make tests depend on what is installed here. It needs an injected lookup. Toolbox's ~/Applications/JetBrains Toolbox is one level deep and already covered. Left for a later round.

comments.author: fix-uninstaller
comments.text: For the architect: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md section 7, lines 168-170 ('Order (Homebrew ORDERED_DIRECTIVES): quit ...; launchctl bootout ...; then one ...') is outside my owned paths, so I have not edited it. It miscites Homebrew: abstract_uninstall.rb:214 says ':launchctl must come before :quit/:signal for cases where app would instantly re-launch'. The implemented order is quit (polite terminate) -> bootout each job by exact label -> quit check again (stillRunning stops everything) -> one Trash batch. Suggested wording: 'quit first (politer than launchd's SIGTERM), boot out each job, then check again for a running copy, because a KeepAlive job can relaunch the app before its bootout; Homebrew puts launchctl before quit for the same reason (abstract_uninstall.rb:214).'

comments.author: fix-uninstaller
comments.text:
Review round 2 resolved in b64a18a + afb0996 on feat/uninstaller. swift build + swift test green (49 tests in the package, 40 in UninstallerTests, no warnings). Leftovers go in a second batch only when the bundle's outcome is .trashed AND its path is empty afterwards (F-0030's "prove it": an updater finishing after the Trash step can put a new copy back). If one Undo matters, a Safety option "stop at the first item not trashed" would bring back one batch (T-0044's call). The bundle, folders and symlinks keep the plan-time identity, and a nil plan identity stays nil, which counts as changedSincePlan. Tests: preferencesRewrittenBeforeAndWhileQuittingAreStillTrashed (atomic rewrite after the plan and again during quit; the trashed item carries the post-quit inode), preferencesReplacedByALinkCountAsChanged. itemReplacedAfterThePlanStopsBeforeAnyStep (folder) still fails closed. The UI's cached-plan drop on changedSincePlan is T-0049's.
3 MEDIUM error text: fixed. UninstallError: LocalizedError, one sentence per case saying what to do ("Demo is still running. Quit it, then try again."). Test: uninstallErrorsReadAsSentences.
4 MEDIUM cancellation: fixed. plan(for:) calls Task.checkCancellation() after installedApps(), before each leftover measure, and before the bundle measure. Test: cancelledPlanStops.
5 LOW group shape: fixed. LeftoverFinder.isAppGroup accepts only `group.` or `<own team ID>.` names with no "/" or NUL. AppBundle.teamIdentifier reads kSecCodeInfoTeamIdentifier. Tests: AppGroupTests.groupThatIsABundleIdNeverTakesThatAppsScripts (ad-hoc app listing com.apple.mail) and appGroupsAreGroupDotOrTheAppsOwnTeam (ad-hoc signing has no team, so the team rule is checked directly). Group fixtures moved from ABCDE12345.* to group.*, and malformed now also covers group.x/../../../Documents.
6 LOW bundle labels: fixed. LaunchdJob.labels(in:of:) keeps a label only when BundleProgram is a relative path without "..", or when Program (else ProgramArguments[0]) lies inside the bundle. runs(inside:) also rejects ".." components now. Test: LeftoverTests.bundleLabelsCountOnlyWhenTheJobRunsTheBundlesOwnProgram (Keystone label, ../../usr/bin/true, Demo.app/../Other.app are all dropped).
7 LOW allocated: not done in this branch, because the scaffold TrashItem has no allocated parameter and the build would break. At the merge with feat/safety-trash, pass allocated: plan.appMeasurement.allocated on the bundle item in uninstall(), and allocated: leftover.measurement.allocated in itemToTrash(for:). That is a two-line change for the integrator.

Mutation proof: pass A failed exactly cancelledPlanStops, groupThatIsABundleId, appGroupsAreGroupDot, malformedAppGroup, lockedBundle, preferencesReplacedByALink and itemReplacedAfterThePlan. Pass B failed bundleLabelsCount, preferencesRewritten and uninstallErrorsReadAsSentences. Pass C, with the empty-path check dropped, failed appThatStaysInstalled(reinstalledAfterTrash: true). tasks.verdictNotes:
Round 2: request_changes (1 HIGH). swift build and swift test are green in the worktree (40 tests, c6677c2). The round-1 fixes hold. I also ran the suites against feat/safety-trash 31fc928's real TrashService (overlay export in the scratchpad): the flow, leftover and group suites pass. Probes: scratchpad/review-uninstaller-2/ReviewRound2ProbeTests.swift, in Tests/UninstallerTests. Probes 1 and 2 need the Safety overlay (TrashBackend). Run: swift test --filter ReviewRound2ProbeTests. All 6 probes fail at c6677c2. Verified OK: `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<missing label>` exits 3, which matches Launchd.notLoaded. Sources/Uninstaller has no destructive sinks. Process is used only in LaunchdControl.swift, with an argument array.

1. HIGH, Uninstaller.swift:95. The bundle and the leftovers go to Safety in one batch, and TrashBatch handles each item on its own. So when the bundle is refused or fails, the leftovers are still trashed: the app stays and its data goes. That is F-0030's own incident. Its "after" says: remove the app first, prove it, and run nothing further if that fails. F-0030 is marked fixed. Probe whenTheBundleStaysNoLeftoverIsTrashed: Sparkle's install-on-quit swaps in a new bundle during quit. Real Safety output: bundle .refused(identityChanged), Caches/com.example.Demo .trashed, Preferences/com.example.Demo.plist .trashed. The same happens on any other bundle failure: an App Management EPERM without FDA (C8, unverified) or a backend error. Fix: trash the bundle alone first and require .trashed before the leftover batch. Or add a Safety option to "stop the batch at the first item not trashed", so there is still one batch and one Undo. At minimum, re-run checkUnchanged on the bundle after the last quit. Reopen F-0030 until then.
2. MEDIUM, Preferences identity. cfprefsd replaces the plist on every write: I measured `defaults write` twice, and the inode went from 98718088 to 98718089. Apps save window frames and settings when they quit. So the identity recorded at plan time no longer matches, Safety refuses the plist, and the app is gone while its preferences stay. Probe preferencesSavedWhileQuittingAreStillTrashed: bundle and Caches trashed, plist .refused(identityChanged). Before quit it is worse: any preference write between plan and confirm makes checkUnchanged throw changedSincePlan. The UI caches plans by URL (UninstallModel.plans), so every retry fails the same way until the plan is made again. Fix: after the final quit, re-read the identity of each chosen leftover that is still a regular file at the same path (not a symlink), and pass that identity. Keep strict identity for the bundle and for folders. The UI should drop its cached plan on changedSincePlan.
3. MEDIUM, Models.swift:104. UninstallError has no LocalizedError text, and the UI shows error.localizedDescription. A user then sees "The uninstall stopped before moving anything: The operation couldn't be completed. (Uninstaller.UninstallError error 4.)" for stillRunning, the most common failure. Probe uninstallErrorsReadAsSentences. Fix: conform to LocalizedError, with one sentence per case that tells the user what to do.
4. MEDIUM, Uninstaller.swift:43-67. plan(for:) never checks cancellation: the GCD continuation in offCooperativePool and ScanEngine.measure's Task.detached never see it. The UI loads plans from .task(id: selectedApp) and relies on cancellation for stale ones. So arrowing through the list runs every plan to the end, concurrently: every leftover is walked, plus 0.3-0.9 s of entitlement reads for apps with groups. Probe cancelledPlanStops: cancelled before it starts, it still returns a full plan. Fix: try Task.checkCancellation() after installedApps(), after the finder, and for each candidate in the measure loop.
5. LOW-MEDIUM, LeftoverFinder.swift:156. Application Scripts/<group> is accepted on the name alone. A group entry that is not shaped like an app group (neither `group.` nor `<TEAMID>.`) can name another app's folder. Probe groupThatIsABundleIdNeverTakesThatAppsScripts: an ad-hoc app listing "com.apple.mail" gets Application Scripts/com.apple.mail, where Mail keeps the user's rule scripts, preselected. Fix: accept only groups that start with `group.` or with the app's own team ID (kSecCodeInfoTeamIdentifier) followed by ".".
6. LOW, LeftoverFinder.run():75 and Uninstaller.swift:87. Labels from the bundle's Contents/Library/LaunchAgents plists are booted out whatever program they run. Probe bundleAgentWhoseProgramIsElsewhereIsNotBootedOut: Label com.google.keystone.agent, with the program outside the bundle, is booted out. Harm: it stops another vendor's job until the next login, or blocks the uninstall with bootoutFailed when the label is com.apple.* under SIP. Fix: keep a label only when BundleProgram is set, or when Program or ProgramArguments[0] lies inside the bundle.
7. LOW, merge with feat/safety-trash. TrashItem gains `allocated` (default 0). The Uninstaller builds items without it, so History shows 0 B for every uninstall (the probe output shows allocated: 0). Pass plan.appMeasurement.allocated and leftover.measurement.allocated.
8. LOW, Uninstaller.blocker(for:). A bundle the user Locked in Finder (uchg makes access(W_OK) false, checked in the scratchpad) gets "Owned by the system, so removing it needs an administrator", which is the wrong reason. Check UF_IMMUTABLE first and say it is Locked in Get Info.

tasks.title: App shell: sidebar, Overview, Full Disk Access onboarding, History, snapshot tooling
tasks.description:
**Goal:** the app shell every screen plugs into, the Overview, Full Disk Access onboarding, History, the design system and the snapshot tooling (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 8-10).

**Owned paths:** `Sources/MacontrolUI/{Shell,Overview,Onboarding,History,Snapshot}/`, `Sources/MacontrolCore/Permissions/`, `Sources/Macontrol/`, `scripts/`, `Tests/MacontrolUITests/` except `DiskMap*`, `Clean*` and `Uninstall*` test files (owned by T-0048 and T-0049).

**Build**
1. Shell: sidebar (Overview, Disk Map, Clean, Uninstall, History), toolbar scan-scope picker (Home, Macintosh HD, Choose Folder...) that drives `DiskMapModel.scan`, ⌘1-⌘5 section shortcuts, ⌘R rescan, window minimum size, a minimal Settings scene, app icon placeholder.
2. Overview: volume capacity bar (used, available, purgeable as a dated note with no purge action), largest folders from the last scan, "N GB safe to clean" link into Clean once the cleaner has scanned, FDA banner. `Theme` tokens and `floatingSurface()` for all UI tasks.
3. FDA onboarding sheet on launch when the probe is not `.granted`: explanation, Open Settings (deep link, legacy `com.apple.preference.security?Privacy_AllFiles` fallback), draggable app icon + Reveal in Finder, poll every second while visible and on `didBecomeActiveNotification`, auto-continue on grant, Relaunch button when still denied after returning, Continue without -> limited-mode banner naming what is skipped. Probe stays per-user (never the system TCC.db); add a `home:`-injected test.
4. History: journal entries grouped by batch, Undo per batch through `TrashService.undo`, wording "In Trash, frees X when emptied" (never "freed").
5. Snapshot: keep `Macontrol --snapshot <dir>` rendering every screen light and dark; add the onboarding sheet and any new screen states. `scripts/bundle-app.sh` stays working.

**Acceptance**
- `swift test` green; snapshot PNGs (light and dark) of Overview, onboarding and History attached to this task with `tasks_cli.py attach`.
- No logic in views beyond formatting; models are `@Observable` and testable; VoiceOver labels on custom controls.
- Findings to close: F-0001 (probe test with a fake home), F-0003 (not applicable until M8: leave open), F-0042 (History wording, with safety-trash).

**Read:** topic-distribution-permissions.md (FDA onboarding, facts P1-P8), topic-platform-constraints.md (C1-C5), sources/colinvkim-radix.md (UI), sources/daisydisk.md (UI), sources/momenbasel-puremac.md (FDA flow rows).

---
**Rules for every builder.** Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (your section plus 2, 5, 10, 11). Stay inside your owned paths; `Package.swift`, `Tests/TestSupport/`, `MacontrolCore/FileIdentity.swift` and `ByteFormatting.swift` are frozen (ask the architect by comment). Public signatures in your module are contracts: additions are free, breaking changes need a comment on the consumer tasks first. Tests build fixtures only in `TemporaryDirectory` and never delete, move or trash anything outside it. No `rm -rf`, no shell strings with paths; destructive calls live only in `Sources/Safety` (SinkAuditTests enforces it). Swift 6, strict concurrency clean, small files, comments only for non-obvious whys. Adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code gets a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry in the same commit; GPL, Commons Clause and unlicensed sources are study only. `swift build && swift test` green before every commit; one build at a time (the machine is slow). When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: build-disk-map
comments.text:
From disk-map (T-0048, feat/disk-map). DiskMapModel keeps everything the shell uses: init(engine:trash:tree:), demo(), public tree/progress/focus (still settable; a direct set does not add a Back entry), and scan(_:) async, which the toolbar can call as before (cancelling the caller stops the walk; the map's own Stop Scan button does too). Snapshot gotcha worth knowing for SnapshotTests: a Swift Testing @MainActor test body runs inside a main-queue job, so RunLoop.main.run(until:) inside SnapshotRenderer cannot run other main-actor jobs, and any .task work (the map's async layout) never finishes during the render; the Disk Map shows its spinner there. tasks.verdictNotes:
Round 1 (review-app-shell-1). I ran swift build (no warnings after touching AppModel, FullDiskAccess and main) and swift test (33/33 green). I re-rendered --snapshot to scratchpad/review-app-shell-1/shots. No critical or high issues. On safety: nothing in this module can trash anything. History Undo goes only through TrashService.undo, which on feat/safety-trash checks FileIdentity and uses RENAME_EXCL. There are no shell strings with paths, and the probe only open()s. The relaunch completion handler is @Sendable (NSWorkspace.h has a sendability audit), so there is no main-actor assert crash. Verdict: approve, with these to fix before or at merge.

MEDIUM
1. Cmd-R is bound twice once T-0048 merges. AppCommands.swift:22 binds it to Rescan, and feat/disk-map InspectorPanel.swift:76 binds it to Reveal in Finder (ARCHITECTURE section 8 also says Reveal). Rescan runs DiskMapModel.replaceTree(nil), which clears the Discard Pile and the session's In Trash list without asking. So one keystroke that the user meant as "reveal" can wipe a staged review. Fix: the architect picks one binding (for example Shift-Cmd-R for Rescan, as Finder has no Cmd-R reveal). A Rescan while the pile is not empty should ask first, or keep the pile.
2. Two sources of truth for scanning. AppModel keeps its own isScanning and scope. On feat/disk-map, DiskMapModel has isScanning and starts scans itself (MapHeader.swift:38 Rescan, DiskMapScreen.swift:128/142 Scan Home and Choose Folder). After the merge, a scan started from the Disk Map shows "Rescan" and no Stop in the toolbar, and the Overview has no spinner. The Overview's "Largest in <scope.title>" can then name a scope other than tree.rootURL. There is also a race: AsyncThrowingStream still delivers buffered events after the consumer is cancelled (next() drains pending before it returns nil). So after scan(B) starts, the old scan(A) loop can still set progress and even tree = A. Fix: derive isScanning from diskMap.isScanning, and the scope label from diskMap.tree?.rootURL. Have one scan entry point, and let a scan write only if it is still the current one.
3. History claims "In Trash, frees X when emptied" for items that are no longer there. Once the user empties the Trash, or uses Finder's Put Back, the journal still says restored=false. So the batch status, the Undo button and the "X in the Trash from Macontrol" total stay forever, and that total only grows. Repro: HistoryModelTests.statusSaysInTrashNeverFreed already asserts "In Trash" for an entry whose trashedPath (/tmp/.Trash/x) does not exist. Fix: in reload(), off the main thread, lstat each unrestored trashedPath and compare its FileIdentity. Mark a missing one "No longer in the Trash", leave it out of inTrashBytes, and disable Undo for it. Test: trash into a TemporaryDirectory, remove the trashed file inside that temp dir, reload, then expect inTrashBytes == 0 and no "In Trash".
4. The Overview's "N GB safe to clean" is the allocated sum of the preselected items (OverviewSummary.swift:51). That overstates clones and hard links (F-0004), and it will disagree with the Clean screen, which uses engine.reclaimable ("never the allocated sum", clean-uninstall-ui CleanModel.swift:9/145). Also, if the cleaner found nothing, cleanItems is empty, so the card falls back to "Find Junk" forever. Fix: show CleanModel's estimate, or word it as found or "up to", and add a "Nothing to clean" state.
5. A grant mid-session leaves the limited scan looking complete. When FDA turns on, the sheet closes and the banner disappears, but the tree scanned without FDA stays on screen. The Overview rows (for example Library) then show the smaller totals with nothing to mark them. That breaks ARCHITECTURE section 9 ("never as smaller totals"), which is the F-0057 class. Fix: after status goes from not granted to .granted, rescan the current scope if a tree exists, or show a "Rescan to include protected folders" note.

LOW
6. The onboarding sheet comes back at every launch after "Continue Without Access". Remember the choice, and keep the banner and sidebar note as the way back in.
7. Keyboard: the onboarding sheet has no .defaultAction (Open System Settings) and no .cancelAction (Continue Without Access), so Return and Esc do nothing. Stop Scan has no Cmd-period.
8. The attached Overview PNGs are stale: they say "Largest in demo", while the current code renders "Largest in Home". Re-attach them.
9. The "Macintosh HD" scope scans only /System/Volumes/Data. The gap between the capacity bar's "used" and the scan total (the sealed system volume, VM, Preboot, snapshots) is never explained (F-0005). Add a line such as "Not in this scan: macOS system and other volumes".
10. The probe returns unknown when both probe files are missing. The user then sees "off" and polling never continues, even after a grant. Add ~/Library/Mail and ~/Library/Messages as further probes.
11. UI polish: at the default size the lower 40% of the Overview is empty. The capacity headline shows 2 decimals ("131,21 GB") while everything else shows 1. In the demo, Movies, Downloads and Documents render with document icons. History batch titles use raw names ("com.example.Editor and 1 more"). Otherwise the look is native and calm in both light and dark.

tasks.description:

**Build**
1. Pure, nonisolated geometry (unit-tested): sunburst (center hole, up to 6 rings, angle proportional to allocated bytes) and squarified treemap (area proportional to bytes). Children too small to draw merge into one labelled "N smaller items" element that opens in the list; nothing silently dropped; no sampling heuristics. Layout computed off the main actor, cancellable, cached per (tree, focus, size). Iterative, no deep recursion.
2. Rendering with SwiftUI `Canvas` at native scale; hit-test index; hover highlight + tooltip; palette: hue per top-level branch, lightness by depth, CVD-checked with `research/bench/windirstat-windirstat/palette_probe.py` (every pair >= dE00 10 under deutan/protan; post the output).

When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: build-app-shell
comments.text: From app-shell (feat/app-shell 91e65bb), what the shell expects from DiskMap: (1) AppModel.scan(scope) calls DiskMapModel.scan(_ url) in a Task and cancels that Task on a new scope or Stop, so keep scan(_:) async and let it end quietly on cancel (setting progress = nil then would help: the Overview shows a spinner from diskMap.progress). (2) The Overview drills in by setting diskMap.focus = <node index> and switching to .diskMap. It reads tree and progress. Please keep those three public. comments.author: build-disk-map
comments.text:
Evidence (feat/disk-map @ 0fbb41e).

Palette (F-0049), palette_probe.py maths (de2000 + Machado simulate imported from research/bench/windirstat-windirstat/palette_probe.py) run on the colours parsed from MapPalette.swift (scratchpad build-disk-map/palette_check.py):

  closest normal: 15.72  (yellow / sand)

Deliberate-bug proofs (each planted in the live file, targeted test run, reverted with git checkout):
1. DiscardPile.add without the ProtectedPaths check -> stagingRefusesProtectedItemsWithTheReason fails: '(pile.add(applications, in: tree) -> nil) == .protected(.protectedLocation("/Applications"))'.
2. Radix-style 100-entry listing sample deciding 'summarize' (F-0040) -> aHugeFileAmongTinyFilesIsNeverMergedAway fails: 'top.contains { $0.node == huge }' and 'merged.first?.count -> 6001 == 6000'. (First attempt sampled the size-sorted list, which always holds the largest file, so the test passed; the fixture now puts the huge file mid-listing.)

comments.author: build-safety-trash
comments.text: Safety (T-0044) for the Discard Pile: disable Move to Trash with ProtectedPaths.refusal(for:) (nil = allowed). .needsCloudConfirmation means ask, then moveToTrash(items, cloudConfirmed: true). Pass keep: [unchecked descendants] on a TrashItem to keep them (F-0026); the report then lists each trashed piece, not the folder. Selecting a folder and something inside it is fine: the inner one is reported trashed via the folder. Match outcomes to nodes by URL.path, not URL (folders gain a trailing slash). comments.author: review-app-shell-1

AsyncThrowingStream still delivers buffered events after the consumer is cancelled, so the old loop can set progress/tree after the new scan started, and its 'defer { isScanning = false }' runs after the new runScan set isScanning = true (map shows not scanning mid-scan).
