comments.author: build-scan-engine
comments.text:
Scan engine (T-0043, branch feat/scan-engine) changed contracts additively; nothing you call was removed or renamed.
- ScanTree: finalizeTotals() now charges each hard-linked inode to the link with the smallest path and marks the others .sharedHardLink at 0 B; callers only set .hardLinked. New: addChild(of:nameBytes:...), relativePathBytes(of:) (byte-exact path, use it for identity-stable keys), storageBytes, bytesPerNode. name(of:) decodes the stored bytes.
- ScanOptions(workerCount:descriptorBudget:) - both optional.
- ReclaimEstimate(freesNow:sharedElsewhere:isIncomplete:) - isIncomplete defaults to false; true when part of the selection could not be read, so show the figure as 'at least'.
- ScanError.notADirectory(URL) is public; scan() of a missing path throws POSIXError.
- scan(URL('/')) walks /System/Volumes/Data once: firmlinked entries at '/Users', '/Applications', ..., Data-only folders (macOS Install Data, .Spotlight-V100) under a real '/System/Volumes/Data' node. Every url(of:) in the tree exists.
- Flags you will see: .unreadable/.incomplete (lower bound, show 'not scanned'), .mountPoint (leaf, 0 B), .dataless (0 B local), .package (sized in full), .compressed, .systemProtected (SF_RESTRICTED).

comments.author: fix-disk-map
comments.text:
Review round 1 resolved on feat/disk-map @ 9d9a156 (one commit on fa4d965). swift build: no warnings. swift test: 46 tests in 12 suites pass, 1 known issue (F-0063, see #3). Every new check was proven by a planted bug, run with a targeted test and reverted with git checkout: M1-M5 below all turned red.

HIGH
1. Stale hover index: fixed. MapChart now stores MapHover(key: LayoutKey, index:), and element(in:) returns an index only if the key matches and the index is in range. Highlight, tooltip and context menu all use that result. A drill-in or a trash splice (which bumps treeVersion) changes the key, so the old index is never read. Test: DiskMapStateTests.aHoverOnlyIndexesTheLayoutItCameFrom covers another focus, an out-of-range index and a spliced tree version. M1: without the key check the test fails (the spliced version resolves to 107).
2. Dismissing the sheet mid-move: fixed. The code is now `let outcomes = apply(report); self.review?.phase = .done(outcomes)`. Cancel is disabled and .interactiveDismissDisabled is set while the phase is .moving. Test: DiskMapReviewTests.dismissingTheSheetWhileMovingStillAppliesTheReport (your probe). M2: the old one-liner fails it.

MEDIUM
3. F-0063 is back to open on the analysis board, with a note. Your probe is now DiskMapReviewTests.trashingTheCarryingHardLinkKeepsBytesThatStayOnDisk, wrapped in withKnownIssue. It turns red ('known issue not recorded') once T-0043 re-charges the surviving link, and then the wrapper can go.
4. Merge with feat/safety-trash, verified in a scratch copy: feat/disk-map plus feat/safety-trash @ 31fc928's Sources/Safety and Tests/SafetyTests. Build clean, 65 DiskMap and Safety tests pass.
 (a) fix-safety-trash restored RefusalReason.notImplemented in 31fc928 ('used by callers that have no TrashService'), so the exhaustive switch in DiskMapText and the no-service fallback compile on both sides unchanged.
 (b) .needsCloudConfirmation no longer blocks staging. The item is staged with StagedItem.isInCloud. The sheet shows the flag on the row and a 'Remove N items from iCloud Drive on every device' checkbox. Move to Trash stays disabled until it is ticked, and then calls moveToTrash(requests, cloudConfirmed: true). Test: cloudItemsAreStagedAndNeedConfirmation. M5: with the gate removed, it moves without asking and the test fails.
 (c) TrashItem(allocated:) does not exist in the scaffold this branch builds against, so it cannot land here before the merge. MERGE-TIME LINE, verified green in the scratch copy: in DiskMapModel+Trash.swift confirmReview, write `TrashItem(url: $0.url, expectedIdentity: $0.identity, allocated: $0.bytes)`.
 Also found in the scratch merge: the real ProtectedPaths resolves paths on disk, so it refuses the demo tree and the fixture trees as missing. DiscardPile now takes its add-time check as `protection:`, which defaults to ProtectedPaths.refusal. The demo and DiskMapFixtures.model(_:) pass `{ _ in nil }`. stagingRefusesProtectedItemsWithTheReason still runs the real policy.
5. Scan race, Cmd-R and dropped state: fixed. scan() takes a generation from beginScan(). Only receive(_:generation:) and finishScan(_:) of the current generation may write, so an old scan can neither set tree/progress nor clear isScanning. The old tree, pile and In Trash list stay until .completed arrives, so Stop brings the previous map back. When a rescan completes, staged items found again at the same path with the same FileIdentity stay staged (ScanTree.node(at:)). Items that changed are dropped. The In Trash list belongs to the old map, and History has those moves. Reveal in Finder is now Shift-Cmd-R, as build-app-shell suggested. Tests: anOlderScanNeverWritesOverANewerOne (M3: without the guard the stale tree lands) and stopKeepsTheMapAndARescanKeepsThePile.
6. Main-actor cost: fixed. Sorted children are cached per (treeVersion, node). listRows is cached per ListRowsKey (tree version, focus, expanded, layout key, limit), and selection is not part of the key. The list pages at 500 node rows and folds the rest into one 'N items more' row that still counts, so the rows still add up. Selecting a node past the limit raises it. Test: aFlatFolderKeepsTheListAndArrowsCheap (200,001 equal-size files, debug build): moveSelection 11 ms (was 91), listRows after a selection change 2.6 us (was 244 ms). The expanded list stays at 501 rows or fewer, and the sums hold before and after 'more'. M4: without the rows cache it takes 151 ms and fails the 5 ms bound.
7. Unscanned content: fixed. StagedItem.isIncomplete is true when the item, or any folder inside it, is .unreadable or .incomplete (ScanTree.hasUnscannedContent checks the ancestry of each flagged node rather than walking the subtree). The sheet rows, the sheet total, the 'frees' line ('Frees at least X') and the tray total all read 'at least X' and show 'Not fully scanned: it may hold more than shown'. The tray chip shows a warning icon and says so in its help. Test: unscannedContentIsStagedAsALowerBound.

LOW
8. Double-click in the centre: the centre tap goes through model.centerClicked(clickCount: NSApp.currentEvent?.clickCount), which goes up only on click 1. Test: aCentreDoubleClickGoesUpOnce (model level). The clickCount wiring in the view was not driven by a UI test.
9. Packages (F-0028): drill(into:) and the focus setter accept only canFocus nodes (isExpandable and not removed), so a package never opens. DiscardPile.add refuses anything inside a package with .insidePackage(name). Test: packagesAreOneItem.
10. focus is validated in its setter (range, isExpandable, not removed). The Overview's `diskMap.focus = node` stays public. leaveRemovedNodes now computes the target first and sets it once. Test: focusOnlyAcceptsFoldersTheMapCanOpen. Each VoiceOver child now has named 'Select' and 'Add to Discard Pile' actions besides open. Still open: the children have no frames and cover only the top level. That needs per-element bounds from MapGeometry; I left it for a follow-up.

tasks.verdictNotes:
Review round 2 of feat/disk-map @ 9d9a156. swift build clean (a cold build in the scratch copy printed no warnings), swift test 46/46 green with 1 known issue. All round-1 fixes check out in the code and their tests: MapHover keyed by LayoutKey, apply() before touching review, Cancel and interactive dismiss disabled while moving, scan generations, focus validation, packages as one item. Probes ran in a git-archive copy, never in the worktree: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-egeb-projects/45c9d2a4-ec2b-4761-8ad2-c890faaddc58/scratchpad/review-disk-map-2/pkg/Tests/MacontrolUITests/ZZReview2ProbeTests.swift (swift test --filter ZZReview2Probe). Safety holds: every trash goes through TrashService with the scan's identity, staging checks ProtectedPaths, nothing shells out, and Finder actions (Reveal, Open in Terminal on the folder, never the file) change nothing. No critical or high issue remains.

MEDIUM
1. An open review survives a rescan, and a trashed outcome with no matching pile item is dropped. replaceTree() rebuilds the pile but leaves `review` alone, so the sheet still lists (and will trash) the old tree's items. In apply(), `.trashed` does `guard let item = stagedItem(at: original) else { continue }`, so an item that went to the Trash is missing from the results. The sheet then says "Nothing was moved. The items stay on the map and in the Discard Pile." Trigger: the shell's Rescan (Cmd-R, AppCommands on feat/app-shell) is not disabled while the sheet is up. If the item is not found again (another scope picked on the scanning screen, or its parent now unreadable), the report is lost.
   Failing tests: aTrashedOutcomeIsNeverDroppedAfterARescan (outcomes.count 0, expected 1) and aRescanDoesNotLeaveAStaleReviewOpen (the review lists old.bin, the pile is empty). The control, controlTrashedOutcomeIsShownWithoutARescan, passes.
   Fix: never `continue` on .trashed. Report it as In Trash by URL, the way notMoved already does without a pile item. In replaceTree, close the review unless phase == .moving, and disable Rescan while model.review != nil (comment posted on T-0047).
   Related, no test: a rescan started during .moving can finish with a tree walked before the move. The trashed items then show as live and the In Trash list is wiped.
2. Main-actor cost on big folders is still high on paths the fix did not time. F-0013's acceptance is "drill-down shows results in under 16 ms". aFlatFolderKeepsTheListAndArrowsCheap warms the sort cache (counted()) before it starts its clock. Probe coldListRowsOnAFlatFolder, 200,001 equal files, debug build:
   - first listRows after a drill-in: 266 ms (373 ms merged with scan-engine, whose name(of:) decodes bytes on every tie-break)
   - after the layout lands: 208 ms
   - after a 1-pt window resize: 190-225 ms
   ListRowsKey includes the whole LayoutKey (width and height), so every resize step, style switch and new layout rebuilds Set(merged) and filters all 200k children.
   Fix: the merged members are exactly the tail of the same sorted order (split() cuts at the first child too small to draw), so listed = sorted.dropLast(merged.count), with no Set and no filter. Key the rows on (treeVersion, focus, merged.count, showsAll, limit), not on the layout's size. Take the sorted children from the off-main layout, or sort off the main actor, instead of sorting 200k names on the main actor at each first drill-in.
3. Staging costs O(whole tree) on the main actor. hasUnscannedContent visits every node for each add, and replaceTree re-adds every staged item. On a 1,010,101-node tree one "Add to Discard Pile" took 260 ms (357 ms merged), debug. Probe: stagingCostOnAMillionNodeTree. A "/" scan has several times as many nodes.
   Fix: one reverse pass per treeVersion that sets a "has unscanned descendant" bit (children have larger indices than parents, as in finalizeTotals), cached like sortedCache. Or walk only the staged subtree.

LOW
4. Merge check: a scratch copy of feat/disk-map plus feat/scan-engine@0755382 (MacontrolCore, ScanEngine, mcscan) and feat/safety-trash@31fc928 (Safety) builds. Every DiskMap test passes except as designed. At merge time:
   (a) trashingTheCarryingHardLinkKeepsBytesThatStayOnDisk fails with "Known issue was not recorded", so drop the withKnownIssue wrapper in the merge commit.
   (b) ReviewSheet ignores ReclaimEstimate.isIncomplete from scan-engine. Say "Frees at least X" when review.isIncomplete || estimate.isIncomplete.
   (c) Add the TrashItem(allocated:) line fix-disk-map noted.
   (d) Once the surviving link is re-charged, TrashedItem.bytes of the carrying link counts bytes still on disk as "In Trash".
5. A failed rescan is invisible while a map exists: scanError only renders in EmptyMapView. Show it over the map.
6. DiskMapItemMenu offers "Open" for any .directory, packages and mount points included. canFocus refuses them, so the menu item does nothing. Gate it on tree.isExpandable.
7. When a rescan does not find a staged item again, the item leaves the pile with no message. Say "N staged items were not in the new scan".
8. The attached snapshots predate the fix round, so the iCloud confirmation toggle, the "at least" sizes and the chip warning were never rendered. Re-run --snapshot and re-attach. The attached ones look clean and native in light and dark.
9. Esc and Space live only in the map's onKeyPress. Once the side list has focus, they do nothing (read from code, not run in the UI). The VoiceOver children still have no frames and cover the top level only (carried over from round 1). beginReview's measure Task is not cancelled when the sheet closes.

Verdict: approve. No critical or high issue. Fix #1 before or at the merge with feat/safety-trash, because that is when .trashed outcomes become real. #2 and #3 are main-thread hitches on large trees, not correctness bugs.

tasks.title: Clean and Uninstall screens
tasks.description:
**Goal:** the Clean and Uninstall screens on top of the `Cleaner` and `Uninstaller` contracts (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md sections 6-8). Build against the scaffold placeholders and demo data; do not wait for the core tasks.

**Owned paths:** `Sources/MacontrolUI/Clean/`, `Sources/MacontrolUI/Uninstall/`, `Tests/MacontrolUITests/Clean*.swift`, `Tests/MacontrolUITests/Uninstall*.swift`.

**Build**
1. Clean: scan on first visit and on demand with streaming rows; items grouped by category with totals; checkboxes seeded from `isPreselected`; safety badge (Safe / Review / Manual) with the rule note in a popover; skipped items disabled with their reason; manual items offer Reveal in Finder only. Footer: "X selected, frees about Y now" (`ScanEngine.reclaimable`). Review sheet lists every item that will move (no truncation) -> `TrashService.moveToTrash` with `item.trashItem` -> per-item outcomes in plain words (refusal reasons) -> trashed rows leave the list and show as "In Trash".
2. Uninstall: searchable app list with lazy sizes and app icons; sections Apps / Apple apps (removable, free to re-download) / Part of macOS (lock, blocker text, no button). Detail: header (icon, version, size), leftovers grouped by evidence with a one-line explanation each; exact-name items unselected; `needsAdministrator` rows say "Needs admin" with Reveal in Finder; running-app warning. Uninstall -> confirmation sheet listing every item and the total -> `Uninstaller.uninstall` -> outcomes.
3. Keep `CleanModel(cleaner:trash:)`, `UninstallModel(uninstaller:)` and their `demo()`; make demo data cover every state (skipped, manual, review, Apple app, built-in, admin-only leftover).

**Acceptance**
- No destructive action without a sheet listing every item; nothing preselected beyond `isPreselected`; keyboard: ⌘F search, Space toggles a row, Return opens review.
- Snapshot PNGs (light and dark) of Clean, its review sheet, Uninstall for a third-party app, an Apple app and a built-in app, attached to this task.
- Findings this UI must surface (close together with the core tasks): F-0011, F-0022, F-0027, F-0042, F-0050.

**Read:** sources/momenbasel-puremac.md (UI rows; CleanupReview filters are MIT), sources/daisydisk.md, sources/alienator88-pearcleaner.md (UI, study only), sources/tw93-mole.md, sources/iliyami-macsai.md (F-0026, F-0027).

---
**Rules for every builder.** Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` first (your section plus 2, 5, 10, 11). Stay inside your owned paths; `Package.swift`, `Tests/TestSupport/`, `MacontrolCore/FileIdentity.swift` and `ByteFormatting.swift` are frozen (ask the architect by comment). Public signatures in your module are contracts: additions are free, breaking changes need a comment on the consumer tasks first. Tests build fixtures only in `TemporaryDirectory` and never delete, move or trash anything outside it. No `rm -rf`, no shell strings with paths; destructive calls live only in `Sources/Safety` (SinkAuditTests enforces it). Swift 6, strict concurrency clean, small files, comments only for non-obvious whys. Adapted MIT/BSD/Apache code gets a `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` entry in the same commit; GPL, Commons Clause and unlicensed sources are study only. `swift build && swift test` green before every commit; one build at a time (the machine is slow). When your code provably avoids a finding: `analysis_cli.py status F-xxxx --set fixed --note "<how + test name>"`. Append 1-3 lessons to M-0001 before finishing.

comments.author: build-uninstaller
comments.text: Uninstaller contract, additive only (feat/uninstaller cb83df9..): 1) Leftover.launchdLabel (String?, init default nil). 2) LeftoverEvidence.contentLibrary (Apple Loops, GarageBand/Logic libraries; always needsAdministrator, never preselected). 3) UninstallPlan.bundleLaunchdLabels (agents inside the bundle, booted out before trashing: show them as 'Stops background item <label>') and UninstallPlan.notes (package receipts, root daemons macontrol cannot stop: show verbatim). 4) UninstallError, thrown before any step runs: blocked(text), needsAdministrator(url), refused(url, reason), changedSincePlan(url) (offer Re-scan), stillRunning(appName) (app did not quit within 10 s), bootoutFailed(label:status:). 5) Uninstaller.init gained systemRoot: and actions: (both defaulted), so AppModel's Uninstaller(engine:trash:) still compiles. Behaviour: plan() for a built-in app has no leftovers (blocker only); a root-owned bundle (Xcode, most App Store apps) has blocker 'Owned by the system...' but still lists leftovers; uninstall(plan, leftovers:) ignores URLs not in the plan and throws if a chosen leftover needsAdministrator, so seed checkboxes from isPreselected and disable admin rows. uninstall() politely quits the app (NSRunningApplication.terminate, same bundle or same id), so warn when it is running. Plan latency is dominated by measuring the bundle (Xcode took 15 s with the placeholder engine): show leftovers progressively or a spinner on the size. Evidence one-liners I suggest: bundleIdentifier 'Named with the app's identifier', containerMetadata 'macOS records this container as the app's', appGroup 'Shared container the app declares', launchdJob 'Background job that starts the app', exactName 'Same name as the app, check before removing', contentLibrary 'Sound library, needs an administrator'.

tasks.verdictNotes:
REQUEST CHANGES (feat/clean-uninstall-ui @ ec8d76a). swift build is clean, and a recompile of every owned Clean/Uninstall file gives no warnings. swift test passes 132/132. Round 1 items 1, 2, 3, 5, 6b, 6c, 7, 9, 10, 11 and 13 are fixed. 6a (isIncomplete) is deferred with a merge note, which is acceptable because feat/scan-engine is not accepted yet. Items 8 and 14 are partly fixed, and 12 is still open (see 7 below). The probe tests are in scratchpad/review-clean-uninstall-ui-2/ZZReview2ProbeTests.swift. Copy the file into Tests/MacontrolUITests and run swift test --filter ZZReview2ProbeTests. I added it to the worktree only to run it, then removed it, so the tree is clean. I did not claim the task, so that its status stays ready_for_review.

HIGH
1. [safety, F-0011/F-0022 regression from fix item 4] A leftover checked only by its seed stays checked after a re-plan says it must not be preselected. UninstallModel.show() writes isPreselected into `choices` the first time it sees a leftover, and after that `chosen[url] == nil` is never true again. So the seed is treated like a user decision for the rest of the session. The core turns preselection off when another installed app claims the item ("Also used by X": a second copy, a shared app group, a shared launchd job). The UI ignores that and keeps the item checked. The confirmation then lists it, and uninstall() trashes the other app's data and boots out its shared job. Probe aLeftoverThatLosesPreselectionIsNotLeftChosen fails with 2 issues. It selects Probe, installs "Probe Beta" with the same identifier and runs rescan(). The cache then carries note "Also used by Probe Beta" and isPreselected == false, but isChosen is true and the confirmation rows contain it. This breaks the acceptance line "nothing preselected beyond isPreselected". Fix: keep only explicit user edits (setChosen/toggle) as overrides, and work out the default from the current plan's isPreselected each time. Also drop an override of true when a leftover gains a note or loses preselection, because that is new information the user has not seen. switchingAppsKeepsTheUsersLeftoverChoices must still pass.

MEDIUM
2. [functional/UI] Blocked apps have no way forward. On a real Mac every Mac App Store app is root-owned: on this machine /Applications/Xcode.app is root:wheel with _MASReceipt. So the Apple apps section gets the blocker "Owned by the system... Reveal it in Finder and drag it to the Trash". (a) The detail has no Reveal in Finder for the bundle: not in the header, the notice or the row context menu. (b) It also shows "Made by Apple. You can remove it and download it again for free", which contradicts the blocker. (c) Leftover checkboxes stay interactive with no action behind them. After the user trashes the app in Finder, it leaves the list, so its leftovers can no longer be reached. Fix: put a Reveal in Finder button on the blocker notice (and in the AppRow context menu), hide the Apple notice when a blocker is present, and turn the leftover checkboxes off (or show them read-only) while canUninstall is false.
3. [UI, F-0050 visibility] TrashSheet has a fixed 640x540 frame, and its header (title, message, every note, warning) is fixedSize, so the list of items to move only gets the height that is left. With 8 notes (4 "Stops background item", 2 root-daemon notes, 2 receipts) and the running warning, 2.5 of 5 rows are visible. With more notes the list shrinks to a sliver. Render: scratchpad/review-clean-uninstall-ui-2/many-notes-sheet.png (probe manyNotesSqueezeTheItemList). Fix: put the notes in a section inside the scrolling List, or cap the header height and let it scroll, or give the sheet a min/ideal height and make it resizable.

LOW
4. The Clean footer shows a stale estimate during Scan Again. scan() empties selection and items, but `estimate` keeps the last .freesNow value, and refreshEstimate returns early while scanning. The footer reads "2 selected, frees about 13.33 GB now" (the old figure) until the scan ends. Fix: set `estimate = .working` in scan().
5. `inTrash` is not keyed by URL. After Scan Again, a cache that its app recreated appears both as a live row and under In Trash with the same id (List(selection:) tags collide). A second trash of it appends a duplicate id to ForEach(model.inTrash). Fix: replace by URL, or drop In Trash rows whose URL comes back live.
6. Uninstall: the search can hide the selected app while its detail and the enabled "Uninstall…" default button stay. Return typed into the search field can then open "Uninstall <hidden app>?". Not verified with real key events. The sheet still names the app, so this is not destructive. Fix: clear selectedApp when the query filters it out, or keep Return away from the search field.
7. (Round 1 #12, still open) After a partial uninstall (the bundle is trashed, a leftover fails), apply() removes the app and its plan and drops `choices`. After Done, the failed leftovers can no longer be reached from the UI. Fix: keep a leftovers-only entry, or at least a Reveal in Finder button in the outcome rows that failed.
8. The error text after side effects is incomplete. stillRunning or bootoutFailed can come after uninstall() has quit the app and booted out jobs, but the sheet says only "The uninstall stopped before moving anything: …". Say that the app was quit and name the background items that were stopped, so the outcome lists every step, as the preview does (F-0069).
9. The measure limiter can lose a size. When a queued row is cancelled (scrolled away) and comes back before a slot frees, the new .task returns at once because `measuring` still holds the URL. The old task then exits on isCancelled, and the row shows "–" until it scrolls away and back. Fix: let the new task wait for the queued one, or remove the URL from `measuring` when a cancelled task gives up.
10. Nits: confirmReview skips the recheck when cleaner == nil but trash != nil. That fails open, although no caller builds it today; guard both. apply(report, to: pending.plan) overwrites a fresher plan found while the sheet was open with the older confirmed plan. The review sheet lists rows in stream order, not in the grouped, largest-first order of the screen.

UI (snapshots): the layout reads clean and PureMac-like in both modes. The badges, In Trash wording and outcome wording are good. The snapshots render in an inactive window (grey prominent/red buttons, grey checkboxes), so they cannot show the accent and destructive tints. That is not a code issue, but one snapshot of a key window would show the real look.

Verified: every destructive path goes through TrashService/Uninstaller with the batch exactly as listed. Recheck runs before the Clean trash, double confirm is guarded by isWorking set before the first await, admin leftovers can never enter a batch, and outcome URLs match because Safety reports under the given URL. No shell, no rm, and no path resolution in the UI.

Verdict: FAIL. 3 of 21 attacks broke. Suite: Tests/SafetyAttackTests (commit d3cc66b on main), 26 tests. Full swift test: 303 tests in 42 suites, green with 5 known issues (the 3 breaks), 3 of 3 runs, ~34 s. Nothing was pushed.

Method: each test builds a hostile tree in a TemporaryDirectory sandbox with a fake home and drives the real TrashService, Cleaner (scan, recheck, trash), Uninstaller (plan, UninstallActions.live with launchctl recorded) and DiskMapModel (real scan, stage, confirm). The Trash backend is a path-based rename into the sandbox that refuses anything whose real parent is outside it. Every test compares an fd-relative snapshot (type, dev, inode, size, flags, link target) before and after, so only the intended paths may differ, and after Undo the tree must match inode for inode.

HELD
- A1 Shell and odd names ($(...), backticks, quotes, &, -rf, *, ~, %d, newline, a JSON line inside a name, Cyrillic lookalike, NFD accent): moved as themselves, no command ran, one journal line each, Undo exact (Trash, disk map, cleaner, launchd label).
- A2 Protected places in the fake home (home, its parent, Library, Library/Caches, Documents, .ssh and a key in it, Keychains, .Trash, iCloud Drive and its provider folder, ../ spellings, sneaky/. through a link, the /System/Volumes/Data spelling): all refused, no backend call, the ordinary cache in the same batch still moved. Disk map: none can be staged.
- A3 Symlinks pointing outside (to Documents, to .ssh, to a file, dangling): the link moves, never the target. A cache link to Documents is sized as a link.
- A4 Hard links to Documents and .ssh files inside a trashed cache: the other names and their bytes stay.
- A5 TOCTOU between scan and delete (folder swapped for a link; a file's parent swapped for a link to a same-named file) for Trash, Clean (recheck keeps the scan identity), disk map and Uninstall (checkUnchanged stops before quit); a swap mid-batch; a swap during the app's quit: all refused.
- A6 Locked file, locked folder, file in a locked folder: refused, flags untouched.
- A7 Running-app cache with real libproc: a cache this test holds open ("In use by swiftpm-testing-helper") and one named after the test executable ("... is running") are skipped; a cache opened after the scan is caught by recheck. The idle cache still moves.
- A8 Vendor folder shared by two apps: uninstalling AppA with every leftover checked takes Vendor/AppA, its cache, prefs, agent and cache link. Vendor/AppB, Vendor/shared.db, Caches/com.vendor and AppB's files stay. Both batches undo.
- A9 LaunchAgent: bootout gets exactly ["bootout", "gui/<uid>/<label with $(...)>"] as one argument, before the plist moves. A label containing "/" stops the uninstall before any launchctl call or move.
- A10 Unchecked children: kept paths spelled through a symlinked parent or in another case survive. The rest moves piece by piece and Undo rebuilds the folder. A kept path past PATH_MAX fails the whole batch closed.
- A11 PATH_MAX: a cache with a chain deeper than PATH_MAX is measured to the bottom, moves whole and comes back whole; an item past PATH_MAX is refused.
- A12 Undo journal replaced by a symlink to .ssh/authorized_keys: nothing moves, and the keys file is not written.

BROKE (filed, each with its failing test wrapped in withKnownIssue)
- T-0053 TrashAttackTests.aSwapInsideTheMoveMustNotTrashTheLinkedFile: a parent swapped for a link after the identity check, during the move, sends Documents/proj/data.bin to the Trash, reported as trashed. Real FileManager.trashItem follows the swapped parent too (probe on a scratch APFS image). Microsecond window; Undo can restore it.
- T-0054 TrashAttackTests.aSwapOntoAHardLinkMustNotTrashTheDocumentsName: when the selected file is a hard link of a Documents file, a parent swapped for a link keeps the identity, so the Documents name is trashed.
- T-0055 TrashAttackTests.aLockedFileInsideASelectedFolderStays: a user-locked file inside a selected folder goes to the Trash with it (only the item and its parent are checked). Real trashItem does the same.

Deliberate-bug proof (scratch worktree, main untouched): 8 mutations, each caught. Identity check removed -> 5 swap attacks fail. Policy disabled -> 4 fail. Keep ignored, journal O_NOFOLLOW dropped, "/" label guard dropped, open-file check dropped, running-app check dropped, vendor folder offered whole -> the matching attacks fail. Uninstall's own checkUnchanged still caught its after-plan swap with the Trash identity check removed.

Side fix (commit d0f5d35, comment on T-0048): DiskMapReviewTests.dismissingTheSheetWhileMovingStillAppliesTheReport spun forever on the main actor, and swift test hung 2 of 3 runs once this suite added main-actor load.

Not covered (code-read only): a bundle's SMAppService plist can name any label, and startsProgram passes any relative BundleProgram, so uninstalling it boots out that label even if another app's job holds it. It needs a hostile or odd bundle and is not filed.

tasks.title: Trash: a folder swapped for a symlink during the move sends another file to the Trash
tasks.description:
Failing test: SafetyAttackTests/TrashAttackTests/aSwapInsideTheMoveMustNotTrashTheLinkedFile (wrapped in withKnownIssue; remove the wrapper when fixed).

What happens: TrashBatch checks policy and FileIdentity on the canonical path, then hands the path string to backend.moveToTrash. If a parent folder of the item is replaced by a symlink after the check and before the move, the path-based move follows the new link: Documents/proj/data.bin went to the Trash instead of the checked cache file, and the outcome says .trashed. Confirmed with the real backend: FileManager.trashItem on a scratch APFS image follows a parent swapped for a symlink (probe: scratchpad/verify-safety/probe.swift, case 2).

Impact: a microsecond window, needs another process changing the tree at that instant. The wrong object is in the Trash and journaled, so Undo can put it back; nothing is deleted.

Suggested fix (Sources/Safety/TrashBatch.swift trash(_:)): after the backend returns, lstat the destination and compare with the identity checked; on mismatch move it back with renamex_np(dest, original, RENAME_EXCL | RENAME_NOFOLLOW_ANY), journal nothing and report .refused(.identityChanged). Optionally open the canonical parent with O_NOFOLLOW_ANY right before the move to narrow the window further.

comments.author: final-fix
comments.text: Fixed on main @ 39b1d2e (Sources/Safety/TrashBatch.swift trash/putBack). Just before the move the canonical parent is opened with O_NOFOLLOW_ANY and its identity recorded, and the item's identity re-read. After backend.moveToTrash returns, lstat(destination) must equal the checked identity and the parent must still open link-free with the same identity. On a mismatch the object goes back to where the path now leads (canonicalPath through the swapped link) with renamex_np(RENAME_EXCL|RENAME_NOFOLLOW_ANY), no journal line, outcome .refused(.identityChanged). If it cannot go back (something took its place) it is journaled under that origin with its real identity and the outcome is .failed, so Undo in History restores it. Tests: TrashAttackTests.aSwapInsideTheMoveMustNotTrashTheLinkedFile (wrapper removed; also asserts an empty journal) and aSwappedMoveThatCannotGoBackIsJournaledForUndo (new Sandbox.afterEachMove hook). Mutation proof: dropping the post-move guard fails both; dropping the fallback journal line fails the second.

tasks.title: Trash: an item reached through a folder that became a symlink passes when the leaf is a hard link of the scanned file
tasks.description:
Failing test: SafetyAttackTests/TrashAttackTests/aSwapOntoAHardLinkMustNotTrashTheDocumentsName (withKnownIssue; remove when fixed).

What happens: Caches/com.example.shared/blob and Documents/proj/blob are hard links of one inode. After the scan, Caches/com.example.shared is replaced by a symlink to Documents/proj. canonicalPath resolves the parent through the new link to Documents/proj/blob, FileIdentity matches (same inode), so TrashBatch moves the Documents name to the Trash. The user selected a cache entry; a name in Documents left. Identity alone cannot tell two names of one inode apart.

Impact: needs a hard link shared with a user folder plus a folder swap between scan and delete. No bytes are lost (the other name keeps the data) and Undo restores it, but the item that moved is not the one the user chose.

Suggested fix: refuse when the canonical parent is not the parent the caller named (the scan's path), up to case and the /System/Volumes/Data spelling; or carry the parent folder's identity in TrashItem and compare it with the opened parent. The post-move identity check proposed for the sibling task does not catch this one (same inode).

comments.author: final-fix
comments.text: Fixed on main @ 39b1d2e (TrashBatch.process + samePlace). After the policy check, the canonical path must equal the path the caller named up to macOS's own spellings: case, the /System/Volumes/Data prefix, and the root links /var, /tmp, /etc into /private (Swift String equality also matches composed and decomposed names). Otherwise .refused(.identityChanged) before the backend is called. Scan paths are already canonical (TemporaryDirectory realpaths, the disk map scans /System/Volumes/Data, home is /Users/x), so only a link on the way trips it. Tests: TrashAttackTests.aSwapOntoAHardLinkMustNotTrashTheDocumentsName (wrapper removed, now expectOnly([]) + no backend call) and systemSpellingsOfAPathStillMove (other case, Data prefix, composed name all still move). Mutations: removing the guard fails the first; comparing raw strings fails the second. Within-batch swaps onto a same-name hard link are also caught by the post-move parent check from T-0053.

tasks.title: Trash: a user-locked file inside a selected folder goes to the Trash with its folder
tasks.description:
Failing test: SafetyAttackTests/TrashAttackTests/aLockedFileInsideASelectedFolderStays (withKnownIssue; remove when fixed).

What happens: ProtectionPolicy.flagRefusal reads UF_IMMUTABLE on the item and its parent only. A folder that holds a file the user locked in Finder is moved whole, locked file included. Confirmed with the real backend: FileManager.trashItem moves such a folder (scratch APFS image, probe case 1). The same path serves Clean (preselected caches), Uninstall leftovers and the disk map.

Impact: the lock is the one keep-this signal a user can set; F-0024's after says locked items are reported as locked and skipped. The file sits in the Trash (Undo restores it), one Empty Trash away from deletion.

Suggested fix: before moving a folder, find locked descendants (the measure walk already visits every entry; ATTR_CMN_FLAGS is cheap in getattrlistbulk) and treat them as implicit keep paths, so TrashBatch.trashKeeping moves everything around them; or refuse the folder with .locked and name the file. Add the case to the test once decided.

comments.author: final-fix
comments.text: Fixed on main @ 39b1d2e, option B (refuse the folder, name the file) rather than moving around the locked item: piecing out an .app bundle would leave a broken app, and every UI already shows refusals per item. ProtectionPolicy.lockedItem(inside:) walks the folder fd-relative (no links followed, stays on its volume, never lists an evicted iCloud folder, skips unreadable folders) for UF_IMMUTABLE|UF_APPEND. TrashBatch.trash runs it right before every move, so items and trashKeeping pieces are both covered; the outcome is the new RefusalReason.holdsLocked(<path inside the folder>), worded in Clean ('Not moved: it holds a/b.txt, which is locked (Finder, Get Info)') and the disk map. Not run while staging (DiscardPile/ProtectedPaths.refusal), since it walks the whole folder. Test: TrashAttackTests.aLockedFileInsideASelectedFolderStays (one and two levels deep, an unlocked sibling still moves, Undo restores). Mutation: skipping the walk fails it. Cost: one fstatat per entry, 10.1 s for the 311k-entry bench fixture on this loaded M1 (ponytail note points at getattrlistbulk if it matters).

comments.text:
Builder notes (ux-polish), branch feat/ux-polish @ 1d8632c, based on main c79b566 (fast-forward merge).

What changed
- ScanEngine: new ScanEvent.preview(ScanTree), about 4/s from 0.25 s on. TreeSink keeps bytesUnderTopLevel, updated once per listing (plus the Data-volume root entries under /System/Volumes/Data, charged to "System"). preview(limit: 256) builds a one-level tree of the largest root children. The completed tree is built exactly as before.
- ScanEngine.volumeBytesInUse(at:) returns ATTR_VOL_SPACEUSED when the root is a mount point. "/" and the Data volume both mean the Data volume. APFS capacity and free space are per container, and statfs gave 237 GB for "/" and Data alike. SPACEUSED gave 12.6 GB and 202.2 GB, which matches df.
- DiskMapModel: preview, previewVersion, expectedTotal (last scan's total when the same root is scanned again, else the volume's used bytes, else nil). All are cleared in beginScan and finishScan and gated by the scan generation.
- ScanningView: header with a bar and the current path, a preview sunburst with a legend (nothing can be hovered yet) or a labelled treemap, and a caption. ScanPreviewChart is Equatable on (version, style) and lays out inline: one ring of at most 256 items.

Measured
- Real stream over ~/projects (888k nodes, read-only, debug engine): 90 previews, first at 0.27 s, largest gap 0.38 s, 0 shrinks. In 8 top-level folders the last preview ran ahead of the final total. In every one, the excess equals the bytes of hard links that finalizeTotals charges once (for example macontrol +378,839,040 B, which is exactly its extra links).
- Cost under the walk lock (release build): preview() took 300 ms with 200k entries at the top when it read self.tree once per child. Copying the tree to a local first brought it to 3 ms. The top-level walk took 561 ms for 150k listings at depth 12 through self.tree; a ScanTree method brings that to 90 ms, against a 15 ms baseline. Previews are also spaced to at most 1/10 of the walk.

- TreeSinkTests.previewSizesOnlyGrowAndEndAtTheFinishedTotals, the Data-root bytes pinned in dataVolumeRootIsPlacedAtUserFacingPaths, ScanEngineTests.previewOfAFinishedWalkMatchesTheCompletedScan (real walk vs Fixtures.scanTree), volumeBytesInUseOnlyForAVolumeRoot, DiskMapStateTests.previewsShowUntilTheScanCompletes, and DiskMapSnapshotTests.scanningStateRenders (both styles, 1180x760 and 900x600, light and dark).

fix-live-map-1, round 3 fixes at ab11937 (feat/ux-polish, one commit on 37d8380). swift build is green, and swift test passed 324/324 in 62 s. The worktree was clean afterwards, and $TMPDIR macontrol-tests-* stayed at 293 before and after.

(1, medium) Colours: fixed with a different rule. First-seen order is gone.
- MapPalette.ScanColours holds a name-to-slot map. On each preview, DiskMapModel updates it with the names that have bytes, largest first. Zero-byte names get no colour.
- The 8 largest names always have 8 different colours. Each keeps its colour unless another of them chose it first; in that case it takes the lowest free colour. The order of choosing is: the last finished map's largest, then last preview's largest, then the rest by size.
- A smaller name keeps the first colour it gets: its rank slot, or the lowest one its neighbours don't have.
- On `.completed`, `finish` runs the last update on the finished tree (its top 256, using the sort the list uses next). It gives a new colour to any smaller name that sits next to a name of the same colour. This runs once, not on every preview, because doing it on every preview made two folders of about the same size swap colours back and forth.
- A scan of the same folder starts from the last map's colours. This fixes (c).
- The builder takes `colours: [String: Int]`. A name missing from it gets its rank slot, so demo trees and trees that did not come from a scan look as they do on main. MapPalette.slots(firstSeen:) is removed.

Your Monte Carlo probe, run against this commit (same seed, 500 scans, 12 to 40 names, steps 0 to 60):
- 2 of the 4 largest share a colour: 0 scans (was 167). 2 of the 8 largest: 0 (was 409; main 0).
- Colour changes between previews: 279 of 182,002 name pairs, in 148 scans (was 2,702 of 181,979, in 424 scans). Every one of them is a name joining the 8 largest.
- Neighbours of one colour in the finished map: 0 (main 0).
- Rescan with a different walk order: the 8 largest have the same colours in 500 of 500 scans. During a rescan, a smaller folder can give up its colour once to one of those 8: 769 of 180,986 pairs.
- Known cost: when the preview turns into the finished map, `finish` recolours about 0.3 smaller names per scan (298 in 1,000 scans) to keep neighbours apart. The 8 largest keep their colours.

Tests:
- DiskMapPaletteTests.scanColoursKeepTheLargestApartAndEachNameSteady, replacing the firstSeen test. 500 random scans of 1 to 40 names. It checks that the 8 largest are distinct on every update; that a colour changes only when its name joins the 8 largest; that the finished map has no neighbours of one colour; and that a rescan with a new walk order never moves a colour of the last map's 8 largest.
- DiskMapStateTests.aHomeFolderScanKeepsItsLargestFoldersApart, in both styles, through the real model and builder. It uses your 20 home names. The first preview has bytes only for Library, .zsh_history and .gitconfig. Then Music and Downloads are drawn past the 8th and grow into the 8 largest; that preview makes 2 counted changes, both allowed. It checks that the finished map's 8 largest have 8 colours, the same ones as the last preview; that drawn names change colour only when they join the 8 largest; and that a second scan (beginScan(of: "/x"), other order) keeps those 8 colours the whole time and ends with the same 8.
- Deliberate-bug proofs, run in a scratch export with one build per batch. All 5 were caught, and the control run was clean:
  - B1, no rescan seed plus no neighbour pass: home 7 issues, palette 651.
  - B2, a newcomer keeps a colour already taken: home 7, palette 6,945.
  - B3, last preview's largest lose their priority: home 17, palette 8,841.
  - B4, finish does not record the map's largest: home 9, palette 19,611.
  - B5, the model skips `finish` on completion: home 9.
- Snapshots (headless): the scanning to scanned sunburst pair keeps each folder's colour: Library blue, projects amber, Pictures teal, Movies pink, Music yellow, Downloads plum. Attached as fix-live-map-1-*.

(2, nit) Previews are opt-in: `ScanEngine.scan(_:previews: Bool = false)`. Only DiskMapModel passes true, so mcscan and Fixtures.scanTree walk with no preview pauses. There is no test for this, because proving it needs a walk longer than 0.25 s. The gate is one ternary in scan().

It passed alone in 0.77 s, and the second full run passed 324/324. That test has the same wall-clock-under-load problem as the one in M-0001's live-map lesson 1.

(1, medium, Move to Trash does not recolour): FIXED at the shared point. treeDidChange() now runs treeColours.finish(ranked:) on the new tree's top 256, sorted the way the side list sorts them. Both writers of `tree` go through it: replaceTree on .completed (which now does `treeColours = previewColours; replaceTree(result)`) and the Move to Trash splice. It checks three things: the 8 largest have 8 colours, the 7 that stay keep theirs, and no two ring neighbours share a colour.

(2, low, ring closure): FIXED. ScanColours.neighbourSlots now works around the ring, so the last name's other neighbour is the first. Both finish() and a new smaller name's first colour use it. Nine folders now give n8=1, the same as main. (3, low, neighbours during previews): the limit is now STATED, not smoothed. The ScanColours doc says the finished map never puts one colour on two neighbours, but while a scan runs two touching wedges below the 8 largest can share one, in about 1 preview in 12 of a random sweep. The finish() doc gives the reason: recolouring on every preview made colours flip back and forth. Corrected acceptance: neighbouring slices never share a colour in the finished map, and that includes after a Move to Trash. During previews, the 8 largest always have 8 different colours, and a smaller wedge can match the wedge next to it.

(4, low, nothing tests that the app asks for previews): FIXED. ScanOptions has two new internal fields, progressInterval (default 0.1 s) and firstPreview (default 250 ms), and buildTree and walk read them; the defaults leave the app unchanged. The new test is DiskMapStateTests.theAppAsksForPreviewsAndAPlainScanGetsNone. It gives the real DiskMapModel.scan an engine with a 1 ms interval and firstPreview .zero, then runs it on 40 folders and expects previewVersion > 0. A plain engine scan must give progress > 0 and previews == 0. Each side retries up to 20 times, because a small tree can finish before the first progress tick.

Deliberate-bug proofs. I ran them in a scratch git-archive copy with a cold build, 2 builds, filter DiskMapStateTests|DiskMapPaletteTests:
- M1: treeDidChange recolours only while isScanning, which is ab11937's behaviour. The trash test fails with 16 issues: the top 8 have 7 colours in 7 of 8 cases per style.
- M3: DiskMapModel.scan calls engine.scan(root) without previews. The previews test fails with previewVersion 0.
- M2: neighbourSlots goes back to linear neighbours. The palette sweep fails with 56 issues, and the trash test fails with 4 issues (ring last == first after f0 or f1 is trashed).
- M4: the engine always takes previews. The previews test fails because the plain scan got previews.

I also ran your ReviewProbe2Tests against 574288a:
- P1: the ring's last and first share a colour in 0 of 500 maps (was 45; main 0).
- P2: two of the top 8 share a colour after a trash in 0 of 300 runs (was 271; main 0). Adjacent wedges of one colour: 0.
- P3b: 1,543 of 18,300 preview frames, the same as before. That is the limit stated in (3).

Note: in the first full run, aFlatFolderKeepsTheListAndArrowsCheap failed once, 63 ms against its 50 ms limit, with the load average at 38 to 52. It passed alone in 13 ms and in the second full run in 12 ms. This test and its limit are unchanged from main, and this change does not touch that path.

Round 4 @ ab11937 (review-live-map-2). Verified OK: swift build green; swift test 324/324 in 66 s in the worktree, worktree clean afterwards. No macontrol-tests-* folder was created while that run lasted (the count moves with 3 other suites running). The branch still merges cleanly into main 5910c96 (git merge-tree). Re-read of the code: previews are built on the walk's run thread with the FolderWalk lock held. Per preview, the main actor gets at most 256 entries plus one ScanColours.update. ScanPreviewChart is Equatable on (version, style). On .completed, the sort is the side list's own cached sortedChildren, so the main thread does no extra sort. The final tree is unchanged (describe() test). readGoal, Stop and the generation guards are as in round 3. Previews are opt-in, and mcscan does not ask for them. Round-3 dispositions: (1) implemented as described, and the top-8 invariant holds on every update; (2) implemented.
Probes are in scratchpad/review-live-map-2/export/Tests/MacontrolUITests/ReviewProbe2Tests.swift and use the real DiskMapModel and MapLayoutBuilder (sunburst, 800x600@2x).
ISSUES:
(1, medium, colours after Move to Trash) A splice does not recolour. DiskMapModel+Trash sets tree and calls treeDidChange(), and treeColours stays as the scan left it. The folder that moves into the 8 largest keeps its sticky slot, which one of the 8 already holds. Example: A..J, trash B. The branch gives A=0 C=2 D=3 E=4 F=5 G=6 H=7 I=0, so A and I are both blue; main gives 8 colours. Sweep of 300 trashes of one top-8 folder (9-30 names): two of the 8 largest share a colour in 271 on the branch and 0 on main. This regresses main in the map's main action and lasts until the next scan. The fix note calls it "as before this change", but main is the baseline. Fix: after treeDidChange() in the splice, run the same finish that .completed runs (treeColours.finish(ranked: ranked(sortedChildren(of: root).prefix(256), in: tree))). Add a test that trashes one of the 8 largest.
(2, low, ring closure) ScanColours.finish and slot(at:) check only index-1 and index+1, but the sunburst ring closes. Main's MapPalette.slot(for:of:) guards last against first, and topSlots bypasses it for every name in `colours`. Example: 9 folders, all drawn. The branch gives n8=0 next to n0=0 (blue on blue); main gives n8=1. Sweep of 500 finished maps with 2-24 names, all drawn: last and first share a colour in 45 on the branch and 0 on main. The round-2 palette test checked (index + 1) % total; its ab11937 replacement checks only linear neighbours, so this passes. Fix: count ranked.first as a neighbour of ranked.last. This is exact when every name with bytes is drawn; otherwise a grey smaller-items wedge sits between them, and the extra check is harmless. Restore the ring check in the test.
(3, low, neighbours during previews) By design, the neighbour pass runs only in finish. Through the real model and builder, 1,543 of 18,300 preview frames (300 random scans of 9-40 names) show adjacent wedges of one colour, ring closure included; rank colouring shows 0. The round-3 acceptance text says "neighbouring slices never share a colour", which is now true only for the finished map. Either guard it with hysteresis, or state the limit in the disposition and in ScanColours' doc.
(4, low, test gap) Nothing tests that the app asks for previews. Deliberate bug: engine.scan(root, previews: true) changed to engine.scan(root) in DiskMapModel.scan. Built, then --filter "DiskMap|ScanEngine|TreeSink|Shell|Overview|Snapshot" passed 112/112, so the live map vanishes from the app with a green suite. One option: make the first-preview delay and the progress interval injectable, then assert that scan(_, previews: true) yields at least one .preview and scan(_) yields none.
Not a defect: the per-listing bytesUnderTopLevel accumulation still runs with previews off. By the builder's own numbers it adds about 75 ms per 150k listings, under 1% of a home scan.

tasks.description: Seen 2026-09-23 while running the full suite on main @ 39b1d2e: CleanerScanTests.fileHeldOpenByARunningProcessIsSkipped and CleanModelTests.scanStreamsARealCatalogAndEstimatesTheSelection fail with reason 'Could not check which files DTServiceHub has open' (both fail the same way in a clean copy; both passed earlier today). Two DTServiceHub processes (Xcode's and the iOS 26.5 simulator runtime's, pid 6614/6670, owned by the user) were running. InUseGuard.skipReason returns the first uninspected process for every item, so while any Simulator or Instruments session runs, Clean preselects nothing. Options: limit the uninspected check to items whose owner could be that process, or retry the inspection, or report it once as a caution instead of a skip. comments.author: feas-apple-apps
comments.text: Requirements from T-0070 (docs/research/feasibility-apple-apps.md) for the privileged path: (1) delete root-owned, non-restricted bundles and folders in /Applications, /Library/Application Support, /Library/Audio, /Library/Developer; (2) delete receipt files /var/db/receipts/<id>.{bom,plist} (same as pkgutil --forget; MAS installs DO leave a receipt: com.apple.pkg.Xcode, InstallProcessName=appstoreagent, verified); (3) refuse SF_RESTRICTED items up front (/Library/Apple, /System/Library/AssetsV2): even root gets EPERM there; (4) with hardcore mode off, rename into the INVOKING USER's ~/.Trash (same volume). A root process calling trashItem probably lands in root's Trash, where the user can neither see nor undo it (inferred, unverified). Verified: a non-root admin cannot move a root:wheel 0755 bundle to another parent (EACCES on the moved folder's '..' update), so even 'Move to Trash' of Apple apps needs your helper. Open: does App Management/TCC block a root helper from deleting a whole Apple-signed bundle unless the helper has FDA?

comments.author: feas-permanent
comments.text: Two facts from T-0069 that affect the helper's 'remove' step (feasibility-privileged.md step 4 and fact 16). (1) removefileat(fd, name) gives no fd safety: it calls fcntl(fd, F_GETPATH) and then removefile() on the joined absolute path (apple-oss-distributions/removefile @ removefile-85.100.6, removefile.c:255-297). The walk is fts by full path (removefile_tree_walker.c:238). (2) When euid is 0, removefile clears UF_IMMUTABLE/UF_APPEND with chflags before it unlinks (removefile_tree_walker.c:117, 166, 200). In the helper it would delete files the user Locked, which breaks the F-0024/F-0070 rule. Unprivileged, locked files fail with EPERM, verified here. (3) Flag availability: on macOS 14 (xnu-10002.1.13, vfs_syscalls.c:6294), unlinkat accepts only AT_REMOVEDIR, AT_REMOVEDIR_DATALESS and AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW_ANY and returns EINVAL for anything else. AT_RESOLVE_BENEATH and AT_NODELETEBUSY first appear in xnu-12377.1.9 (macOS 26.0), AT_UNIQUE in 12377.121.6, and O_RESOLVE_BENEATH in xnu-11417 (15.4+). So the helper needs the same fd-relative remover the app uses, with no removefile. T-0069 proposes one in Sources/Safety that both processes compile (docs/research/feasibility-permanent.md).

sessions.summary: Recommend one-shot AppleScript 'do shell script ... with administrator privileges' (via NSAppleScript) launching a bundled ad-hoc-signed argv helper; the only route that works with ad-hoc + no paid account, is supported/non-deprecated, and needs no caller-code check. SMAppService.daemon/SMJobBless out (SDK: LaunchDaemons must be notarized; ad-hoc daemons fail per DTS). AEWP (dlsym, deprecated, Swift-unavailable) kept as shell-free fallback. sudo rejected (DTS: not API). Verified locally: ad-hoc caller checks are worthless (identifier req + Pearcleaner cert-equality both pass for a different binary); do shell script quoting round-trips 21/21 hostile filenames but the /bin/sh inherits env and PS4/BASH_ENV inject code -> pass paths as data in a 0600 request file, not on the shell line, and scrub the helper env. Helper re-runs the same ProtectedPaths policy + (dev,inode) recheck fd-relative no-follow as root (avoids F-0002/F-0012/F-0014). Report: docs/research/feasibility-privileged.md; journal M-0047; M-0001 +2 lessons.

log.detail: Scope split from T-0070 (feas-apple-apps): restore points / APFS local snapshots…

sessions.summary: Feasibility done. Recommend ONE removal engine in Sources/Safety with two sinks: keep the full v1 TrashBatch pre-flight (canonicalize, ProtectedPaths containment, (dev,ino) re-check, keep-expansion, mount/SF_RESTRICTED/locked refusal); hardcore mode changes only the sink to a fd-relative depth-first remover (open O_NOFOLLOW_ANY, openat O_NOFOLLOW, unlinkat/AT_REMOVEDIR, never crossing st_dev, per-item {path,errno}). Verified on scratch fixtures + XNU/removefile source: do NOT use removefile(3)/removefileat (full-path fts; as root it chflags-clears UF_IMMUTABLE, breaking F-0024/F-0070), FileManager.removeItem or rm. AT_RESOLVE_BENEATH/AT_NODELETEBUSY are macOS 26 only, AT_UNIQUE 26.x, so on the macOS-14 floor rely on O_NOFOLLOW+openat+unlinkat+own identity check. fd walk is also 2-5x faster than rm/removefile/FileManager and the only one deep-safe (>PATH_MAX) and thread-safe (par8 ~5-8s vs rm ~18-80s on a 154k-entry tree). Restore point: tmutil localsnapshot runs unprivileged and with no TM destination (made+deleted one here, net zero), but fs_snapshot_create needs root + the restricted com.apple.developer.vfs.snapshot entitlement (unreachable), snapshots are purgeable and rollback is whole-volume in Recovery — so offer it as an honest best-effort prompt, never as what makes hardcore safe. History: .deleted outcome, trashedPath null, status 'Deleted permanently - not recoverable', no Undo. Doc: docs/research/feasibility-permanent.md; journal M-0048; M-0001 appended.

tasks.description: Catalog removable Apple apps + leftovers/content (sizes, owners, SIP), exact procedure/risks/revert for sealed /System/Applications removal on macOS 14-26, detection APIs, space saved, SIP-safe alternatives. Output: docs/research/feasibility-apple-apps.md; journal M-0046.

sessions.summary: docs/research/feasibility-apple-apps.md + journal M-0046. Verdict: Apple's /Applications apps (GarageBand/iMovie/iWork/Xcode/Logic) are fully removable via T-0068's helper (not SIP-protected; root:wheel, so even Move to Trash needs root, EACCES proxy verified). Xcode here = 26.29 GB incl. 12.43 GB simulator runtimes in SIP-restricted AssetsV2 (simctl only) and 6.05 GB CoreSimulator/Caches; MAS installs leave a pkgutil receipt (appstoreagent). Sealed /System/Applications: impossible while SIP+auth-root on; 65 bundles = 0.73 GB total, daemons live elsewhere, updates restore them, old sealed snapshot likely keeps the bytes. Detection verified without root: csr_check(1<<1)/(1<<11) via @_silgen_name + IOKit 'Sealed'. Recommend: per-app Apple profiles JSON; sealed apps = honest status + SIP-safe alternatives + hardcore-only user-run guide; no automated mount/bless in M7. Side finding: 3,614 stale LaunchServices records from test fixtures (comment on T-0046).

tasks.description:
**Module `hardcore-ui`.** Design: `docs/DESIGN-debloat.md` §1 (all), §2.6 (restore-point box), §3.6 (admin rows), §6.3 (revision r2).

**Owned paths:** `Sources/MacontrolUI/{Shell,Clean,DiskMap,Uninstall,History}/**`; `Tests/MacontrolUITests/**` except files named `Debloat*` or `Sealed*`.

**Brief:** the always-visible "Hardcore mode" checkbox in the toolbar (last trailing item, every screen, `.help` tooltip with the r2 texts), the turn-on modal (three bullets + "Back up first", NO checkbox; red "Turn On Hardcore Mode" with no shortcut is the confirmation; Return and Esc cancel), the red banner while on, every destructive surface's copy and colour per the §1.4 table ("Frees up to X", red strip "Permanent: skips the Trash" inside permanent sheets, D4 items listed apart under "Moved to the Trash" with reasons and excluded from X), the result reporting the MEASURED change of `VolumeSummary.available` (+ snapshot line when below half the estimate; "Partly deleted … the rest is in the Trash" text), History (permanent batches without Undo; restore-point line with the rollback clause; helper-trashed `asAdministrator` items without Undo and with the Finder text; batch Undo skips them), the unchecked restore-point box (disabled below 1 GB available), "Admin" rows only in Clean and Uninstall (Debloat via debloat-catalog) with the prompt note without "once" and, in Trash mode, Finder's password-on-empty note, and `AppModel.live()` wiring (`PrivilegedLauncher.bundled()` → Clean/Uninstall/Debloat models only, never `DiskMapModel`; `recoverPrivilegedResults()` at launch). Mode captured when a confirmation opens. Never persisted.

**Acceptance** (§6.3 hardcore-ui)
1. Toggle inside the window on all six screens at 900x600 and 1600x1000, light and dark; banner visible while on (NSView-tree assertions).
2. Tooltip, modal (three bullets, no checkbox), banner and §1.4 strings exactly as the design.
3. Off at launch; no `UserDefaults` write when toggling (test).
4. Return/Esc cancel the modal; Return in every confirmation sheet removes nothing, both modes (hosted-window key events).
5. A confirmation keeps its opening mode after the toggle changes.
6. Permanent sheets show the red strip; D4 items listed under "Moved to the Trash" with their reason, left out of X.
7. Result: measured free-space change (injected before/after `VolumeSummary`), snapshot line below half, "Partly deleted" text.
8. History: permanent batch status, no Undo, not in "in the Trash"; restore-point line with rollback clause; helper-trashed items without Undo + Finder text, batch Undo skips them; demo has one permanent and one helper-trashed batch.
9. Restore-point box: unchecked; disabled below 1 GB available (injected); create only when ticked (injected); failure asks before deleting.
10. With a launcher: admin rows in Clean/Uninstall selectable + badge + sheet notes (no "once"; Finder note in Trash mode); Disk Map keeps v1 "Needs admin" even with a launcher (`DiskMapModel` has no launcher parameter); without a launcher: v1 everywhere.

12. Snapshots attached; full `swift test` green.

comments.author: build-sealed-apps
comments.text: Finding for the UI test helpers (hardcore-ui owns Tests/MacontrolUITests and Shell; SnapshotRenderer.swift has no listed owner). runHeadless() stops focus stealing, but windows still appear on the user's screen: AppKit constrains a TITLED window when it is ordered in, so setFrameOrigin(-20000,-20000) + orderFrontRegardless() leaves it at (0,0), the bottom-left of the display. Probe: titled window frame (0,0,400,332) after orderFrontRegardless; a borderless window, or an NSWindow subclass whose constrainFrameRect(_:to:) returns its input, stays at -20000, and CGWindowListCreateImage still captures it (4,733 of 5,360 samples had the content colour). Affected: SnapshotRenderer.png for every sized shot ([.titled, .fullSizeContentView]), Snapshot.largestScrollView (CleanSnapshotTests.swift:68) and MinimumSizeTests.swift:14. Suggested fix, 10 lines, in SnapshotRenderer.runHeadless() (every UI test calls it before making a window; the app calls it only for --snapshot): a one-time method_setImplementation on NSWindow.constrainFrameRect(_:to:) returning the frame unchanged. The patch is at scratchpad build-sealed-apps/offscreen-windows.patch. I used it uncommitted for my three full-suite runs, so they put nothing on screen. The Sealed* tests do not depend on it: they use their own non-constraining window and borderless shots. Also: Color.sealedWarning in SealedGuideSheet.swift is a local red text colour (6.8:1 light, 5.8:1 dark from pixels). Tell me, or leave a note, when Theme.dangerText lands, and it switches to that.

tasks.title: Permanent delete engine in Safety: fd-relative remover, removal pre-flight, restore point
tasks.description:
**Module `permanent-engine`** (Safety). Design: `docs/DESIGN-debloat.md` §2 (all), §3.6 (the three passes), §6.3 (revision r2); evidence `docs/research/feasibility-permanent.md`.

**Owned paths:** `Sources/Safety/{RemovalEngine (new),TrashBatch,TrashService,TrashJournal,RestorePoint,ProtectedPaths,ProtectedLocations}.swift`; `Tests/SafetyTests/**` except `SinkAudit*` and `Privileged*`; `Tests/SafetyAttackTests/Permanent*.swift`.

**Brief:** `TrashService.remove(_:mode:…)`. Permanent mode = TRASH THEN ERASE (r2: ux 4, sec 4): a folder (incl. `.app`) is moved to the Trash with v1's sink (identity checked before and after, T-0053), then `RemovalEngine.erase(trashed:identity:)` empties it in the Trash; a file is one `RemovalEngine.unlink` in place. The erase does not re-apply the policy to the Trash path (it would refuse `~/.Trash`). Single-thread fd-relative depth-first walk (`open(O_NOFOLLOW_ANY)` parent, identity on the fd, `openat(O_NOFOLLOW)` descent, read-all-then-unlink, never cross `st_dev`, never list a dataless folder, `unlinkat(AT_REMOVEDIR)` up, per-entry `{path, errno}` failures; a partial erase leaves the rest in the Trash: "Partly deleted … the rest is in the Trash as "<name>""). No in-place fallback when a volume has no Trash. `EPERM` on an `.app` Trash move → App Management message, nothing changed. `removalBlocker(inside:)` replaces `lockedItem(inside:)`. Trash-only rule (D4): iCloud, dataless, and the new `ProtectedLocations.trashOnly` list (Notes group container + container, AddressBook, Calendars, Safari, MobileSync/Backup) go to the Trash in permanent mode, with sheet reasons. `systemNeverTouch` gains `/Library/Preferences/SystemConfiguration`, `/Library/Preferences/OpenDirectory`, `/Library/Application Support/Apple`, `/Library/Apple`, `/Library/Developer/CommandLineTools` (r2: sec 3b). `TrashItem.requiresGone` (lstat before pre-flight; anything there → "Not removed, because <name> is still there.") and the three passes of §3.6 in `remove` (in-process, one `PrivilegedRouting.run` call for set-aside `.needsAdministrator` items, deferred items after) against the stubbed routing. `.deleted` outcome, `JournalEntry.trashedPath == nil`, `restorePoint`, `asAdministrator` (absent → false); `undo(batch:)` keeps its v1 signature and skips permanent and asAdministrator lines. `RestorePoint.create()` runs `/usr/bin/tmutil localsnapshot` with an argv array. Never `removefile`, `removeItem`, `rm`, `chflags`.

**Acceptance**
1. Every applicable v1 `TrashServiceTests` / `SafetyAttackTests` case re-run in permanent mode with `Sandbox.tree` after == before minus intended.
2. §2.7 cases: leaf/mid-tree symlink canary, folder swapped for a link mid-walk, mounted 20 MB APFS image, 300-level tree, deep locked file, unwritable subfolder (`needsAdministrator`), iCloud-path item (fixture Trash); r2: entry 500 of 1,000 fails → original path gone, rest in fixture Trash with the message; `.app` Trash move EPERM → message, tree unchanged; `requiresGone` present → not touched, both modes; each `trashOnly` path → fixture Trash; each new `systemNeverTouch` path refused; three passes in order against a routing stub, and a stub throwing `.cancelled` for a root-owned bundle leaves every leftover untouched, both modes.
3. Six deliberate-bug proofs: no `O_NOFOLLOW`, no identity re-check, ignore `st_dev`, `removefile`, unlink-while-readdir, erase in place instead of after the Trash move.
4. v1 journal fixtures decode; undo skips permanent and asAdministrator entries.
5. `RestorePoint` parser tested on captured output; live call only with `MACONTROL_TMUTIL=1`.
6. Bench note: a 150k-entry APFS clone deleted, time in the task comment.
Merge to main as soon as approved (playbook O3): privileged-helper rebases on it.

comments.author: build-permanent-engine
comments.text:
Build done on feat/permanent-engine (391f195, 263e913, 7e3a77d, 38cccf5, merge of main c434a9a, e208462). Full swift test 369/369 (3 runs of 368 after the last test file was added, 66-90 s each under a watchdog, then one final run 369/369 after e208462); gated MACONTROL_DISK_IMAGE_TESTS=1 41/41; no macontrol-tests-* folder left by these suites (set diff before/after).

Deviations from the design, each deliberate: (a) RemovalEngine.unlink(canonical:identity:) is named deleteFile(canonical:identity:), because the sink audit's rule unlink(?!at) forbids that token in every file. (b) The erase and the removal-blocker walk are loops over an explicit stack, still one fd per depth level: the recursive version crashed the test process with SIGBUS on the 300-level tree, since TrashService runs on a DispatchSerialQueue thread with a 512 KB stack (v1 lockedItem had the same latent crash past about 250 levels). (c) The App Management EPERM message applies in both modes (the Trash move is the same). (d) Items with requiresGone are processed after all items without it, so a bundle goes before its leftovers wherever they live. (e) removalBlocker in permanent mode also sends a folder it cannot open or list to needsAdministrator (fail closed), not only an unwritable one.

Deliberate-bug proofs (targeted runs, each restored with git checkout -- Sources): drop O_NOFOLLOW_ANY in deleteFile -> aSwapJustBeforeAnInPlaceDeleteMustNotReachTheLinkedFile fails (the Documents hard-link name is deleted); drop O_NOFOLLOW in the walk -> aFolderSwappedForALinkMidWalkIsRemovedAsTheLink fails (outcome turns partial: the fstat re-check still stops the follow), and with the re-check also dropped the canary folder is emptied; skip identity in erase -> aFolderSwappedInTheTrashBeforeTheEraseIsNotErased fails; skip identity in deleteFile -> aFileSwappedBeforeItsDeleteIsNotDeleted fails; ignore st_dev -> aVolumeMountedDuringTheEraseIsNeverEntered fails (canary on the mounted image deleted, 'Resource busy'); removefile in RemovalEngine.swift -> SinkAuditTests fails ('Safety/RemovalEngine.swift: removefile'); erase in place instead of after the Trash move -> anEraseThatStopsHalfwayLeavesTheRestInTheTrash fails (original path keeps 500 entries); erase before the post-move check -> aFolderSwappedInsideTheMoveIsNeverErased fails (Documents folder erased). Also proven: new systemNeverTouch paths, trashOnly in the sink, requiresGone, the deferral (threePassesInOrder), the writability row, the unreadable-folder row, the App Management mapping. NOT provable here: read-while-unlink. A C probe that unlinks during readdir left 0 of 1k/10k/30k entries on APFS and 0 of 1k/10k on HFS+, and the 10k test passes with that mutation; the read-all-first rule stays because POSIX leaves it unspecified.

Bench (acceptance 8): 147,000 files in 7,070 folders (Xcode-shaped, 1 file in 10 holding 8 KiB), an APFS clone, remove(.permanent) = pre-flight walk + Trash move + erase, debug build, load average 8-14: 18.9 s, 14.8 s, 14.7 s (MACONTROL_BENCH_PERMANENT=1 swift test --filter PermanentBenchTests).

Not run: the live RestorePoint test (MACONTROL_TMUTIL=1). It makes a real snapshot of this Mac, which pins deleted blocks on a disk that has about 6.7 GiB free; the parser is tested on the output captured by feas-permanent. Dataless (SF_DATALESS) paths are untested: no fixture can make an evicted file without a File Provider.

B2: git merge-tree with feat/privileged-helper, feat/hardcore-ui, feat/sealed-apps: no text conflicts (feat/debloat-catalog conflicts with main already in Uninstaller/AppBundle.swift, not mine). ProtectionPolicy.lockedItem(inside:) is gone; feat/privileged-helper calls it in PrivilegedExecutor.swift:157, see my comment on T-0075. A cold scratch merge with feat/hardcore-ui (66bcb08) built and passed 368/368, but that branch changes only one test line so far.

comments.author: build-privileged-helper
comments.text: From privileged-helper (feat/privileged-helper): (1) Contract request, additive: TrashItem needs 'public var bundleIdentifier: String?' (init parameter, default nil). The helper's first-component rule allows com.apple.*/Apple*/. names only when they start with the item's bundle identifier; without the field, PrivilegedRouting sends nil and Apple leftovers in /Library pass only through PrivilegedScope.appleContent. You own TrashService.swift, so please add it; I wire it in routing and Uninstaller on rebase. (2) Audit trap: the rule unlink(?!at) bans the token 'unlink' outside RemovalEngine.swift, so a call 'RemovalEngine.unlink(canonical:identity:)' from TrashBatch or PrivilegedExecutor fails the sink audit. Please name the file entry point without 'unlink' (e.g. erase(file:identity:)). (3) The helper's permanent sink is the trash sink, then your erase on the trashed copy; until you merge it stops in the Trash with 'Moved to the Trash, but not deleted yet. Empty the Trash to finish.' Tests that flip when you merge: PrivilegedExecutorTests.permanentDeletesAfterTheTrashMove and liveConfigurationIsAProtectedLocation (systemNeverTouch additions, sec 3b), both withKnownIssue. (4) PrivilegedRouting.run returns exactly one outcome per item. Cancel -> .failed('Not removed: the administrator password was not given.'); items with keep -> .failed; no expectedIdentity or a non-canonical path -> .refused(.identityChanged); out of PrivilegedScope -> .refused(.protectedLocation). It writes its own journal lines (asAdministrator true) through TrashJournal. (5) I changed one line in TrashService.swift: recoverPrivilegedResults() now calls PrivilegedRouting.recover(journalURL:). (6) Uninstaller now makes ONE remove call with requiresGone on every leftover, so on main without your requiresGone check a leftover of an app whose bundle stays would be trashed: merge order must be engine first. (7) Fork-without-exec finding: a forked child using Swift/Foundation crashed 9/100 in _os_log_preferences_refresh (os_log region is VM_INHERIT_NONE); main.swift now marks every region VM_INHERIT_COPY before the fork (100/100).

tasks.title: Privileged helper: admin-authorized root deletes with root-side re-validation
tasks.description:
**Module `privileged-helper`.** Design: `docs/DESIGN-debloat.md` §3 (all), §6.3 (revision r2); evidence `docs/research/feasibility-privileged.md`.

**Owned paths:** `Sources/Safety/Privileged*.swift` (Launcher, Request, Scope, Executor, Routing), `Sources/PrivilegedHelper/**` (main.swift, LaunchdSystem.swift), `scripts/bundle-app.sh`, `Sources/Uninstaller/{Uninstaller,Models,UninstallActions,LaunchdControl}.swift`; `Tests/SafetyTests/Privileged*.swift`, `Tests/SafetyAttackTests/Privileged*.swift`, `Tests/UninstallerTests/{UninstallFlow,Admin}*.swift`.

**Brief:** `NSAppleScript` (main actor, fixed source, argv as an Apple-event list) → `do shell script … with prompt … with administrator privileges` → `Contents/Helpers/macontrol-priv` (hardened runtime, ad-hoc or self-signed). App: `scrubEnvironment()` (called by main.swift; the launcher only checks the allowlist and throws `.launchFailed` otherwise), 0700 request folder, 0600 `request.json`, SHA-256 in argv; after `do shell script` returns, open `result.jsonl` ONCE (`O_NOFOLLOW`), require regular + `st_uid == 0` + `st_nlink == 1`, poll that fd (never the path); pid line from the child within 5 s; `kill(pid,0)` liveness; journal lines as results arrive (`asAdministrator: true`); `recoverPrivilegedResults()` merges only root-owned single-link result files. Request: ops `trash` | `permanent` only (NO `restore`, r2: sec 2); per-item optional `bundleIdentifier` and `requiresGone`. Helper: clear env, foreground checks (owner/mode/hash/size → exit 65/77), create result file `O_EXCL`, then `fork()` via `@_silgen_name` with no exec, `setsid`, stdio to /dev/null; the child works from the checked bytes in memory (r2: sec 1). Per item: `PrivilegedScope` (+ first-component rule: refuse names below F starting with `com.apple.`, `Apple` or `.` unless they start with the item's `bundleIdentifier` or lie in `PrivilegedScope.appleContent`) → full `ProtectionPolicy` with `home:` and `journal:` of the requesting user spelled out → identity → `removalBlocker` → `requiresGone` (ENOENT) → LaunchDaemon: `launchctl print system/<Label>`, bootout only on an exact `path = <plist>` line, else remove the file without bootout ("stops at the next restart") → sink: trash (`renameatx_np` into `<home>/.Trash`, then `fstatat` identity check, rename back + `identityChanged` on mismatch) or permanent (trash sink, then `RemovalEngine.erase`; files `unlink`). Routing request builder for pass 2 of §3.6 (one request per `remove` call). Uninstaller: `uninstall(_ jobs:mode:)` batch (pre-checks, quits, bootouts per app, skip failing apps; then ONE `remove` call with each bundle followed by its leftovers carrying `requiresGone` = bundle; the v1 two-batch code goes), single-app wrapper, no blocker for root-owned bundles with a launcher, admin leftovers allowed, receipts area, `isPreselected` change, `UninstallActions.remove`.

**Acceptance** (§3.9, §6.3)
1. Request round trip with the 21 hostile names; 65/77 cases; no `restore` op in the type; `PrivilegedScope` table incl. `/private/etc/sudoers`, `/Library/Keychains/x`, `/Applications`, receipts `..`/subfolder, another user's home, `com.apple.loginwindow.plist`, `.GlobalPreferences.plist`, `SystemConfiguration/preferences.plist`, `Application Support/Apple/ParentalControls/x` refused; `com.apple.dt.Xcode.plist` (with bundleIdentifier) and `Apple Loops/Apple/x` (appleContent) allowed.
2. Executor (DEBUG-injected system root, euid and result-owner) on a TemporaryDirectory: both sinks with `Sandbox.tree` diffs, Trash collision names, post-rename swap renamed back, `requiresGone`, LaunchDaemon print match/mismatch via injected runner.
3. Built helper run directly (non-root, debug): detaches, pid/result/done; a hook rewrites `request.json` after the foreground check and outcomes still match the original; `kill -9` → `helperStopped` for the rest; orphaned root-owned result merged exactly once; user-owned or hard-linked result ignored.
4. AppleScript source equals the design constant; `scrubEnvironment` allowlist exact; launcher throws `.launchFailed` on an unscrubbed env; `PrivilegedLauncher.bundled(` only in `Shell/AppModel.swift`; grep test: no `homeDirectoryForCurrentUser`/`NSHomeDirectory`/`applicationSupportDirectory`/`defaultJournalURL`/defaulted-home policy in helper code.
5. Eight deliberate-bug proofs: scope check, hash check, `O_EXCL`, child reopening request.json, first-component rule, systemNeverTouch additions, post-rename identity check, root's home (item `<home>/Library/Caches/com.apple.bird/x` with `bundleIdentifier: com.apple.bird`).
6. `codesign -dv` on the bundled helper: `flags=0x10002(adhoc,runtime)`, identifier `dev.macontrol.Macontrol.priv`; `codesign --verify --strict --deep` on the app.
7. `Uninstaller.uninstall(jobs)` with injected actions: one `remove` call for N apps; leftovers carry `requiresGone`; failing app skipped, others go on; root-owned bundle fixture uninstalled with an injected launcher; receipts; without a launcher v1 errors unchanged.
Rebase on permanent-engine once it merges; run the executor tests against the real engine before review.
