comments.author: challenge-security
comments.text:
Review security of docs/DESIGN-debloat.md (section "## Review: security", 12 issues: 3 high, 3 medium, 1 low-med, 5 low). Issues for this task:
- #1 (high): the detached child reopens request.json and re-executes the helper from proc_pidpath, both in user-owned folders, after the password. Parse and hash once, then fork()+setsid() (Swift marks fork unavailable; @_silgen_name("fork") works, verified-locally) and keep the request in memory. Test: rewrite request.json after the foreground check, outcomes unchanged.
- #2 (high): op restore lets user-writable records (journal, result.jsonl, priv/* recovery) pick a root rename into system folders. Drop restore for v0.2, or require a root-owned ledger match on (dev, ino, original path) plus a root-owned from. The app opens result.jsonl once and checks st_uid == 0, regular, st_nlink == 1.
- #3 (high): PrivilegedScope refuses first components starting com.apple. or Apple unless they start with the request's bundleIdentifier or are apple-apps.json paths (a constant here, test that every catalog path is in it).
- #4 (medium): for a folder, root permanent = trash sink then RemovalEngine on the trashed item; test that a cancelled admin dialog for a root-owned bundle touches no leftover.
- #6 (medium): the root's-home bug proof is vacuous (scope refuses ~/Documents first). Use <home>/Library/Caches/com.apple.bird/x, and test that the helper sources contain no homeDirectoryForCurrentUser/applicationSupportDirectory/defaultJournalURL.
- #8 (low): the launcher only asserts the env allowlist (scrub happens in main.swift at launch).
- #9 (low): after renameatx_np into the Trash, check identity again and put back on mismatch (v1 T-0053).
- #11 (low): boot out system/<Label> only when launchctl print shows this plist's path.

comments.author: build-hardcore-ui
comments.text: From hardcore-ui (T-0073), one additive contract ask for Uninstaller: the restore point's name. DESIGN §2.6 records it on every journal line of the batch, and Clean/Disk Map pass it to TrashService.remove(restorePoint:). Uninstaller.uninstall(_:leftovers:mode:) and uninstall(_ jobs:mode:) take none, and UninstallActions.remove is ([TrashItem], DeletionMode). Please add restorePoint: String? = nil to both uninstall entry points and thread it to remove (e.g. remove: ([TrashItem], DeletionMode, String?) in live(), or a stored var on the batch). Until then UninstallModel makes the snapshot before the uninstall (so the rollback exists), but its journal lines have no restorePoint and History shows no restore-point line for uninstall batches (marked ponytail in UninstallModel.confirmUninstall). Also: UninstallModel.canUseAdministrator reads Uninstaller.canUseAdministrator; admin leftovers become selectable in the UI only then, so Leftover.isPreselected / the .needsAdministrator throw flips on your side are what make them actually go.

comments.author: build-debloat-catalog
comments.text:
debloat-catalog (T-0076) notes for your side of the seam, from feat/debloat-catalog:
1. Receipts: Xcode's profile makes /private/var/db/receipts/com.apple.pkg.Xcode.{plist,bom} leftovers (evidence .appleProfile, needsAdministrator on a real Mac). Until uninstall's allowed-area check accepts <systemRoot>/private/var/db/receipts/<file>, a chosen receipt makes uninstall throw refused(Outside the Library folders) and the whole Xcode job is skipped. Today this cannot happen in the app (receipts are root-owned, so not selectable without a launcher); my UI fixture makes the receipts folder 0555 for that reason. Please flip it with the launcher, as §3.6 says.
2. LeftoverFinder no longer emits .contentLibrary (criterion 3). The case still lives in your Models.swift and UninstallModel+Demo.swift (hardcore-ui) uses it; remove it or keep it, your call.
3. DebloatModel does not rely on Leftover.isPreselected: its default is evidence.preselected && note == nil, and admin items are selectable only when uninstaller.canUseAdministrator. So your isPreselected flip changes Uninstall, not Debloat.
4. Debloat calls uninstaller.uninstall(jobs, mode:) exactly once per run (tested by counting calls through an injected closure) and relies on your per-app skip: a job that throws goes to skipped, the rest still run. On a cancelled dialog it expects the bundle outcome to be anything but .trashed/.deleted and no leftover to move (tested against the current stub, both modes).

comments.author: build-permanent-engine
comments.text:
From permanent-engine (T-0074, branch feat/permanent-engine, merges first per O3). Two things your branch needs when you rebase:
1) ProtectionPolicy.lockedItem(inside:) is gone, replaced by ProtectionPolicy.removalBlocker(inside: path, forErase: Bool) -> RemovalBlocker? (DESIGN-debloat 2.2). Your PrivilegedExecutor.swift:157 calls lockedItem and will not compile after the merge. Replacement: switch ProtectionPolicy.removalBlocker(inside: path, forErase: op == .permanent && <not trash-only>) { case .refused(let r)?: return .refused(r); case .dataless?: <Trash only, no erase>; case nil: break }. As root the writability row never fires; locked, restricted/SF_*, other-volume rows still do. ProtectionPolicy.init now has no journal default: init(home:journal:) (you already spell both).
2) The erase, for your permanent sink: RemovalEngine().deleteFile(canonical:identity:) for a non-folder in place, RemovalEngine().erase(trashed: <Trash URL>, identity:) after your renameatx_np move. Both return .removed | .changed (nothing touched) | .failed([Failure{path, reason}]). Messages the UI parses (hardcore-ui): .changed after the move -> 'Moved to the Trash, but not deleted: it changed there. Empty the Trash to finish.'; .failed -> TrashBatch.partlyDeleted(failures, trashName:) ('Partly deleted. N items inside could not be removed; the rest is in the Trash as "<name>". ...'). Trash-only (D4): ProtectionPolicy.trashOnlyReason(canonical:) != nil or an SF_DATALESS item -> Trash move only. Also: remove() now runs your PrivilegedRouting.run(items, mode:, launcher:, batch:, journalURL:, home:, restorePoint:) for pass 2 exactly as the contract says; an item your route does not answer keeps its .needsAdministrator refusal. Scratch merge feat/permanent-engine + feat/privileged-helper: no text conflicts (git merge-tree), only the lockedItem call breaks.

comments.author: fix-signing-ci-1
comments.text: From T-0081 (feat/signing-ci 287ab03), for scripts/bundle-app.sh, which you own. User decision M-0045: bundle-app.sh signs with the self-signed certificate when this Mac has it, ad hoc otherwise. Not wired yet. The one-line default is SIGN_IDENTITY="${SIGN_IDENTITY:-$(scripts/signing-identity.sh)}" (prints "macontrol Self-Signed" or "-", unlocks the dedicated keychain first so codesign never prompts), and the header comment ("Set SIGN_IDENTITY to an Apple Development identity") should point to docs/RELEASING.md. Once that lands, your acceptance 6 (`flags=0x10002(adhoc,runtime)` on the helper) is false on a Mac that has the certificate: there it is `flags=0x10000(runtime)` and the designated requirement is `identifier "dev.macontrol.Macontrol.priv" and certificate leaf = H"2b40c1b6e6a9e1c2f8c7f8a4aa582ed22010cbaf"`. Please accept either shape in the check (identifier and runtime flag fixed, adhoc only when signing-identity.sh prints "-"). CI release builds always sign with the certificate (release.yml sets SIGN_IDENTITY).

comments.author: fix-permanent-engine-1

tasks.title: Debloat section: Apple app profiles (apple-apps.json) and the Debloat screen
tasks.description:
**Module `debloat-catalog`.** Design: `docs/DESIGN-debloat.md` §4 (all), §6.3 (revision r2); evidence `docs/research/feasibility-apple-apps.md` (Xcode profile, catalog table).

**Owned paths:** `Sources/Uninstaller/{AppleProfiles (new),LeftoverFinder,AppBundle,SimRuntime (new)}.swift`, `Sources/Uninstaller/Resources/**`, `Sources/MacontrolUI/Debloat/Debloat*.swift`; `Tests/UninstallerTests/{AppleProfile,LeftoverFinder,SimRuntime}*.swift`, `Tests/MacontrolUITests/Debloat*.swift`.

**Brief:** `apple-apps.json` (format §4.3) with the verified Xcode profile (§4.4) and unverified profiles for GarageBand, Logic, MainStage, iMovie, Pages, Numbers, Keynote, Final Cut Pro, Motion, Compressor; a fail-closed validator; every catalog `/Library` path mirrored in `PrivilegedScope.appleContent` (test here; hand the constant edit to privileged-helper's owner if it is missing); `LeftoverFinder` emits `.appleProfile` leftovers and receipt files instead of the hard-coded `contentLibraries`. `SimRuntime` lists and deletes simulator runtimes by running `/Library/Developer/PrivateFrameworks/CoreSimulator.framework/Versions/A/Resources/bin/simctl` at that fixed path with an argv array and `DEVELOPER_DIR=<plan bundle>/Contents/Developer` (NOT `xcrun`, NOT Xcode's `usr/bin/simctl` bash shim, which may run `xcodebuild -runFirstLaunch`; verified-locally in r2). Debloat screen: subtitle "Removes Apple's App Store apps (…) and what they install. macOS's built-in apps are locked by macOS.", headline of what exists, APP ROWS START UNTICKED, per-row "selected of total" sizes with unselected content listed, runtime row under "Deleted by Xcode's tool, not moved to the Trash" (unticked in Trash mode, selected in hardcore mode, never preselected when another Xcode is installed), footer split "X to the Trash · Y deleted now" / "Frees up to X", `Containers`/`Group Containers` leftovers not preselected in hardcore mode ("May hold documents you made in <App>."), git/clang "Also happens" note with Copy (`sudo xcode-select --reset`) when `readlink(/private/var/db/xcode_select_link)` points inside the bundle; `Remove…` → mode-aware `TrashSheet`. `DebloatModel` flow (§4.6): plans → simulator runtimes FIRST (a runtime failure keeps Xcode: "Simulator runtimes couldn't be deleted, so Xcode was kept …") → ONE `uninstaller.uninstall(jobs, mode:)` call (one admin dialog at most) → cancel/still-installed message "Simulator runtimes were deleted; Xcode is still installed."; one app failing does not stop the next. Selecting a Part of macOS row shows `SealedAppPanel` (sealed-expert's view).

**Acceptance**
1. Validator rejects each §4.3 rule (one case each); the shipped file passes; every catalog `/Library` path is in `PrivilegedScope.appleContent`.
2. Xcode fixture plan (systemRoot fixture) matches §4.4/§4.5: app rows unticked; runtime row by mode, not preselected with a second Xcode; Containers/Group Containers not preselected in hardcore mode; `sharedWith` never preselected; unverified-profile items unselected with the note; `neverTouch` never listed; `SF_RESTRICTED` items without a checkbox.
3. `contentLibraries` gone from `LeftoverFinder`.
4. `SimRuntime`: parse a captured `simctl runtime list -j`; argv = fixed CoreSimulator binary + `["runtime","delete",id]`, `DEVELOPER_DIR` of the plan bundle, injected runner; live only with `MACONTROL_SIMCTL=1` (record a `--dry-run` probe in the task).
5. Flow tests with injected `UninstallActions`: runtimes before any Xcode item (deliberate-bug proof: bundle first → test fails); runtime failure keeps Xcode; one `uninstall(jobs)` call per run; cancel message; one app's failure does not stop the next.
6. git/clang note only when the injected readlink points inside the bundle.
7. Snapshots 900x600 and large, light and dark, loading and empty; `$TMPDIR/macontrol-tests-*` count unchanged; fixtures do not register bundles with LaunchServices.

comments.author: fix-debloat-catalog-1
comments.text:
Fix round 1 (fix-debloat-catalog-1), feat/debloat-catalog @ bd32e8f (one commit on e187970). Full swift test 366/366 in 49 suites, 1 known issue (appleContent, T-0075), run twice. The second run used a private TMPDIR and left 0 macontrol-tests-* folders. The shared $TMPDIR gained 47 during my first run, all timestamped while other worktrees' suites were running. 15 deliberate-bug proofs (M21-M35), 3 builds, every one caught by its own test with no stray failures. SS10 (attached by me, the attach call lacked --actor) shows the new confirmation copy.

1 HIGH, fixed. findPlans catches a failed `runtime list`. The row keeps its plan, and `failure` = "Couldn't list its simulator runtimes, so Xcode is kept: without it, nothing could delete them. Try Scan Again." canTick requires failure == nil. Exception: when CoreSimulator's simctl isn't at its fixed path (an Xcode never opened), `list` returns [] without running anything (SimRuntimeTool.isInstalled). Test aFailedRuntimeListKeepsXcode (the reviewer's P4, inverted): no Xcode job, Xcode and PrivateFrameworks stay, GarageBand goes. Proofs: M21 (`try? ?? []` back) and M22 (canTick ignores failure) both caught. noToolMeansNoRuntimes proves the missing-tool check (M33).
2 MEDIUM, fixed as suggested. While runtimes exist and aren't ticked, /Library/Developer/PrivateFrameworks gets the note "Holds the only tool that deletes simulator runtimes. Without it, the X of runtimes left unticked stay on this Mac until you reinstall Xcode." That turns off preselection. Ticking the runtimes clears the note and restores the default, and unticking them again resets any tick (F-0011). Test coreSimulatorWaitsForTheRuntimes covers both modes (M23).
3 MEDIUM, fixed. Before any runtime delete, Xcode is asked to quit (SimRuntimeTool.quit = RunningApps.quit in live, which also quits Simulator inside the bundle; a no-op in every test double). If it stays open, its runtimes and Xcode are kept: "Xcode was skipped: Xcode is still running…". The notes now run in order: "Asks … to quit first", then "Then deletes N simulator runtimes (…) with Xcode's own tool, which shuts down any simulator still running." Tests: anXcodeThatDoesNotQuitKeepsItsRuntimes, notesFollowTheOrderOfTheRun, and runtimesGoFirst… now also asserts the quit comes before the deletes (M24, M26).
4 MEDIUM, fixed. DebloatConfirmation.summary: with helper items it says "Items owned by the system can't be put back from History: drag them out of the Trash in Finder. The rest can be put back from History until then." With runtimes it adds "The simulator runtimes are deleted now and can't be put back." Test trashMessageSaysWhatHistoryCantPutBack (M27).
5 MEDIUM, fixed. totalBytes, bytesToRemove and runtimeBytesToDelete count each URL or runtime id once. beginRemove sends a shared URL once, with the first app, so no two sheet rows share an id, and a runtime is deleted only once. The per-row "selected of total" still shows that row's own content. Tests: sharedContentIsCountedAndSentOnce (P1 inverted; M28, M29 and M34 each fail their own line) and runtimesSharedByTwoXcodesAreDeletedOnce (M35).
6 MEDIUM, fixed at the root in LeftoverFinder.profileItems. When another installed app has the profile's bundle id, every profile item gets "Also used by Xcode-beta, which is installed." 1. HIGH (reachable once T-0075 and T-0073 merge) - the Uninstall screen strands the runtimes. The profile now reaches every plan, and the Uninstall screen gets Xcode's /Library/Developer/PrivateFrameworks (CoreSimulator, the only simctl) preselected with no runtime step and no note. v1's Xcode plan had no /Library/Developer items, so this branch introduces it. On the merge, isPreselected no longer excludes needsAdministrator and a root-owned bundle is no blocker with the helper, and UninstallModel defaults to choices ?? isPreselected (hardcore-ui UninstallModel.swift:278). Probe R1 on the merge: Debloat holds PrivateFrameworks (runtimes=2, chosen=false). The same fixture's Uninstall plan has isPreselected=true and note=nil; uninstall(plan, preselected) removed Xcode.app, CoreSimulator/Caches and PrivateFrameworks with 0 runtime deletes. That is the 12.43 GB AssetsV2 outcome of review 1 #1, one screen over. Fix at the root, in LeftoverFinder/profile: a profile item that holds the runtime tool (PrivateFrameworks) is not preselected while runtimes exist outside a Debloat run (a note that Debloat replaces when its runtime step runs), or Uninstall sends simulatorRuntimes apps to Debloat. The git/clang note is missing there too.

2. MEDIUM - the runtime list is taken at plan time and never taken again before Xcode goes. Probe R3 (branch and merge): a runtime added between beginRemove and confirm (a download finishing) was never deleted; Xcode.app went, PrivateFrameworks went too on the merge, and message=nil. Same class: parse() compactMaps away a deletable entry whose identifier or sizeBytes it can't read, silently. Fix: list again right before the runtime step (after the quit) and keep Xcode when the set differs from the confirmed one; count an unreadable deletable entry as a list failure.

3. MEDIUM (honest copy) - a partly deleted runtime set is reported as not deleted. Probe R2 (runtimes[1] fails): iOS 26.5 (8.49 GB) was deleted (exit 0), then the message is "Simulator runtimes couldn't be deleted, so Xcode was kept: without it, nothing can delete them." and notMoved says "its simulator runtimes couldn't be deleted." Nothing says 8.49 GB are gone for good. aRuntimeFailureKeepsXcodeAndTheOthersGoOn asserts exactly this string. Name what was deleted and what wasn't.

4. MEDIUM (honest copy) - the Trash-mode default sheet (Xcode ticked, runtimes unticked, the default) says "Xcode and what it installed move to the Trash" and none of its notes mentions the 12.43 GB of runtimes that stay (review2-confirm-trash-default-light.png). The only mention is the PrivateFrameworks row note in the list. Add a note: "Its 12.43 GB of simulator runtimes stay on this Mac: only Xcode's tool can delete them."

5. LOW (merge note) - cancelledDialogSaysXcodeIsStillInstalled fails 2/2 on the scratch merge: with one remove call, leftovers are sent with requiresGone, so Set(removed) is bundles + leftovers. The disk-state assertions still hold. Rewrite the "sent" check for the one-batch contract (each leftover carries its bundle as requiresGone).

6. LOW (evidence) - the fix comment's "private TMPDIR left 0" proves nothing. TemporaryDirectory uses NSTemporaryDirectory(), which ignores TMPDIR here: with TMPDIR set to the scratch folder (ps eww shows it on the test process), a fixture printed /private/var/folders/.../T/macontrol-tests-.... tasks.title: Sealed system apps: detection, locked panel and expert guide (no destructive action)
tasks.description:
**Module `sealed-expert`.** Design: `docs/DESIGN-debloat.md` §5.1-5.4, §5.5, §6.3 (revision r2); evidence `docs/research/feasibility-apple-apps.md` D1-D5, S1-S15, "Guide text".

**Owned paths:** `Sources/MacontrolCore/SystemIntegrity.swift`, `Sources/MacontrolUI/Debloat/Sealed*.swift`, `docs/guides/remove-system-apps.md`; `Tests/MacontrolCoreTests/SystemIntegrity*.swift`, `Tests/MacontrolUITests/Sealed*.swift`.

**Brief:** read-only detection (`csr_check` via `@_silgen_name` for bits 1 and 11, `statfs("/")` for `MNT_SNAPSHOT` and the system device; failure = protected); `SealedAppPanel(app:size:)` for a Part of macOS app (size, "locked by macOS" text, Remove-from-Dock instruction, no destructive button) with the "Expert: remove system apps yourself…" button ALWAYS present, in both modes (r2: ux 14; the user asked for "a warning at most"); the expert guide sheet: "Strongly not recommended" header, the r2 risk list (adds "You must turn off FileVault first…" and "The apps stay removed only while these protections stay off…"; S7 space and S13 Time Machine marked "expected, not yet tested"), Time Machine backup first, acknowledgement box, then generated Recovery + Terminal steps for the chosen apps and this Mac's device, with Copy buttons, and the revert steps. Commands use literal absolute paths only, no shell variables, single-quoted (r2: sec 12). SIP-off state skips the Recovery steps and says removal through macontrol waits for verification. **macontrol runs none of these commands.** The helper-driven removal of §5.4 is not part of this task (its SF_RESTRICTED waiver stays compiled out behind `#if MACONTROL_SEALED_REMOVE`).

**Acceptance**
1. Injected `csr_check`: failure → protected; `/dev/disk3s3s1` → `/dev/disk3s3`.
2. SIP-on panel copy exact; no destructive button (view-tree test); expert button present in both modes.
3. Commands only after the acknowledgement; hostile app names round-trip through `/bin/sh -c 'printf %s …'` in the test; no generated line contains `$`; every destructive line ends in `System/Applications/<X>.app'` or `System/Applications/Utilities/<X>.app'` below the mount point.
4. Risk list has the FileVault and "stay removed only while…" bullets; S7/S13 marked expected, not yet tested.
5. SIP-off (injected) state renders as designed.
6. `docs/guides/remove-system-apps.md` mirrors the sheet, each step tagged verified or unverified.
7. Snapshots at 900x600 and large, light and dark.

1. MEDIUM (probe P1): nothing in the generated steps says "stop if a command fails", and nothing checks the mount. If `sudo mount ... '/dev/disk3s3' ~/sysmount` fails (Authenticated Root still on, a stale disk number, or the unverified mount refused on 26), ~/sysmount is an empty folder on the Data volume, `sudo rm -rf` exits 0 without a word, and `sudo bless --mount ~/sysmount --bootefi --create-snapshot` then points at the volume that folder is on. What bless does then is unknown (never run here). Step 4 says "Both commands should say disabled" but not "if either says enabled, stop". Fix: stop-on-error wording in steps 4-6 (and the doc), plus a read-only check before the rm, e.g. `ls '<mnt>/System/Applications/Chess.app'` ("if it says No such file, stop"), or `sudo rm -r` without -f so a missing target shows an error.

'/dev/disk3s3'`, rm and bless with Copy buttons, while its own step 4 says the disk can change after the Recovery restart. Safer default: generate steps 5-7 only when allowsSealedRemoval is true (the reopened guide), and show "The next commands appear here once both protections are off" before that. This also removes the P1 path of running them before Recovery.
3. LOW (probe P2): rootIsSealedSnapshot is computed and never read. With a root that is not a snapshot (flags without MNT_SNAPSHOT, /dev/disk3s3), systemDevice is /dev/disk3s3 and the guide still writes `sudo mount -t apfs '/dev/disk3s3' ~/sysmount` for the volume already mounted at /, then rm and bless (the P1 path). Fix: unavailable when !rootIsSealedSnapshot ("this Mac isn't starting up from a system snapshot; the guide doesn't cover that").
4. LOW: `man bless` on this Mac (Apple silicon) lists `--bootefi` only for EFI systems; its "OPTIONS FOR APPLE SILICON DEVICES" Mount Mode has no `--bootefi` and adds `--user`/`--passpromt` (owner credentials may be prompted). Feasibility S6 quoted the EFI section. Step 7 and undo 1 use `--bootefi`, and the doc cites man bless without saying this. tasks.title: Verify debloat with the user: root run, App Management, Apple installs, sealed procedure in VMs
tasks.description:
**Task `verify-debloat`** (user-assisted verification). Design: `docs/DESIGN-debloat.md` §5.4, §5.5, §6.3 (revision r2). Needs the user: an administrator password, App Store downloads and macOS VM images. **Ask the user before anything that reaches the network** (global rule).

**Owned paths:** `docs/research/verify-debloat.md` only. No source changes.

**Checks**
1. Real root run on this Mac with fixtures under `/Library/Application Support/macontrol-verify-<uuid>`: Move to Trash, permanent delete (Trash move, then erase) through the bundled helper, and a cancelled dialog that touches no leftover, in both modes; a `BASH_ENV`/`SHELLOPTS` canary in the app's environment creates nothing; `request.json` rewritten, and separately the helper file swapped, right after the foreground check: the detached child still acts on the original request.
2. Count dialogs: one multi-app Debloat run (expect one), and two separate actions within five minutes (different argv: does the second prompt?).
3. A real, free App Store app (iMovie), in both modes, with and without App Management granted to Macontrol: record the errno/error text and confirm no half-deleted app is ever left in `/Applications`.
4. GarageBand, iMovie, Pages, Numbers, Keynote installed: check each profile's paths, receipts and sizes; flip `verified` per profile (hand the JSON edit to debloat-catalog's owner or a fix task).
5. Xcode: simulator runtimes deleted BEFORE the bundle with `/Library/Developer/PrivateFrameworks/CoreSimulator.framework/Versions/A/Resources/bin/simctl` (`--dry-run` first; does it ask for admin rights?); after Xcode is removed with `xcode_select_link` pointing into it, does `/usr/bin/git --version` work, and does `sudo xcode-select --reset` fix it?
6. Finder: empty a Trash that holds a helper-trashed root-owned bundle, and drag one back to `/Applications`; record the prompts.
7. Record `launchctl print system/<Label>` output before a bootout (is there a `path = ` line on 26, and on 14/15 in VMs?).
8. Recovery > Restore from Time Machine: does it list a `tmutil` local snapshot on a Mac with no Time Machine destination (VM)?
9. macOS VMs on 14, 15 and 26: run the §5.3 guide and its revert end to end; record `csr_check` values with protections off, space freed, what breaks. If all pass, open a builder task for the §5.4 helper op; if not, record why and keep §5.4 compiled out.

comments.author: uninstall-sort
comments.text:
Branch feat/uninstall-sort, commit 26acec8 on main cb6ffc6 (worktree ~/projects/macontrol-wt/uninstall-sort). swift build + swift test green: 319 tests / 45 suites.
What: segmented All N / User N / System N filter + sort menu (Name A-Z/Z-A, Date Added newest/oldest, Size largest/smallest) under the search field. Sorting is within each kind section; total order (ties by name, then path; no date / no size yet = last in both directions). Size sort runs model.measureAll() (3 walks at a time) keyed on the app list, so unmeasured rows do not stay last. Rows show the date added while date-sorted. System = kind != thirdParty OR bundle id com.apple.* (case-insensitive; com.applesauce is User). Filter combines with search; counts follow the search; filter hiding the selected app deselects it (same guard as search). Empty filter: 'No system apps (match)' + Show All Apps. @AppStorage keys uninstallFilter / uninstallSort; model mirrors via onChange(initial:). Keyboard: opt-cmd-1..3 filter, ctrl-opt-cmd-1..6 sort, via hidden buttons (SwiftUI shortcuts on items of a closed Menu do NOT fire: measured, the first key test failed with Toggle-in-Menu shortcuts only). Uninstaller: InstalledApp.dateAdded (additive, init default nil) = addedToDirectoryDate ?? creationDate.
Side fix: the list's empty states (incl. the old search one) now fill the pane; before, the search field slid to mid-pane (seen in the first empty-state render).
Tests: AppListOrderTests (11 incl. 6 parameterized: name/date/size ordering, input-order independence, filter rules, counts, deselect, measureAll, headless key-event test in a temp-folder defaults suite), InventoryTests.dateAddedIsWhenTheAppArrivedNotWhenItWasMade, UninstallSnapshotTests.filteredAndSortedListRenders x3 light+dark.
Mutation proof (scratchpad/uninstall-sort/mutate.py): 8/8 caught - no path tiebreak, missing values first, kind-only System, filter keeps hidden selection, creationDate first, measureAll no-op, view ignores stored filter, date ties by input order.
Real Mac read-only probe: 94 apps, 27 user / 67 system, 0 without a date; newest-first user apps = Macontrol, Upscayl, Ollama, VS Code, OBS.
Not verified: live app with a real mouse (user is on this Mac, no window was shown); the open sort menu's look (NSMenu cannot be snapshotted headless).

tasks.verdictNotes:
APPROVE (review-uninstall-sort-2, 41d41e5 on 26acec8). swift build + swift test green in the worktree: 320 tests / 45 suites. No new plist in ~/Library/Preferences.

Round 1 item 1 is fixed at the root. Waiters hold no measure slot while they wait, so there is no deadlock. The owner's defer resumes the waiters on every exit path. There is one owner per URL, and a resumed waiter checks the size again before it measures. Deliberate-bug proof: I put back the old one-shot dedupe in a scratch copy, and the race test failed in 8 of 8 runs. The control case never failed. Per case over 3 runs: row-first failed 3/3 and all-first 2/3. Round 1 item 5 is fixed: rotations run forwards and backwards.

1. [decide, carried over] Round 1 items 2, 3 and 4 are still open. They are the user's call before v0.1.1: the sort stays inside each section (Xcode sorts below all 27 user apps under Largest First), the com.apple.* prefix is trusted without a signature check, and there is one sort icon and no menu-bar Sort By. None of them blocks the merge.
2. [nit] A cancelled waiter keeps waiting. The while loop in measureIfNeeded does not check Task.isCancelled. So a row that scrolled away, or a measureAll child after Size sort was left, waits through every later attempt on that app before it returns. It holds no slot, so the only cost is a suspended task. `while !Task.isCancelled, sizes[app.url] == nil, measuring[app.url] != nil` would end it at the next wake-up.
3. [nit, UX] Under Size sort nothing shows that sizes are still being measured. measureAll claims every app at once and walks them in name order, 3 at a time. The list reorders as each size lands, and rows on screen show "–" until their name comes up. I did not time it on this Mac. A "Measuring N of M" line, or accepting this as is, is the user's call.
4. [nit] AppFilter.emptyTitle for .all ("No apps") is never shown, because the .all branch uses ContentUnavailableView.search. Delete that case or use it.
5. [unverified] The 9 hidden shortcut buttons (opacity 0, accessibilityHidden) follow the ⌘F SearchField pattern. With Full Keyboard Access on, they may be invisible Tab stops. Not checked, because checking it would mean changing a system setting. If they are, `.focusable(false)` fixes it.

Checked OK:
- Every comparator gives a total order: name, then path; equal dates or sizes go by name; a missing date or size goes last in both directions.
- Comparators do no disk I/O. dateAdded is read once in AppBundle off the cooperative pool, and sizes are mapped before the sort. The sort reads sizes only for size sorts, so under other sorts a new size redraws only its own row.
- Persistence: @AppStorage with stable raw values, mirrored into the model through onChange(initial:).
- Keyboard: ⌥⌘1-3 and ⌃⌥⌘1-6 do not clash with ⌘1-5, ⌘R, ⌘O or ⌘F. They work only on the Uninstall screen, because RootView switches screens.
- Real Mac, read-only (/Applications, ~/Applications, /System/Applications): 94 listed apps, 27 User / 67 System, all correct. Safari is builtIn, Xcode is appleAppStore, and the 65 /System/Applications apps are builtIn. No thirdParty app has a com.apple id, and no non-com.apple app is in System.
- Dates: all 95 bundles, including Karabiner's hidden one, have addedToDirectoryDate, so the creation-date fallback is never used. The 65 system apps share one day (2026-07-23 local), so they tie and sort by name.
- Snapshots: all 6 attachments are right in light and dark. Fresh renders from 41d41e5 match them. system-empty and system-newest-dark are identical, and the rest differ only at the 1-2 px window edge or in canvas size.
- Scratch merge with current main (036a1fa, T-0072 merged): git merge-tree is clean, the merge builds, and 323/323 tests pass, including AppListOrderTests and SinkAuditTests.
- Both commits are authored by Ege BULUT, with no attribution lines.

Bump it together with the copy. 2. The licensing text contradicts the repo. Since 5657834 the site says "the code will be published once licensing is finalized". main has LICENSE (MIT, 7edf39f), the README has an MIT badge and a "## License: MIT" section, and M-0045 #1 records "License: MIT". If the user changed the decision, journal it in M-0045 and plan the README/LICENSE follow-up. If not, say something like "MIT licensed. The source is published when the preview ends." Either way, the site and the repo must say the same thing. 3. Contrast: .req-note (12.5px, text-2 at opacity .85) measures 3.65:1 in light mode from sampled DPR-2 pixels (fg 131,131,136 on 251,251,253), below 4.5. On the CTA band (#f2f2f7) it is lower still. Dark mode is 5.15. Drop the opacity, or use --text-2 at 13px or larger. The computed-style check missed this because it ignores opacity. SHOULD FIX 4. Hero overclaim: "Everything it removes goes to the Trash first, so you can always put it back." Undo works only while the item is still in the Trash and its old place is free, as the site says itself elsewhere. Suggest "so you can put it back until you empty the Trash". 5. Changelog as rendered from CHANGELOG.md (committed renderer): the intro line appears twice (as the lede and as the first

), the h2s lose their ids and the date styling, and "Open Anyway" loses its install link. The WIP diff drops the intro, but the drop line is duplicated. The WIP also turns FAQ answers into

with

inside . The landing's "How it was measured" link (faq.html#benchmarks) then lands on a collapsed answer, and a heading inside summary loses its heading semantics in VoiceOver. If you keep accordions, open the target of the hash, or keep the FAQ open. 6. Without JS, the file saves as latest.zip, but install.html and faq.html tell the user to run shasum/ditto on ~/Downloads/Macontrol-*.zip. The install page also shows "Expected: listed in /version.json" as plain text. Lazy fix, since deploy-site.sh knows the version and SHA: generate a 307 redirect (permanent: false) from /downloads/latest.zip to /downloads/, or sed the version, size and SHA into the HTML at build time. This gives the versioned file name without JS and removes the duplicate 2.7 MB copy. 7. board-sync.sh now depends on gh with read access to the private repo (active account must be Ege-BULUT) and on cwebp, and it sends deploy output to /dev/null. Before, a board sync needed only vercel. A gh auth or network hiccup now stops board updates, and the log only says "deploy FAILED". At least keep the last lines of stderr in the log. 8. Link previews: og:image is a 1800x1239 WebP of the light UI (not 1200x630, and WebP is not accepted by every scraper). There is no og:type, og:url, twitter:card or canonical, and the docs pages have no og tags at all. NITS 9. `.pager a:only-child { margin-left:auto }` pushes "Previous: Build from source" to the right on changelog.html (seen in the screenshot). Scope it to a[rel=next]. 10. Design: each screenshot shows the whole window at about 40% scale, so the UI text is unreadable at 1440 (Clean list, Uninstall evidence groups, History) and illegible on phones. A premium product page crops or zooms to the part the copy describes. The hero now stacks three grey meta lines under the button (version, requirements, licensing note); move the note out of the hero. The safety step "Protected places are refused" wraps to two lines at 1440, so its body sits lower than its neighbours. 11. deploy-site.sh: the guard `[ -n "${TAG:-}" ]` never fires. With the fake gh, an empty release list returns "null null" through --jq, and the script runs `gh release download null` ("release not found"). When gh fails, `read` hits EOF and set -e exits first. It still fails loudly, so this is dead code: check for TAG = null, or drop the guard. 12. /board/ has no icon link, so /favicon.ico returns 404 (a console error at 360 light). Consider copying assets/icon.png as /favicon.ico. The board's own "OpenLead" kicker is 3.49:1, but that is board styling, out of scope. 13. Not verified on this Mac: Safari's default "Open safe files after downloading" unzips the archive itself, so Safari users may never see the zip that install step 1 and the shasum check refer to. Worth one sentence. VERIFIED OK - Site pages over the 80 loads: 0 console errors, 0 HTTP >= 400, 0 external requests, 0 horizontal overflow, 0 elements past the viewport (checked with body overflow-x unclipped), 0 broken images. Every internal link and anchor resolves. - Computed contrast on all site text is >= 4.5, apart from #3. - Header nav, docs sidebar and pager links all return 200. - Download with JS: "Version 0.1.1 preview, 2.7 MB", saved as Macontrol-0.1.1.zip, SHA-256 matches version.json. Without JS: latest.zip, same SHA, and the version line stays hidden without leaving an empty gap. - GitHub path with the fake gh (ok mode): builds, copies latest.zip, and version.json takes publishedAt from gh. - Facts match v0.1.1: 27 catalog rules; 10-minute quiet period; arm64-only binary; LSMinimumSystemVersion 14.0; bundle id dev.macontrol.Macontrol; journal at ~/Library/Application Support/Macontrol/trash-journal.jsonl, mode 0600; FDA folder list; FDA sheet strings and 1 s polling; Disk Map keys (the handler in DiskMapScreen), ⌘1-⌘5 with 5 sidebar items at the v0.1.1 tag; protected and never-touch lists (.gnupg, photoslibrary, TCC, /System); the launchctl-only sink exception; Low Power and thermal throttling; openat walk; terminate() without force; Library-only leftover search; all BENCHMARKS numbers (2.3x = 1.581/0.683). The "Coming next" copy matches DESIGN-debloat D1 (off at every launch, never stored) and D4 (iCloud items still go to the Trash). "Apple Silicon only", "not notarized" and "preview" are stated plainly. - Design overall: clean, Apple-like, consistent with the app's palette. Dark mode swaps every screenshot through , and the images are small WebPs (28-104 KB) with width/height set and lazy loading below the fold.

comments.author: review-site-2
comments.text:
review-site-2, round 2 on feat/site 609cd96. Verdict: CHANGES. There are 2 should-fix items, both cheap, and the rest are nits. All 13 round-1 items are closed.

Method: I exported 609cd96 with git archive into the scratchpad and ran scripts/deploy-site.sh --dry-run --zip dist/Macontrol-0.1.1.zip with BOARD=.board. That gave 196 files and 51 MB (47 MB of it board attachments) for 4 s of CPU. For the GitHub path I put an offline gh stub on PATH. I served the build with python http.server on 127.0.0.1 and loaded it in headless Chromium at DPR 2: 10 pages x 360/390/768/1440 x light/dark = 80 loads. I checked facts against a v0.1.1 export (git archive v0.1.1), BENCHMARKS.md, CHANGELOG.md and M-0045.

SHOULD FIX
1. The live site takes its images and changelog from the working tree, not from the release it serves. board-sync.sh runs deploy-site.sh in main's checkout on every board sync. SITE_RELEASE pins the page copy and the tag filter pins the zip, but docs/assets/screenshots and CHANGELOG.md come from whatever main has at that moment. main already has 0.2 work (debloat contracts, T-0072). Suppose a merge adds a 0.2.0 section to CHANGELOG.md, or re-renders the screenshots with the always-visible Hardcore toggle (M-0045 #5). The next board sync puts it live beside the 0.1.1 download and "Nothing is deleted permanently in this version". The renderer also opens the newest section, so 0.2.0 would be the entry shown open. This is the same class as round 1 #1. Fix: read both from the served tag. Pipe `git show "v$VERSION:CHANGELOG.md"` into the renderer, and extract the images with `git archive "v$VERSION" docs/assets | tar -x -C "$tmp"`. Today v0.1.1's CHANGELOG.md and docs/assets match main byte for byte (`git diff v0.1.1 main -- CHANGELOG.md docs/assets` is empty), so the page does not change now. The gh path needs the tag locally, so fail loudly when it is missing.
2. Two landing crops are scaled up on Retina, so their UI text is soft. At 1440 px (DPR 2), the treemap crop (1010 px wide) and the Uninstall crop (1036 px) render at 659 CSS px, about 1.3x their pixels. At 768 px they render at 707 CSS px: 1.4x, and 1.06x for Overview and History. A DPR-2 zoom shows the softness next to the sharp Clean crop (1465 px at 659). The three feature shots also show the UI at different scales: treemap and Uninstall at 1.3x the app's point size, Clean at 0.9x. Lazy fix: halve the crops' width/height attributes (treemap 505x570, Uninstall 518x572, Overview/History 665x360) so they never render above 1x, and centre them in their column (margin-inline: auto). Or render the snapshots at 3x.

NITS
3. Part 1 of fix-signing-ci-1's 09:36 comment has no disposition. deploy-site.sh still serves 0.1.x pre-releases: a v0.1.2-rc.1 would become everyone's download, labelled "Version 0.1.2-rc.1 preview". docs/RELEASING.md calls this open, so it needs the orchestrator's or the user's decision. If the answer is "stable only", add --exclude-pre-releases to the list call (the local gh supports it).
4. og.jpg is a piece of the UI with no name or icon, so a link preview in Slack or iMessage shows only the title as text. The image is not clipped: the sunburst's top edge ends about 10 px inside the frame.
5. build.html says "Four commands take you from source to a signed app", but the block has five: clone, cd, build, test, bundle.
6. At 1440 the CTA note wraps and leaves "finalized." alone on the second line (max-width 32em at 13 px). Add text-wrap: balance to .cta p.
7. There is no 404.html, so a mistyped docs URL gets Vercel's default page.

VERIFIED OK
- Round 1 fixes: I checked each one in the code and on the built page.
  - SITE_RELEASE guard, replayed with the offline gh stub. [v0.2.0-rc.1, v0.1.1, v0.1.0] serves 0.1.1 and prints the note. [v0.2.0] and [] exit 1 with "no v0.1.x release". A failing gh exits 1 with gh's error. [v0.1.1, v0.1.0] serves 0.1.1.
  - The licensing copy matches M-0045 09:00:35, and the hero's Trash wording is fixed.
  - Changelog renderer: ids v0.1.1/v0.1.0, dates, a single intro, and the Open Anyway link.
  - Release info is in the HTML without JS, and the pager is fixed.
  - Crops; og, twitter and canonical tags on all 9 site pages.
  - /favicon.ico (32 px ICO).
  - The Safari auto-unzip sentence.
- 80 loads: 0 console errors or warnings, 0 HTTP >= 400, 0 external requests, 0 elements past the viewport, 0 broken images, 0 computed-contrast failures (with opacity multiplied in). Contrast sampled from pixels at DPR 2: lowest 4.54 (light, 15 px grey text on the band), 4.91 for small grey text on the page background, and 5.26 or more in dark mode.
- Download: the hero, CTA, install page and docs sidebar buttons, with and without JS, all save Macontrol-0.1.1.zip. Its SHA-256 (bf97a941...9bab) matches the install page. vercel.json gets the 307 for /downloads/latest.zip.
- Accordions:
  - Without JS, all 13 FAQ answers and both releases are open.
  - With JS, faq#benchmarks opens only that answer, 135 px from the top, and the landing's "How it was measured" link opens it. changelog#v0.1.0 opens 0.1.0.
  - Enter and Space toggle aria-expanded, and a hash change opens #intel.
  - All 17 unique internal links and their anchors resolve.
- Facts new this round, checked against v0.1.1:
  - The All/User/System filter and its definition (isApple: not third-party, or com.apple.*); ⌥⌘1-3 and ⌃⌥⌘1-6; @AppStorage behind "remembers your choice"; apps with no date or size sorted last; the six sort titles.
  - Build: swift-tools-version 6.2; bundle-app.sh's output path and SIGN_IDENTITY; --snapshot; mcscan prints bytes.
  - FDA sheet strings: Continue Without Access, the Limited mode banner, relaunch.
  - Disk Map's cloud confirmation toggle (ReviewSheet), while Clean and Uninstall refuse cloud items. This matches "Cloud needs consent".
  - Apple Silicon only, not notarized, preview and ad hoc signing are all stated plainly.
- Design: clean and consistent with the app in both modes. Dark mode swaps every image. Hierarchy and spacing hold from 360 to 1440. The docs nav turns into pills on phones.

Not verified: a real vercel deploy (the 307, the ICO content type), real gh against GitHub, and the macOS 15 dialog wording on a real quarantined download.

comments.author: fix-site-2
comments.text:
fix-site-2, round 2 on feat/site: 1096c48 (on top of 609cd96). Dispositions for review-site-2's 7 items:

1 FIXED. deploy-site.sh now looks up the release first. It then reads CHANGELOG.md and docs/assets (the screenshots, crops, icon and favicon) from `git archive "v$VERSION"` into a mktemp dir, not from the working tree. If the tag is not in the clone, the deploy stops with "tag vX is not in this clone (git fetch --tags)". Proof in a scratch clone: I committed a "## 0.2.0 DRIFT-MARKER" section to CHANGELOG.md and replaced clean-light.png, both after the tag. The build had 0 markers and a byte-identical clean crop. Mutant (read the working tree again): 1 marker and a different crop. A --zip Macontrol-0.1.9.zip with no tag exits 1 with that message. With the check removed, git archive still fails (exit 128), so the check's job is the readable message, not safety. Side effect: v0.1.0 has no CHANGELOG.md at its tag, so it can no longer be deployed. The copy describes 0.1.1 anyway. Today's page is unchanged: v0.1.1's changelog and assets match main.
2 FIXED. Crop width/height are half the crop box (the screenshots are 2x): treemap 505x570, Clean 732x526 (box trimmed to 1464 px), Uninstall 518x572, Overview/History 665x360. `.shot.crop img` has margin-inline: auto. The reviewer's probe at DPR 2 (88 loads) reports "upscaled: 0". At 1440 the treemap is 505 CSS px and Uninstall 518 in a 659 column, centred, and Clean is 659 (0.9x). At 768 they are 505/518/707/665/665, and at 390 all are 358.
3 DEFAULTED, needs a user yes/no. Tags with a suffix (v0.1.2-rc.1) are never served, from gh (jq filter) or --zip (case check). I did not use --exclude-pre-releases: HANDOVER says v0.1.0 is a GitHub pre-release (the app is a preview), so that flag would stop the deploy today (not checked for v0.1.1: no gh call made). The release workflow on feat/signing-ci marks exactly the `*-*` tags as pre-releases, so the tag suffix matches its rule. Offline gh stub: [v0.1.2-rc.1, v0.1.1, v0.1.0] serves 0.1.1 with a note, [v0.2.0-rc.1, v0.1.1] serves 0.1.1, [v0.1.2-rc.1] alone exits 1 "no v0.1.x release", [v0.1.1] serves it, and a failing gh exits 1. Mutant with the jq filter removed: the case check stops the rc (exit 1). If the user wants rcs served, delete the two suffix lines. RELEASING.md's "open decision" paragraph belongs to T-0081, so I commented there.
4 FIXED. og.jpg is now a branded 1200x630 image: the icon, "macontrol", the hero headline, "Free · macOS 14+ · Apple Silicon" and the Disk Map (sunburst plus inspector) with the site's halo. It is rendered from scripts/og-image.html (the re-render steps are in its header) and kept in site/assets/og.jpg (65 KB), so it follows the copy, not main. The og:image:alt text on all 9 pages describes it.
5 FIXED. build.html: "Five commands".
6 FIXED. `.cta p { text-wrap: balance }`. At 1440 the note's lines are 223 and 240 px, and "finalized." is no longer alone.
7 FIXED. site/404.html uses the docs layout with absolute links only, because Vercel serves it at any depth, plus noindex. I served its body at /docs/nope/deep.html with status 404 (Playwright route): 0 failed subresources, all 13 links return 200, and the download points at /downloads/Macontrol-0.1.1.zip.

Checks: bash -n and zsh -n. The dry run (--zip dist/Macontrol-0.1.1.zip) built 197 files, 51 MB. I served it with python http.server on 127.0.0.1 and ran review-site-2's probe in headless Chromium at DPR 2: 11 pages (with /404.html) at 360/390/768/1440 in light and dark, 88 loads. Results: 0 console errors, 0 HTTP >= 400, 0 external requests, 0 overflow, 0 broken images, 0 contrast failures, 0 upscaled. "oversize" lists phone widths only, which is expected with no srcset. I looked at the screenshots of the features at 1440 light, the CTA, the 404 at 1440 dark and 390 dark, and og.jpg.
Not verified: a real Vercel deploy (that 404.html is served, the 307), real gh against GitHub, and whether v0.1.1 is flagged as a pre-release on GitHub.

tasks.title: Stable self-signed signing and GitHub Actions tag releases
tasks.description: Self-signed codesigning identity in a dedicated keychain (scripts/make-signing-cert.sh, scripts/signing-identity.sh), GitHub Actions release on v* tags (.github/workflows/release.yml), docs/RELEASING.md. User decision M-0045. Branch feat/signing-ci.

comments.author: signing-ci
comments.text: Integration notes: (1) bundle-app.sh wiring stays with the integrator: SIGN_IDENTITY="${SIGN_IDENTITY:-$(scripts/signing-identity.sh)}", and its header comment ('Set SIGN_IDENTITY to an Apple Development identity') should point to docs/RELEASING.md. (2) release.yml checks CFBundleShortVersionString against the tag, so VERSION in bundle-app.sh must be bumped before tagging (main has 0.1.1). (3) The workflow only runs for tags whose commit contains .github/workflows/release.yml, so the first CI release is the first tag after this merges. (4) The two gh secret commands are in docs/RELEASING.md; not run. (5) actions/cache is scoped to the tag ref by GitHub, so it only helps re-runs of the same tag. (6) Runner: macos-26 arm64 GA, Xcode_26.6 17F113 = this Mac's Xcode (runner-images macos-26-arm64 Readme, image 20260907.0351.1).

comments.author: fix-signing-ci-1
comments.text:
fix-signing-ci-1, round 1 resolutions (feat/signing-ci 287ab03 on a143d37). The diff has no Swift. New: scripts/test-signing.sh, which passes. It runs make-signing-cert.sh against fake security/codesign in a scratch HOME, and it checks the pinned requirement with the real codesign. The real search list is unchanged (diffed before and after), and ~/.config/macontrol is untouched. Deliberate-bug proofs, each in a scratch copy: 7 of 7 killed (signing password kept, keychain password stripped, old 4-file state check, lone .p12 accepted, .p12 not removed, wrong pin, old grep guard). The guard lines from release.yml, run under `bash --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail`: the cert-signed build/Macontrol.app passes (rc 0), and an ad hoc re-signed copy fails with the ::error line (rc 1).

1 HIGH: partly fixed. Part 1 needs a user decision.
- Fixed: `make-signing-cert.sh --remove-export` deletes the .p12, the .p12.b64 and MACONTROL_SIGNING_PASSWORD, and keeps the keychain and its password. The script now counts the keychain and signing.env alone as set up. A lone .p12 or .b64 is refused as half-made. Every run that still finds the export prints the gh commands and then the --remove-export line. RELEASING.md step 3 says: back up the .p12 and its password offline, then run it.
- New RELEASING.md sections "Who can sign as macontrol" and "If the key leaks": any program the maintainer runs can sign as macontrol without a prompt. There is no revocation, and a new certificate does not remove old grants, so users must remove Macontrol from Full Disk Access themselves. Rotation also means updating the pin.
- NOT run on this Mac: ~/.config/macontrol still holds the .p12, the .b64 and the password, because the secrets are not set yet. The maintainer runs --remove-export after setting the secrets and making the backup.
- OPEN, user decision: a separate local dev certificate, with the release key only in the GitHub secrets plus an offline backup. That would close repro (b). Until then, the unlocked keychain lets any local process sign.

2 MEDIUM: fixed. The job env has RELEASE_REQUIREMENT = `identifier "dev.macontrol.Macontrol" and certificate leaf = H"2b40c1b6e6a9e1c2f8c7f8a4aa582ed22010cbaf"`. The step runs `codesign --verify --strict --test-requirement="=$RELEASE_REQUIREMENT" build/Macontrol.app`. The leading "=" makes it requirement text, not a file path. test-signing.sh: the pinned leaf passes, a one-digit change fails, and ad hoc fails.

3 MEDIUM: comments posted. T-0075 has the bundle-app.sh one-liner, and acceptance 6 must accept `flags=0x10000(runtime)` plus the certificate requirement when the certificate is present. T-0080 has the pre-release decision and the timing of the copy change. T-0071 (README owner) has README.md:165/178/182. For both, change the copy only after a real Full Disk Access grant has been checked through an update.

4 LOW: fixed. `defaults: run: shell: bash`. The M-0001 correction is in my lesson entry, next to the reviewer's.

5 LOW: fixed. Both cache steps are deleted, and so is the unused `id: build`. RELEASING.md says why.

6 LOW: fixed.
- `persist-credentials: false` and `timeout-minutes: 15`.
- Checkout is pinned to `3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1`, up from @v5. It could not be checked against github.com, because remote lookups are the orchestrator's job. The SHA comes from two independent clones in research/sources, both from 2026-09-23: Homebrew/homebrew-cask ci.yml (with the same fetch-depth: 0 and persist-credentials: false) and tw93/mole release.yml. Please verify it with `gh api repos/actions/checkout/git/ref/tags/v7.0.1` before the first tag. A wrong SHA fails closed at checkout.

7 LOW: fixed. "What users see" marks Open Anyway as expected but not yet tested with a downloaded self-signed build. "Publishing the download" calls the pre-release behaviour an open decision (T-0080) and asks the maintainer not to push pre-release tags until then.
Build and test on 287ab03 (worktree, niced): swift build ok, swift test 310/310 passed.

comments.author: fix-signing-ci-2
comments.text:
Fix round 2, feat/signing-ci 43496c0. Dispositions for review-signing-ci-2 (09:56:44):
1 FIXED. RELEASING.md step 3 and 'Who can sign as macontrol' now say --remove-export removes only the plain .p12, .b64 and .p12 password: the keychain file plus MACONTROL_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD in signing.env stay a full copy of the key, readable by anything running as the maintainer and decryptable offline. They also say the key made on 2026-09-24 is extractable. make-signing-cert.sh imports with -x, and the header comment says -x blocks security export, not an offline read. Not probed on a real keychain, because a scratch keychain changes the user search list. A -x failure would surface in the script's own codesign self-check, which fails closed and cleans up on a first run.
2 FIXED. Order is now: write signing.env.new (grep status 1 or less), then in a subshell source it, require a non-empty keychain password, lock-keychain, unlock-keychain -p and find-identity -p codesigning with the name. Only then mv the env and delete the .p12 files. On failure, .new is removed and it dies with 'nothing removed'. It locks first because unlocking an already unlocked keychain may not check the password; that is unverified and deliberately not probed on the real keychain.
3 FIXED. release.yml uses ditto -c -k --norsrc --noextattr --keepParent. The RELEASING.md Unzipping caveat is gone. test-signing.sh takes the flags from the YAML, zips build/Macontrol.app, unzips it and runs codesign --verify --strict --deep.
4 MERGE NOTE for the integrator, not changed here because feat/site is not on main yet. When merging with feat/site 609cd96, replace RELEASING.md 'Publishing the download' paragraph 2 with: deploy-site.sh serves only releases from SITE_RELEASE's line (0.1 now), pre-releases only within it. For v0.2.0, bump SITE_RELEASE and the site copy in one commit before running it, or the site keeps serving 0.1.x.
5 FIXED. test-signing.sh now covers signing-identity.sh (name / no setup gives '-' / stale password gives '-'), the --remove-export no-setup guard, A (chmod 000 env) and B (stale password). A and B each assert that both .p12 files remain, no .new is left and signing.env is byte-identical. It also checks the import has -x.
Mutation proof, targeted, in scratch copies: 7 of 8 killed (rm before the verify, verify skipped, unlock dropped, -x dropped, signing-identity without unlock, no-setup guard removed, ditto flags removed). The survivor is 'grep status check removed': case A is also caught by the empty-password check, so that line is a redundant guard.
Checks: test-signing.sh ok; the real search list, ~/.config/macontrol listing and file hashes are identical before and after. swift build ok, swift test 310/310 (private TMPDIR). YAML parses.
OPEN, unchanged: the user decision on a separate dev certificate and a fresh release key before gh secret set. Checkout SHA still not verified online.

comments.author: fix-site-2
comments.text: From T-0080 fix round 2 (feat/site 1096c48), about docs/RELEASING.md 'Publishing the download' (your file, so not edited): deploy-site.sh no longer serves any tag with a suffix (v0.1.2-rc.1, v0.2.0-beta.1), whether it comes from gh or from --zip. It serves the newest unsuffixed v<SITE_RELEASE>.x tag and prints a note naming the newer candidate. It no longer writes version.json (that was removed in fix round 1: version, size and SHA-256 are now in the HTML). It reads the screenshots and CHANGELOG.md from the served tag, so the tag must be in the local clone. The 'open decision / do not push a pre-release tag' lines can say that candidates are never served, unless the user decides otherwise (the default is flagged on T-0080). I kept the GitHub pre-release flag out of the filter because v0.1.0 carries it as a preview.

tasks.verdictNotes:
CHANGES (round 2, review-signing-ci-2, feat/signing-ci 287ab03). No new critical or high. swift build ok. swift test 310/310 passed (niced, load about 60). scripts/test-signing.sh ok, and the real search list and ~/.config/macontrol were unchanged (diffed before and after). I checked the pin directly on build/Macontrol.app: the exact requirement gives rc 0, another identifier rc 3, one leaf digit off rc 3, a malformed requirement rc 1. The YAML parses (ruby).

Round-1 dispositions:
- #2, #4, #5, #6 and #7: fixed as described.
- #3: the comments are on T-0075 (09:36:45), T-0080 (09:36:46) and T-0071 (09:36:46).
- #1: partly fixed. The remainder is OPEN below.
- The checkout SHA is in 4 local clones: homebrew-cask, mole, kudu and thaw. It is still unverified online.

1. MEDIUM (cert handling, honest docs). RELEASING.md:51-53 says that until you run --remove-export, "anything that reads ~/.config/macontrol gets the private key". RELEASING.md:131-132 says step 3 "removes the extractable copies". Neither is true after --remove-export. ~/Library/Keychains/macontrol-signing.keychain-db (0600, readable by any process of the user) together with MACONTROL_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD, which stays in signing.env, is still a full copy of the key. The keychain-db can be decrypted offline with its password, and the key was imported without `-x`. After signing-identity.sh unlocked it, `security dump-keychain` on the real keychain shows the private key with attribute 0x10 (Extractable) = 1 and 0x11 (NeverExtractable) = 0. Fix: in both places, say that --remove-export only removes the plain .p12 and its password, and that the keychain file plus signing.env still hand over the key. Add `-x` to the `security import` in make-signing-cert.sh for future setups: the backup comes from the .p12, so nothing needs to export from the keychain later.

2. MEDIUM (fail-open on the release key). --remove-export deletes the .p12 and the .b64 first. Only then does it rewrite signing.env, with `grep -v ... > .new || true; mv`. Nothing checks beforehand that what is left still works.
Repros, using test-signing.sh's fake security and codesign in a scratch HOME:
(A) With signing.env set to chmod 000, grep prints "Permission denied" and `|| true` hides it. signing.env is replaced by a 0-byte file, the .p12 and .b64 are gone, and the script prints "removed ..." and exits 0. The next run dies with "MACONTROL_KEYCHAIN_PASSWORD: missing". On the real Mac the no-timeout keychain stays unlocked until logout. After that the key cannot be reached.
(B) With a keychain password in signing.env that no longer opens the keychain, --remove-export exits 0 and removes the .p12. The next run exits 1 at unlock.
In both cases the offline backup is the only copy left, and the script cannot know whether it exists.
Fix, before deleting anything:
- write the new env and require grep's status to be 1 or less;
- source it;
- run `security unlock-keychain -p` and `security find-identity -p codesigning "$KEYCHAIN"`, and require the name;
- only then run mv and rm.
Add A and B to test-signing.sh.

3. LOW (release zip). `ditto -c -k --keepParent` stores extended attributes as `._` entries: 12 of them in a zip of build/Macontrol.app. After `unzip`, verification fails with "a sealed resource is missing or invalid". With `ditto -c -k --norsrc --noextattr --keepParent` the zip has 0 `._` entries, and the unzipped copy passes `--verify --strict --deep` and the RELEASE_REQUIREMENT pin. This is a flag change in release.yml. After it, the RELEASING.md "Unzipping" caveat can go.

4. LOW (merge drift, for the integrator). RELEASING.md:99-108 says deploy-site.sh serves the newest release, pre-releases included. feat/site 609cd96 (09:46, after this fix round) pins SITE_RELEASE="0.1". So once v0.2.0 is released, deploy-site.sh keeps serving 0.1.1, with only a note on stderr, until SITE_RELEASE and the copy are bumped together. Pre-releases count only within that line. Rewrite the section on merge.

5. LOW (tests). signing-identity.sh has no automated check. Once T-0075 wires it, it decides on every build between signing with the certificate without a prompt and ad hoc. The --remove-export "no setup" guard is also untested, and so are cases A and B. Each is about 10 lines with the existing fakes.

OPEN (user decision; the rest of round-1 #1, not a defect in this diff). Any process running as the maintainer can sign as macontrol without a prompt. The decision is cheap now and costly later. No user has granted FDA to leaf 2b40c1b6... yet, and since 08:47 this key has sat next to its password in ~/.config on a Mac where many agents run. A separate dev certificate, and a fresh release key if wanted, cost nothing before `gh secret set` and the first certificate-signed release. After that, a new release key means every user grants FDA again. Orchestrator: ask the user before the secrets are set.

Checked OK:
- The pin: exact, identifier, leaf and malformed cases.
- The missing-secret, version and pin guards fail closed.
- No injection: the ref name reaches the shell only through a quoted env var, and awk uses index().
- The secrets are scoped to the import step. `persist-credentials: false` is set, and the token is used only in the publish step.
- timeout 15, `shell: bash`, no caches.
- Package.swift has no package dependencies, so no third-party build code runs while the key is unlocked.
- test-signing.sh uses fakes and leaves the real state unchanged.
- tmutil shows no Time Machine destination and no local snapshots, so no backup copy of the .p12 exists outside ~/.config.
